OP001 / #2655
MAIN RESULTS OF THE INTERNATIONAL, MULTICENTER, TRIPLE THERAPY PREVENTION OF RECURRENT INTRACEREBRAL DISEASE EVENTS TRIAL (TRIDENT)
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 01.C. Anderson1, A. Rodgers2, A. De Silva3, R. Freed1, N. Espinosa1, S. Martins4, C. Klijn5, O. Marques Pontes Neto6, K. Wahab7, F. Schreuder5, R. Al-Shahi Salman8, C. Chow9, J. Chalmers1
1The George Institute for Global Health, Brain Health, Camperdown, Australia, 2The George Institute for Global Health, Cardiovascular, Camperdown, Australia, 3University of Kelaniya, Colombo, Sri Lanka, 4Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul, Porto Alegre, Brazil, 5Donders Institute for Brain, Cognition and Behaviour, Radboud University Medical Centre, Neurology, Nijmegen, Netherlands, 6Hospital das Clínicas da Faculdade de Medicina de Ribeirão Preto, Neurology, Ribeirão Preto, Brazil, 7University of Ilorin Teaching Hospital, Medicine, Ilorin, Nigeria, 8University of Edinburgh, Edinburgh, United Kingdom, 9University of Sydney, Westmead Applied Research Centre, Sydney, Australia
Background and Aims: Blood pressure (BP) lowering therapy prevents recurrent stroke and other serious cardiovascular events, but many patients fail to achieve effective BP control due to use of ineffective regimens, poor adherence, clinician inertia, and concerns over side-effects. TRIDENT aimed to determine effectiveness of more-intensive BP control with a single ‘triple pill’ (fixed low-dose combination of telmisartan 20mg, amlodipine 2.5mg and indapamide 1.25mg) for secondary prevention after an acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).
Methods: An international, double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized trial in adults with ICH and mild-moderate hypertension (systolic BP 130-160mmHg) on any background antihypertensive therapy provided triple pill/placebo could be added on top. The double-blind treatment period was preceded by a 2-week, single-blind, active run-in phase in which participants received the triple pill. The study planned to enrol ~1500 patients with a mean 3-years follow-up to provide 90% power to detect a hazard ratio 0.5 on the primary endpoint of total stroke. Secondary outcomes included recurrent ICH, cardiovascular events, BP control, disability, cognitive impairment/dementia, and safety.
Results: Overall, 1671 patients were randomized between September 28, 2017 and November 30, 2024, at 57 active sites in 10 countries. Baseline characteristics including prior medical history and BP lowering medication were well balanced between groups. The study was completed in 2025 and the main results are to be presented at the WSC.
Conclusions: Fixed triple low-dose combination BP lowering could improve long-term outcome after acute ICH.

ANALYSIS OF MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY FOR LARGE CORE ISCHEMIC STROKE (ATLAS) COLLABORATION – AN INDIVIDUAL PATIENT-LEVEL DATA (IPD) META-ANALYSIS OF SIX RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 01.A. Sarraj1, G. Thomalla2, S. Yoshimura3, X. Huo4, A. Yoo5, C. Arquizan6, B. Lapergue7, L. Churilov8, H. Johns8, D. Pujara1, B. Campbell9, T. Jovin10, T. Morimoto11, M. Bendszus12, O. Zaidat13, V. Costalat14, Z. Miao15
1University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, Cleveland, United States of America, 2Universitatsklinikum Hamburg-Eppendorf, Hamburg, Germany, 3Hyogo Medical University, Department Of Neurosurgery, Nishinomiya, Japan, 4Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Department Of Cerebral Vascular Disease, Neurological Disease Center, Beijing, China, 5Texas Stroke Institute, Dallas, United States of America, 6Hôpital Gui de Chauliac, Montpellier, France, 7CHU Dijon-Bourgogne, Dijon, France, 8University of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, 9University of Melbourne, Melbourne, Australia, 10Cooper University, Camden, United States of America, 11Hyogo Medical University, Department Of Data Science, Nishinomiya, Japan, 12Heidelberg University Hospital, Neuroradiology/neurology, Heidelberg, Germany, 13Bon Secours Mercy Health St Vincent Medical Center, Neurosciences Institute, Toledo, United States of America, 14Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Montpellier, Montpellier, France, 15Dept. of Neurology and Stroke Center Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University China National Clinical Research Center for Neurological Diseases, Neurology, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) efficacy and safety in patients with large ischemic stroke was recently demonstrated in multiple randomized trials. A pooled patient-level meta-analysis may help strengthen the overall evidence and provide insights into clinical and imaging subgroups.
Methods: We will perform an individual patient-level meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to explore the evidence for efficacy and safety of EVT in patients with large ischemic core up to 24 hours of last known well in key clinical and imaging subgroups. A research plan and statistical analysis protocol was developed a-priori and registered to PROSPERO, which will guide the meta-analysis. A systematic search of PubMed and EMBASE was executed to identify eligible clinical trials that randomized patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (ICA/MCA) and a large ischemic core on non-contrast CT/MRI (ASPECTS 5 or less) and/or CT/MR perfusion/diffusion imaging (ischemic core⩾50 ml) to receive EVT vs medical care only and were published after 3/2018. Identified clinical trials were invited to contribute patient data. The primary efficacy outcome is the distribution of modified Rankin Scale score at 90-day follow-up. Secondary outcomes include functional independence (mRS 0-2), independent ambulation (mRS 0-3), symptomatic ICH (SITS-MOST definition) and mortality. Additionally, analysis of primary and secondary outcomes will be repeated in pre-specified subgroups based on clinical and imaging characteristics.
Results: Six clinical trials (RESCUE Japan LIMIT, ANGEL ASPECT, SELECT2, TENSION, LASTE and TESLA) met eligibility criteria and were included in this meta-analysis. The results will be available for presentation at the World Stroke Conference 2025.
Conclusions: Provided at conference
OP003 / #3095
POOLED INDIVIDUAL PATIENT DATA META-ANALYSIS OF TRIALS OF TENECTEPLASE COMPARED TO ALTEPLASE IN ACUTE ISCHAEMIC STROKE (CATALYST-TNK)
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 01.K. Muir1, B. Menon2, M. Parsons3, B. Campbell4, Y. Wang5, Y. Xiong6, N. Greenlaw7, A. Mcconnachie7
1University of Glasgow, School Of Cardiovascular & Metabolic Health, Glasgow, United Kingdom, 2University of Calgary, Dept Of Neuroclinical Sciences, calgary, Canada, 3University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia, 4University of Melbourne, Melbourne, Australia, 5Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Beijing, China, 6China National Clinical Research Center for Neurologic Diseases, Beijing, China, 7University of Glasgow, Robertson Centre For Biostatistics, Glasgow, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Individual trials have shown non-inferiority of tenecteplase and aggregate data meta-analyses suggest possible superiority of tenecteplase. CATALYST-TNK is an individual patient data meta-analysis of trials comparing these agents within 4.5h of last being known well.
Methods: Individual data will be pooled from available clinical trials that compared tenecteplase 0.25mg/kg with alteplase. The primary outcome is excellent neurological recovery (mRS 0 – 1) at day 90. A hierarchical analysis will investigate first non-inferiority, then superiority of tenecteplase. Groups will be compared using modified Poisson regression to estimate the log of the relative risk (RR) of the primary outcome, adjusted for age, sex, baseline NIHSS score, and onset to treatment time. If the lower limit of the 95% CI for the RR is greater than the non-inferiority limit (-3% absolute risk difference applied to a relative risk scale), then tenecteplase will be considered non-inferior to alteplase. If the lower limit of the 95% CI for the RR >1, then tenecteplase will be considered superior to alteplase. Secondary outcomes will be mRS distribution at 90 days; early major NIHSS improvement; death; sICH; and fatal ICH within 7 days.
Results: Data from 9 phase 2 and 3 trials comparing Tenecteplase 0.25mg/kg with alteplase 0.9mg/kg are expected to be included, in total involving 5,884 patients. Analysis will include data available from all pooled studies by the time of presentation.
Conclusions: Individual patient data pooled analysis will refine non-inferiority estimates and explore potential superiority of tenecteplase 0.25mg/kg compared with alteplase <4.5h from last being known well.

THE RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLIND, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED, PHASE 3 FOCUS STUDY OF GANGLIOSIDE GM1 FOR ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE (AIS)
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 01.X. Zhang1, Y. Xu1, A. Guo2, P. Chen2, D. Yu3, J. Zhu4, Y. Ma5, J. Guo6, J. Zhao7, H. Chen8, S. Hou9, Y. Li9, Z. Wang10, C. Guo11, P. Zhou12, C. Wei13, D. Wang14, L. Yang15, C. Gui16, Q. Dong17, Y. Yang18, H. Li18, F. Ma18
1Drum Tower Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing University School of Medicine, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China, 2Xianyang Hospital of Yan'an University, xianyang, China, 3Xianning Central Hospital, Xianning, China, 4Halison International Peace Hospital of Hengshui City, Hengshui, China, 5Beipiao Central Hospital, Beipiao, China, 6XuZhou Central Hospital, Xuzhou, China, 7Central Hospital of Minhang District, Shanghai, China, 8The General Hospital of Northern Theater Command of the Chinese People's Liberation Army, Shenyang, China, 9Shanghai Pudong Hospital, Fudan University Pudong Medical Center, Shanghai, China, 10Taizhou First People's Hospital, Taizhou, China, 11Liaocheng People's Hospital, Liaocheng, China, 12Xiangyang No. 1 People's Hospital, Xiangyang, Xiangyang, China, 13Nanshi Hospital Affiliated to Henan University, Nanyang, China, 14Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical College, Xuzhou, China, 15Chongqing Emergency Medical Center, Chongqing University Central Hospital, Chongqing, China, 16Dazhou Central Hospital, Dazhou, China, 17Huashan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China, 18Qilu Pharmaceutical, Jinan, China
Background and Aims: The clinical application indicates GM1 may enhance the outcomes for AIS patients. This study aims to evaluate efficacy and safety of GM1 for AIS.
Methods: AIS patients with time of symptom onset⩽24 h and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) of 5–20 (7–20 after protocol amendment) were randomized to GM1 (100 mg, qd) or placebo (qd) for 12–14d, stratified by age (⩽/>50 years) and thrombolysis (yes/no). The primary outcome was proportion of patients with modified Rankin Scale (mRS)⩽2 at D90. Efficacy and safety were evaluated in patients with NIHSS of 7–20 and 5–20, respectively.
Results: In this interim analysis, from November 2020 to May 2023, totally 1019 patients were included for efficacy analysis (GM1: 516; Placebo: 503). 349 (67.6%) patients in the GM1 group and 289 (57.5%) patients in the placebo group had mRS⩽2 at D90, with rate difference (RD) of 10.16% (98.78% CI 2.70%–17.61%; P=0.0007).

This study has been early terminated due to the positive results. In subgroups of randomization strata, age⩽75 years, time of symptom onset, and significant rate differences in the primary outcome were obtained. Proportions of patients with mRS⩽1 at D90 were significantly higher for GM1 (RD 6.63% [95% CI 0.58%–12.69%]; P=0.0313). No significant difference in proportions of patients with mRS ⩽1 at D14/30, NIHSS changes, patient-reported outcomes, etc., between the two groups were observed (all P>0.05). Adverse event incidences were similar in the two groups.
Conclusions: GM1 significantly improved functional outcome at D90 for AIS compared with placebo.
OP005 / #3069
EVALUATION OF A MULTI-COMPONENT INTERVENTION TO IMPROVE THE OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS UNDERGOING ENDOVASCULAR TREATMENT IN CHINA (OPTIMAL): A CLUSTER-RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 01.Y. He, J. Yang, M. Lou
Department of Neurology, the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University, School of Medicine., Hangzhou, China
Background and Aims: In-hospital delay, which has profound impact on the efficacy of endovascular treatment (EVT), is a challenging problem in China. However, few randomized trials focusing on reducing in-hospital delay prior to EVT to improve patient outcomes have been carried out. We aimed to evaluate the effect of a multicomponent intervention on the clinical outcomes and in-hospital delay of patients undergoing EVT.

Methods:This cluster-randomized trial (NCT05874596), conducted between July 1, 2022 and June 30, 2023, 1:1 randomized 16 hospitals to PEITER (Persuasion Enablement Incentivization Training Education Restriction, Figure 1) intervention or routine care plus stroke registry. All the patients undergoing EVT within 24 hours of stroke onset were included. The PEITER group received a 1-year PEITEM 6-component intervention based on the behavioral theory via video teleconferences and in-site meetings. The primary outcome was the proportion 3-month modified Rankin scale (mRS) ⩽ 3.

Results:A total of 1288 patients were included, with 666 in the PEITER group and 622 in the control group. The proportion of 3-month mRS ⩽ 3 was higher in the PERTER group (66.4% vs. 57.2%, adjusted odds ratio: 1.646 [1.054-2.57]; ICC = 0.02; P = 0.028; Figure 2). Among secondary outcomes, the median of door-to-puncture time (DPT) was 103 mins in the PERTER group and 111 mins in the control group (adjusted mean difference: -22.4 [-42.0-2.8]; ICC = 0.03; P = 0.025). The proportion DPT in the two groups is presented in Figure 3.
Conclusions: The PERTER intervention resulted in a shorter in-hospital delay and better outcomes in patients undergoing EVT.

Background and Aims: Tenecteplase, a genetically modified tissue plasminogen activator with greater fibrin specificity and a longer half-life than alteplase, is increasingly used for thrombolysis prior to endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in ischemic stroke. This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of tenecteplase versus alteplase at 0.6 mg/kg, an official dosage in Japan, in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO).
Methods: We conducted a multicenter, open-label, randomized phase II trial in patients with LVO in the internal carotid, middle cerebral, or basilar arteries who were eligible for EVT within 4.5 hours of symptom onset in Japan. Patients were randomized to receive either tenecteplase (0.25 mg/kg) or alteplase (0.6 mg/kg). The primary outcome was substantial angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b to 3) or no retrievable thrombus on the initial angiogram. Secondary outcomes included modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 90 days and safety outcomes, such as symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH) and mortality.
Results: Among 221 patients enrolled, 108 (median age of 79 years, female 42%) received tenecteplase and 113 (median age of 78 years, female 43%) received alteplase.
Conclusions: The results will be presented in the late-breaking session at WSC 2025.

IMPACT OF CATHETER ABLATION ON SECONDARY STROKE PREVENTION IN PATIENTS WITH NONVALVULAR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION RECEIVING EDOXABAN: THE STABLED STUDY
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 02.Y. Nishiyama1, K. Kimura2, W. Shimizu3, T. Otsuka4, Y. Sakamoto5, Y.-K. Iwasaki3
1University of Fukui Hospital, Department Of Neurology, Fukui, Japan, 2Nippon Medical School, Department Of Neurology, Tokyo, Japan, 3Nippon Medical School, Department Of Cardiovascular Medicine, Tokyo, Japan, 4Nippon Medical School, Department Of Hygiene And Public Health, Tokyo, Japan, 5Nippon Medical School, Department Of Neurology, Graduate School Of Medicine, Tokyo, Japan
Background and Aims: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of catheter ablation (CA) combined with standard edoxaban therapy (ST) in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) who had a history of ischemic stroke (IS).
Methods: This was a multicenter, randomized, open-label, parallel-group study comparing ST+CA with ST alone in NVAF patients with a recent history of IS. The study was conducted in Japan from January 2018 to March 2024 (jRCTs031180249). CA was performed based on pulmonary vein isolation with atrial ablation after ⩾4 weeks of edoxaban administration and within 1–6 months of index stroke onset. The primary endpoint was a composite of recurrent IS, systemic embolism, all-cause death, and hospitalization for heart failure.
Results: A total of 249 patients were randomized (ST group: 124; ST+CA group: 125). Baseline characteristics were well balanced between the two groups. Overall, 75.1% of patients were male, with a mean age of 71.7 years. The median follow-up was 3.7 years in the ST group and 3.6 years in the ST+CA group. The primary endpoint occurred at a rate of 4.9% per patient-year in the ST group and 5.6% per patient-year in the ST+CA group (log-rank p = 0.70). The events for each component were shown in the Table. CA-related adverse events occurred in 1.6% of patients in the ST+CA group.

Conclusions: The primary endpoint did not differ between the groups. These findings indicate that CA did not reduce the risk of recurrent stroke in patients with NVAF and a prior history of stroke.

EVALUATION OF SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF INTRACRANIAL SELF-EXPANDING DRUG-ELUTING STENTS FOR SYMPTOMATIC INTRACRANIAL ATHEROSCLEROTIC STENOSIS: A PROSPECTIVE, MULTICENTER, RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED, SUPERIORITY CLINICAL TRIAL PROTOCOL
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 02.Y. He, Y. He, J. Zhao, Z. Zhu, W. Liu, L. Zhu, Z. Wang, T. Li
Zhengzhou University People's Hospital, Department Of Cerebrovascular Disease, Zhengzhou, China
Background and Aims: In-stent restenosis (ISR) is a crucial factor that affects the long-term efficacy of intracranial bare metal stent (BMS) implantation for intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS). Patients with intracranial ISR are at a high risk of recurrent ischemic events. The NOVA intracranial drug-eluting stent trial demonstrates that a drug-eluting stent (DES) can reduce ISR and stroke recurrence after intracranial bare stent implantation. However, the application of balloon-expanded DES necessitates specific vascular conditions. The objective of this study is to assess the safety and efficacy of self-expanding DES for treating symptomatic ICAS.
Methods: This is a prospective, multicentre, randomised, controlled, superiority clinical trial that is conducted in 16 clinical trial centres in China. This study aims to recruit 208 patients with symptomatic intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis. Eligible subjects are randomly assigned to two groups at a ratio of 1:1. The experimental group is treated with self-expanding DES. The control group is treated with self-expanding BMS. All subjects are followed up within 7 days after surgery or before discharge, 30 days after surgery, and 6, 12, and 24 months after surgery. The primary outcome of the trial is the incidence of in-stent restenosis at 6 months after surgery to verify the safety and efficacy of intracranial drug-eluting stents.

Results: The trial completed enrollment, and data collection/verification is ongoing. The final results will be made available on completion of enrollment and follow-up.
Conclusions: This study aims to introduce a new treatment option by conducting a randomized controlled trial comparing intracranial self-expanding DESs with self-expanding BMSs for ICAS.

24Health Science Center, Ningbo University, Ningbo, China, 25Center for Public Health and Epidemic Preparedness & Response, Peking University, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been used for intracranial aneurysm detection, however, Level-I evidence is lack and no randomized controlled trial (RCT) has been performed. This first double-blinded, sham-AI controlled RCT (IDEAL study) aims to rigorously evaluating whether AI augmentation improves real-world diagnostic performances and influences patients' downstream management and outcomes.
Methods: This investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, double-blinded, sham-AI RCT was conducted at 21 tertiary hospitals across China (ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06118840). Eligible patients scheduled for head CT angiography (CTA) were randomized 1:1 to the True-AI arm (radiologists assisted by real AI) or Sham-AI arm (sham-AI assistance). Sham-AI was a novel, placebo-like control, mimicking the interface and specificity of real AI but with near-zero sensitivity, designed to blind radiologists to group allocation and mitigate cognitive bias. Coprimary outcomes include patient-level sensitivity (superiority) and specificity (noninferiority, margin 5%) for aneurysm detection. Secondary outcomes encompass workload, treatment-related events, and quality-of-life measures during follow-up. The target sample size was 6450 for 80% power.

Results: A total of 6470 participants were enrolled between May 20, 2024, and April 8, 2025 (True-AI: 3234; Sham-AI: 3236). Enrollment is complete, and the cohort is undergoing reference standard establishment and 3-month follow-up assessments. Primary results and secondary outcomes are expected in October 2025.
Conclusions: IDEAL study will provide the first Level-I evidence on the real-world impact of AI in intracranial aneurysm detection, potentially setting a paradigm for evaluating AI in radiology. Findings may inform clinical guidelines by quantifying AI's clinical utility while demonstrating whether AI-assisted diagnosis improves patient outcomes and healthcare efficiency.

ARPEGGIO PHASE 2 RANDOMIZED DOSE SELECTION TRIAL OF NOVEL CEREBROPROTECTANT SCP776 IN EVT TREATED AIS PATIENTS
PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 02.K. Kuchenbecker1, T. O'Reilly1, A. Stukel1, K. Dabbagh1, M. Corrigan1, W. Clark2, S. Guedry2, D. Gulati3, L. Herren3, P. Wechsler4, C. Reinhart4, F. Kaddouh5, V. Background and Aims: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients undergoing EVT are at risk of ischemia–reperfusion injury. Scp776 is a first-in-class novel Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 engineered to target and rescue apoptotic cells and protect against injury progression in large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke. We evaluated the safety and explored cerebroprotective efficacy of scp776 in AIS.
Methods: ARPEGGIO is a phase 2, placebo-controlled, dose-selection, randomized clinical trial (20 sites, US) that enrolled AIS patients with ICA/M1/M2 occlusion, NIHSS ⩾ 6, intended for EVT within 24 h of LKW, that evaluated, low-, mid-, or high-dose scp776 + standard of care. The primary safety endpoint was number of treatment-emergent serious adverse events (SAEs) prior to discharge. Top-line efficacy endpoints were NIHSS at discharge (adjusted for baseline) and final infarct volume (adjusted for baseline ASPECTS). Analyses were performed in the modified intent-to-treat (MITT) population.
Results: From 03/2023 to 06/2025, we completed enrollment of 119 participants in the MITT. The average age was 70.0±13.5 years and 49% were females. Median baseline NIHSS was 15[10-19] and ASPECTs was 8[7-9]. The Average last known well to study drug administration was 14.5[8.9-18.1]hrs. Conclusions: This two-part Phase 2 study establishes safety and explores early efficacy signals for scp776 as a cerebroprotective adjunctive to EVT. Pending results will guide dose selection, future pivotal drug development, and the potential to improve outcomes in large vessel occlusion stroke.

PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 03.X. Liu, L. Liu

Background and Aims: Acute ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular therapy (EVT) still face significant risks of poor functional outcomes. PLENARY, AWARDS & LATE BREAKING 03.I. Mcgurgan, A. Webb, N. Lovett, L. Li, K. Lau, N. Paul, F. Cuthbertson, M. Wilson, J. Edens, E.-R. Vaughan-Fowler, L. Binney, L. Silver, U. Fischer, L. Tarassenko, P. Rothwell
University of Oxford, Wolfson Center For Prevention Of Stroke And Dementia, Oxford, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Early BP-lowering is not recommended in major ischaemic stroke, but there is uncertainty in acute TIA/minor stroke, particularly about the safety of early/intensive treatment in non-hospitalised patients. In a prospective population-based three-phase sequential comparison, we determined the feasibility, safety and effectiveness of early/intensive BP-lowering for non-hospitalised TIA/minor stroke.
Methods: All patients with a first acute TIA/minor stroke in the population (Oxford Vascular Study) were included in analyses. In Phase-1(04/2002-09/2004), no antihypertensives were given acutely. In Phase-3(04/2008-03/2019), all patients with measured/suspected hypertension were also offered immediate remote-telemetric home-BP-monitoring (RT-HBPM) with daily physician-guided treatment (target<130/80mmHg). Conclusions: Early intensive BP-lowering after TIA/minor stroke is safe in non-hospitalised patients and substantially reduces major recurrent stroke at the population level. Lancet submission imminent

Background and Aims: The National institute for Health and Care Excellence recommends that stroke survivors should exercise at nationally recommended levels to prevent secondary strokes. There are widespread exercise referral schemes (NERS) that support people with such conditions. There is limited evidence regarding uptake and adherence rates in the stroke population. The aim of this study was to explore the barriers and enablers of stroke survivors who have completed the NERS programme using the COM-B framework.
Methods: Ten stroke survivors (n=10) and two communication partners (n=2) took part in a series of semi-structured interviews or focus groups. The semi-structured interview schedule was designed using the COM-B framework. The interviews were transcribed verbatim and then analysed using a theoretical thematic analysis approach.
Results: The over-arching theme from this study identified NERS as a learning environment for recovery and discovery. Seven sub-themes were identified as enabling participation in NERS: a learning space to redefine and rebuild; safe and supportive spaces and people; peer learning for all; a sense of community; positive behaviour change; overcoming stroke symptoms and exercise enhancing mental wellbeing. Three sub-themes were identified as barriers to participation in NERS: non-accessible environments and people; the challenge of adjusting to the “new me” and stroke symptoms as distinct barriers to NERS.
Conclusions: This is the first study to explore the enablers and barriers to stroke survivors accessing NERS using the COM-B framework. The insights offered here highlight the value that exercise schemes can offer as a wider learning environment to support long term adjustment and recovery after stroke.

Traditional stroke therapies rely on training and “open-loop” stimulation delivered without regard to patient intent. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) detect movement intentions from EEG and promote activity-dependent plasticity, showing promise in rehabilitation. BCIs enable timely coupling between efferent brain signals and afferent somatosensory feedback—a “closed-loop” delivery—and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) report added value for motor recovery. Conclusions: BCI-triggered functional movements delivered in a closed-loop, activity-dependent manner produced clinically meaningful and statistically significant motor gains, especially in the most severely impaired patients—underscoring the potential of intensive, functionally relevant BCI therapy to enhance post-stroke arm and hand recovery.

LOCATION-SPECIFIC GENE EXPRESSION IN CEREBRAL VASCULAR SMOOTH MUSCLE CELLS (VSMCS) UNVEILS DIVERGENT ANEURYSM PATHWAYS

Background and Aims: The human cerebral arterial circulation comprises anterior and posterior systems connected by the circle of Willis. Approximately 70–80% of cerebral aneurysms causing subarachnoid hemorrhage originate in the anterior circulation. Cerebral aneurysm (CA) prevalence varies by location due to hemodynamic forces, genetic factors, and embryologic differences. This study compared gene expression profiles of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) from anterior (middle cerebral artery, MCA) and posterior (vertebrobasilar artery, VBA) circulations to identify location-specific mechanisms in aneurysm development.
Methods: VSMC layers from autopsy-derived MCA and VBA samples underwent mRNA sequencing. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were analyzed and validated via qRT-PCR.
Results: Sixty-one DEGs were identified. Conclusions: This study provides the first genetic evidence of intrinsic molecular differences between VSMCs of the anterior (MCA) and posterior (VBA) cerebral circulations, revealing location-specific pathways in aneurysm pathogenesis. This first genetic comparison of VSMCs between cerebral circulations reveals location-specific mechanisms in aneurysm formation, offering insights for diagnostic markers and therapeutic targets (This work was supported by National Forensic Service (NFS2025_MED08), Ministry of the Interior and Safety, Republic of Korea, and National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) grant funded by the Korea Government (MEST) (RS-2024-00342397).

1Gaziosmanpaşa University, Faculty Of Health Sciences, Tokat, Turkey, 2Balıkesir University, balıkesir, Turkey, 3Kirikkale University, Kirikkale, Turkey
Background and Aims: Abstract Background:
Spasticity is a common motor impairment after stroke, particularly affecting the wrist and finger flexor muscles, leading to functional limitations in the upper extremity. Local vibration (LV) has been proposed as a non-invasive method to modulate muscle tone via proprioceptive stimulation. Objective:
This study aimed to investigate the effects of local vibration applied to wrist flexor muscles on spasticity in post-stroke individuals.
Methods: Thirty hemiplegic stroke patients (aged 18–75 years) were randomly assigned to two groups: (1) the Vibration Group (n=15) received conventional physiotherapy in addition to LV (80 Hz frequency, 1 mm amplitude, 15 minutes per session); and (2) the Control Group (n=15) received only conventional physiotherapy. IMPACT OF HUMAN ALBUMIN IN ACUTE LARGE CORE ISCHEMIC STROKE

Background and Aims: The efficacy of albumin as a neuroprotective agent in acute ischemic stroke with large infarct core remains unclear. We investigated whether adjuvant albumin therapy improves outcomes in patients with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO) undergoing thrombectomy.

Background and Aims: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) can cause sudden, profound monocular vision loss, often leading to permanent disability. Despite parallels with ischemic stroke, evidence-based treatment is lacking. TenCRAOS is the first completed multicentre randomized trial investigating whether systemic tenecteplase improves visual recovery in CRAO when given within 4.5 hours of symptom onset.
Methods: We conducted an investigator-initiated, multicenter, double-blind, double-dummy, randomized, controlled trial at 16 hospitals across six European countries. Adults with acute, non-arteritic CRAO confirmed by an ophthalmologist were enrolled within 4.5 hours of symptom onset and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive intravenous (IV) tenecteplase (0.25 mg/kg) and oral placebo, or IV placebo and oral aspirin. The primary outcome was visual recovery at 30 days, defined as a best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of ⩽0.7 logarithm of the Minimum Angle of Resolution (logMAR) in the affected eye. Safety endpoints included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality.
Results: A total of 78 patients were randomized; 40 received tenecteplase and 38 received aspirin. Secondary visual outcomes were consistent with the primary result. Adverse events occurred more frequently in the tenecteplase group, including one fatal intracranial hemorrhage.

Background and Aims: SPRINT INDIA trial, a randomized, blinded study across 31 centers, enrolled patients from both government and private healthcare sectors. SEVERITY OF INTRACRANIAL ARTERIAL CALCIFICATION ON CT AND FUTURE DEMENTIA: POPULATION-BASED STUDY AND SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
FREE COMMUNICATION 11: CI, SILENT BRAIN INFARCTS, COGNITION, DEMENTIA, NEUROIMAGING.K. Li, D. Simonato, O. Osomo, P. Rothwell, F.T. Oxford Vascular Study

Background and Aims: Coronary arterial calcification is a widely studied risk factor for acute coronary events, but although intracranial arterial calcification on CT-brain imaging (CT-IAC) is a frequent finding in older individuals, few longitudinal studies have assessed whether its presence, severity, or site predict cognitive impairment and dementia. Given the clinical and mechanistic importance of any associations, we did such a study and a systematic review.
Methods: In a nested case-control study of patients with minor stroke/TIA from the population-based Oxford Vascular Study (OXVASC), site and severity of CT-IAC (qualitatively and artery-specific volume) in cases who developed dementia on follow-up was compared with that in age/sex-matched controls who did not (logistic regression adjusted for other risk factors). Previous longitudinal studies, identified by systematic review, were pooled with OXVASC data using meta-analysis.
Results: In OXVASC (cases=200,controls=200; mean/SD age=78.0/9.3), internal carotid artery CT-IAC volume (top vs. bottom 50%) was independently associated with dementia risk (adjusted OR [aOR]=1.74, 95%CI=1.13-2.68, p=0.013), particularly if bilateral (aOR=2.02, 1.26-3.24, p=0.003), and remained so on pooling with the one published longitudinal study in patients with stroke/TIA (pooled aOR=1.71, 1.21-2.44, p=0.003), and with a similar study in the general population (pooled aOR=1.88, 1.33-2.67, p<0.001), with little overall heterogeneity (I2=0). OPTIMAL MANAGEMENT FOR PATIENTS WITH HIGH ADMISSION BLOOD PRESSURE AFTER INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE
FREE COMMUNICATION 12: VENOUS THROMBOSIS / STROKE IN THE YOUNG / ICH.M. Ouyang1, C. Anderson1, L. Song2, X. Wang1
1The George Institute for Global Health, Sydney, Australia, 2Institute of Science and Technology for Brain-inspired Intelligence, Shanghai, China
Background and Aims: Previous trials have focused on intracerebral haemorrahge (ICH) patients with systolic blood pressure (SBP) between 150–220 mmHg, recommending a target of < 140 mmHg. Limited data exists for BP management for patients admitted with extremely high BP.
Methods: Pooled Individual Data analysis of the Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction in Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage Trials (INTERACT1-3). Patients with ICH onset within 6 hours were randomized to intensive BP lowering vs. usual care. Patients were categorized by admission SBP⩾200mmHg vs. SBP<200mmHg. Restricted cubic splines were used to visualize the optimal BP targets at 30 minutes and 1 hr after randomized treatment. Conclusions: Patients with extremely high SBP could benefit from the BP treatment. The optimal targets of SBP lowering was 170mmHg at 30 minutes and 160mmHg at 1 hr.

Background and Aims: Optimal anticoagulation in acute cerebral vein thrombosis (CVT) remains uncertain. We compared unfractionated heparin (UFH) and enoxaparin, and identified predictors of functional recovery and UFH responsiveness.
Methods: This sub-study from the international CLOT-VENUS registry (2004–2024), included adults with acute CVT treated with UFH or enoxaparin. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were collected. UFH response was measured via a composite responsiveness index (UFH-CRI) based on partial thromboplastin time (PTT). The primary outcome was 6-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Secondary outcomes included discharge mRS and mortality. Multivariate regression and IPTW matching were used for analyses.

Female sex, elevated BMI, and higher NLR were independent predictors of poor UFH responsiveness.

Conclusions: UFH was associated with poorer recovery compared with enoxaparin, likely attributable to suboptimal and inconsistent anticoagulation. However, when UFH achieves consistent therapeutic levels, outcomes are comparable. Early predictors may help guide individualized anticoagulation strategies.

WMH volume progression was associated with similar clinical phenotypes to overall WMH change, while WMH volume regression was most strongly associated with changes in sleep patterns.
Conclusions: WMH volume change over three years was associated with deleterious health outcomes across several body systems. WMH volume progression and regression related to different clinical phenotypes, suggesting differing underlying mechanisms. Future work should further clarify risk factors for WMH volume progression and elucidate the potential benefits of WMH volume regression.

Background and Aims: We evaluated the correlation between cerebrovascular reserve (CVR) on acetazolamide (ACZ) -stress single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) brain scans and collaterals on arterial spin-labeling (ASL) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis.

FREE COMMUNICATION 13: LARGE & SMALL ARTERY DISEASE.S. Fukuda1, Y. Shimogonya2, A. Watanabe1, Y. Yoshimoto1, S. Maruyama1, N. Yonemoto3, K. Fujiwara1, M. Fukuda1, A. Yasoda4
1National Hospital Organization Kyoto Medical Center, Neurosurgery, Kyoto, Japan, 2Nihon University, Koriyama, Japan, 3University of Toyama Faculty of Medicine, Toyama, Japan, 4National Hospital Organization Kyoto Medical Center, Kyoto, Japan
Background and Aims: It is difficult to sufficiently predict the progression of atherosclerotic stenosis based on known risk factors alone. Although hemodynamics plays an important role in atherosclerosis, the hemodynamic environments that promote stenosis progression remain unclear. Carotid stenosis is a major cause of atherosclerotic stroke. Thus, we conducted a prospective observational study to identify hemodynamic predictors of carotid stenosis progression.
Methods: Computational fluid dynamics analysis was performed using individual arterial geometry and flow velocity. Hemodynamic metrics were compared by multivariate analysis between the presence or absence of stenosis progression over the 2-year observation period, using known risk factors as confounding factors.
Results: A total of 545 patients were enrolled, and of the 361 stenotic arteries, 38 had progressive stenosis. Among the carotid arteries with 30%–55% area stenosis, those with stenosis progression had significantly lower time-averaged wall shear stress (WSS) and higher oscillatory shear index (OSI) distal to the stenosis site. Among those with 56%–70% stenosis, stenosis progression is significantly associated with higher time-averaged WSS at the stenotic site and higher transverse WSS at the stenotic and distal site. Arteries with 71%–99% stenosis and stenosis progression had significantly higher OSI at the distal site.
Conclusions: These data reveal the hemodynamic environments involved in atherosclerotic stenosis progression and suggest for the first time that the hemodynamic predictors of stenosis progression varies with the degree of stenosis. Background and Aims: Aerobic exercise improves walking and fitness after stroke, yet is rarely included in rehabilitation programs. Methods: Held in Melbourne, Australia in October 2024, the Dialogue involved individuals with stroke, stroke charities, clinicians (physiotherapists, occupational therapists, exercise physiologists, psychologists), and researchers. Background and Aims: Returning to work (RTW) after cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a complex process that impacts both individual wellbeing and societal productivity. While most reviews on RTW predictors focus on a single diagnosis, recurring medical, psychosocial, and work-related factors suggest the presence of common predictors across CVDs. This systematic review synthesizes predictors of RTW across acute coronary syndrome (ACS), coronary artery disease (CAD), heart failure (HF), and stroke using the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF) framework.
Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic review of systematic reviews was conducted. Background and Aims: Stroke is one of the most common neurological diseases, affecting 15 million people globally each year. The aim of this study was evaluate the effects of a rehabilitation program including Functional Proprioceptive Stimulation (FPS) on body balance and functional fitness in patients after stroke.
Methods: This randomized controlled trial was conducted at a tertiary care rehabilitation centre. Fifty patients with first stroke were recruited and randomly separated into a Sham Group (n=25) or FPS Group (n=25). E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: BASIC SCIENCE, BIOMARKERS.S. Ismael1, M. Umar2, B. Ouvrier2, G. Bix2
1Tulane University, Neuro Surgery, New Orleans, United States of America, 2Tulane University, Neuro Surgery, Clinical Neuroscience Research Center., New Orleans, United States of America
Background and Aims: Endothelial dysfunction, a key mechanism in COVID-19 illness, is also a major risk factor for vascular dementia (VaD). Reduced nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability is a likely pathogenic factor of endothelial dysfunction in COVID-19 patients. We hypothesize that endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS)deficiency contributes to brain endothelial dysfunction in SARS-CoV-2 infection and that SARS-CoV-2 infection accelerates the onset of VaD in eNOS-deficient mice.
Methods: 6-month-old eNOS+/- and WT male mice were infected with 1X104-pfu mouse-adapted (MA10) SARS-CoV-2 and animals were evaluated at 3 days-post-infection (3dpi) for changes in body weight and clinical signs of illness. Viral copy numbers and spike proteins were also quantified in lung and brain. Quantitative PCR and immunofluorescence was used to analyze the markers of inflammation and senescence. Integrated quasi-static acoustic tweezing thromboelastometry was used analyze the coagulation pathway activation.
Results: eNOS+/- infected mice exhibited more disease-associated weight loss (~15%) than WT-infected mice (~5 %). While infected WT and eNOS+/- had comparable pulmonary viral load, neither had detectable virus in the brain. Quantitative PCR analysis of whole brain-isolated mRNA showed increases in multiple proinflammatory mediators such as CCL2 and IL-6 and senescence markers such as p53 and p21 (eNOS+/- >> WT). Similarly, immunofluorescent analysis showed increased Iba1 (microglia marker) fluorescent intensity in the cortex of infected mice (eNOS+/- >> WT).
Conclusions: The eNOS+/- mice experience worsened acute SARS-CoV-2-associated morbidity indicated by increased weight loss, glial activation, neuroinflammation, and senescence markers despite a similar pulmonary viral load. This is the first experimental evidence investigating a link between eNOS and SARS-CoV-2. associated.
EH030 / #1572
PLASMA ANGIOGENESIS PROTEINS AS PREDICTIVE BIOMARKERS FOR POST-STROKE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: BASIC SCIENCE, BIOMARKERS.J.-H. Chen1,2, L. Chan1, C.-J. Hu1, Y.-C. Hsieh2
1Taipei Medical University - Shuang Ho Hospital, New Taipei, Taiwan, 2Ph.D Program in Medical Neuroscience, College of Medical Science and Technology, Taipei Medical University, Taipei, Taiwan
Background and Aims: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) affects approximately 30% to 40% of stroke survivors, leading to reduced quality of life and increased caregiver burden. However, reliable biomarkers for predicting PSCI remain lacking.
Methods: This prospective cohort study enrolled patients with acute ischemic stroke within 7 days of symptom onset. All participants received blood samplings for plasma biomarker analysis while admission and underwent cognitive assessments at 3 and 12 months post-stroke. Patients with large infarcts, strategic infarcts, or severe language or physical disabilities were excluded. PSCI was defined as a CDRSOB ⩾1 at 3 months post-event. Risk factors were identified using the backward selection method and were subsequently used to create predictive models.
Results: A total of 244 patients were enrolled, of whom 77 were classified as having PSCI. Patients with PSCI were older (64.5 vs. 56.5 years), had a higher percentage of education ⩽6 years (42.9% vs. 17.4%), higher NIHSS scores (5.33 vs. 3.62), and a higher percentage with a Fazekas scale score ⩾2 (47% vs. 31%). Follistatin levels were significantly higher in patients with PSCI (770 mg/dl vs. 628 mg/dl). Among those with PSCI at 3 months, our model—combining traditional risk factors, Fazekas scale, IL-8, and Follistatin/PLGF ratio—demonstrated higher predictive accuracy with an AUC of 0.9076. For those with PSCI at 12 months, the model consistently showed higher predictive accuracy with an AUC of 0.9415.

Conclusions: Our model demonstrated excellent predictive accuracy for PSCI by using traditional risk factors combined with plasma angiogenesis biomarkers, providing a novel approach for PSCI prediction.
EH031 / #2090
GENETIC ASSOCIATIONS OF TUMOUR NECROSIS FACTOR WITH ISCHAEMIC STROKE AND STROKE SUBTYPES
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: BASIC SCIENCE, BIOMARKERS.S. Brennan1, J. Buckley1, P. Synnott1, P. Kelly2, J. Mccabe1
1Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Stroke Service, Department Of Geriatric Medicine, Dublin, Ireland, 2Mater University, Dublin, Ireland
Background and Aims: Inflammation is an emerging target for stroke prevention. Tumour necrosis factor (TNF) is associated with stroke in observational studies. This Mendelian randomisation (MR) study aims to elucidate the causal effects of TNF on clinical phenotypes, imaging biomarkers, and stroke subtypes.
Methods: We selected variants associated with TNF levels at genome-wide significance from 30,912 European-ancestry individuals, retaining those with a directionally consistent association with rheumatoid arthritis. Summary level data for stroke-related outcomes were obtained from large consortia.
Results: We validated our TNF genetic instrument using known TNF-pathway cytokines and autoimmune traits, including psoriasis and ulcerative colitis. Following correction for multiple comparisons, 1-SD lower in genetically-predicted TNF was associated with reduced risk of ischaemic stroke (OR 0.51, CI 0.40-0.64), cardioembolic stroke (OR 0.54, 0.32-0.94), and MRI-confirmed lacunar stroke (OR 0.29, 0.15-0.56). Lower TNF was associated with reduced risk of coronary disease (OR 0.42, 0.36-0.48), peripheral artery disease (OR 0.16, 0.11-0.23), and heart failure (OR 0.59, CI 0.53-0.66). Genetically-predicted TNF reduction was associated with several cardiac magnetic resonance traits, including left atrial volume, as well as lower carotid plaque burden (β-1.00, CI -1.51, -0.48) and perivascular space volume (β−0.13, CI -0.24, -0.03). Primary associations were replicated in independent datasets.
Conclusions: This study provides genetic evidence that TNF is causally-associated with ischemic stroke and related aetiological substrates, including atherosclerosis, cardiac function, and small vessel disease. TNF may represent a treatment target for stroke prevention, and existing TNF inhibitors could be repurposed and evaluated for secondary prevention in future RCTs.
EH032 / #764
AZELIRAGON ATTENUATES AGGRAVATION OF CEREBRAL INFARCTION IN DIABETIC RATS: RECEPTOR FOR ADVANCED GLYCATION END-PRODUCT AS A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGET
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: BASIC SCIENCE, BIOMARKERS.J.S. Lee1, B.S. Yoon1, S.-J. Lee1, S.Y. Park1, E.H. Joe2, Y. Oh3, E.-J. Choi4
1Ajou University School of Medicine, Neurology, Suwon, Korea, Republic of, 2Ajou University School of Medicine, Pharmacology, Suwon, Korea, Republic of, 3Yonsei University, Institute For Convergence Research And Education In Advanced Technology, Incheon, Korea, Republic of, 4Korea University, Division Of Life Sciences, College Of Life Sciences, Seoul, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Diabetes or hyperglycemia contributes to neurological deterioration in acute ischemic stroke, yet rapid glucose control strategies have proven ineffective in clinical trials. We investigated whether targeting the receptor for advanced glycation end-products (RAGE) could prevent cerebral infarction worsening in hyperglycemic stroke.
Methods: To generate a diabetic model, streptozotocin was intraperitoneally injected in male Sprague–Dawley rats (7–8 weeks). Transient middle cerebral artery occlusion for 30 minutes was performed on the 34 days after inducing diabetes. Azeliragon, an antagonist against RAGE, was administered as a single intraperitoneal injection immediately after reperfusion.
Results: By 9.4 T animal MRI analysis, total infarct volume was significantly lower in the azeliragon group compared to the vehicle group (125.3 ± 26.2 mm³ vs. 240.5 ± 21.6 mm³; p < 0.01). The modified neurological severity scores were significantly lower in the azeliragon group compared to the vehicle group (6.4 ± 1.7 vs. 11.1 ± 0.7; p = 0.02). Immunohistochemistry and Western blot analysis revealed reactive oxygen species, and apoptotic and inflammatory markers were significantly reduced in the azeliragon group compared to the vehicle group (P < 0.05 for each). The ratio of phosphorylated to total NF-κB p65 decreased significantly in the azeliragon group compared to the vehicle group (P < 0.05). The increased levels of both TNF-α and IL-1β following cerebral ischemia were significantly reduced in the azeliragon group compared to the vehicle group (P < 0.05 for each).
Conclusions: These findings suggest that RAGE antagonism can ameliorate ischemic brain damage and neuroinflammation in diabetic stroke, offering a promising therapeutic strategy.

DIFFERENTIAL METHYLATION AND VARIABILITY METHYLATION REVEAL SPECIFIC STROKE-ASSOCIATED EPIGENETIC SIGNATURES
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: BASIC SCIENCE, BIOMARKERS.C. Gallego Fabrega1, J. Jiménez-Balado2, L. Mariné-Llorente1, A. Macias-Gómez2, N. Cullell3, J. Cárcel-Márquez1, E. Muiño1, L. Llucià Carol3, J. Martín-Campos1, P. Villatoro-González3, P. Boldo4, I. Fernández-Pérez5, P. Camps-Renom6, J. Martí-Fàbregas6, J. Jiménez-Conde5, I. Fernández-Cadenas1
1Institut de Recerca Sant Pau, Stroke Pharmacogenomics And Genetics Group, Barcelona, Spain, 2Hospital del Mar Research Institute of Barcelona, Department Of Neurology, Neurovascular Research Group, Barcelona, Spain, 3Institut de Recerca Sant Pau (IR SANT PAU), Stroke Pharmacogenomics And Genetics Group, Barcelona, Spain, 4Institut de Recerca Sant Pau (IR Sant Pau), Stroke Phamacogenomics And Genetics, Barcelona, Spain, 5Instituto de investigaciones médicas Hospital del Mar (IMIM) Hospital del Mar, Department Of Neurology, Neurovascular Research Group, Barcelona, Spain, 6Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau, Neurology, Barcelona, Spain
Background and Aims: Background: DNA methylation (DNAm) is increasingly recognized as a contributor to ischemic stroke (IS) risk. Traditional Epigenome-Wide Association Studies (EWAS) focus on differentially methylated positions (DMPs), reflecting shifts in mean methylation (location). However, biologically relevant signals may also arise from variability changes—differentially variable positions (DVPs). Joint DMP-DVP approaches integrate both mean and variance, offering greater power and insight into regulatory heterogeneity often missed by conventional analyses.
Methods: Methodology: We analyzed DNAm data from 1,139 IS patients across two hospital-based cohorts using Illumina EPIC (n=798) and 450K (n=341) beadchips. Using the jlst R package, we identified DMPs, DVPs, and joint DMP-DVPs, adjusting for age, sex, smoking, and two principal components, for each dataset. Then, 431,776 shared CpG sites were meta-analyzed, weighted by sample size. CpGs reaching epigenome-wide significance (p < 2.4×10–7) were evaluated for pathway enrichment.
Results: Results: After metanalysis, we identified 17statistically significant DMPs, 6 DVPs, and 94 DMP-DVPs associated with stroke risk. DMPs results have validated previous EWAS results highlighting inflammation and neurogenesis pathways. DVPs results are enriched in genes related to neuronal function, vascular development, and the TFG-β pathway. Interestingly, results from the DMP-DVP analysis identified genes related to inflammation processes especially in the context of neurodevelopment and neurodegenerative disorder.
Conclusions: Conclusions: Our results underscore the complementary value of DMP, DVP, and joint DMP-DVP analyses in revealing overlapping yet distinct epigenetic signatures of stroke. Incorporating methylation variability has captured regulatory dynamics linked to stroke heterogeneity and broadening future biomarker discovery.

PLASMA MULTI-OMICS BIOMARKER PROFILES ANTICIPATE OUTCOME IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE PATIENTS
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: BASIC SCIENCE, BIOMARKERS.A. Moutinho1,2,3, A. Dias1,2, J. Ronholm4, M. Ferreira1,5, C. Vaz6, S. Weiner4, R. Felgueiras6, J. Lopes6, R. Varela6, P. Castro7, B. Carvalho7, J. Vinagre1,3,8, M. Correia2,6, H. Zetterberg4, R. Magalhães2, J. Gobom4, C. Oliveira1,8, L. Maia1,2,6
1Instituto de Investigação e Inovação em Saúde, Porto, Portugal, 2Instituto de Ciências Biomédicas Abel Salazar, Porto, Portugal, 3U-Monitor Lda, Porto, Portugal, 4Institute of Neuroscience and Physiology, Department of Psychiatry and Neurochemistry, University of Gothenburg, Mölndal, Sweden, 5Faculdade de Ciências da Universidade do Porto, Porto, Portugal, 6Serviço de Neurologia, Centro Hospitalar Universitário de Santo António, Porto, Portugal, 7Serviço de Neurologia, Centro Hospitalar Universitário de São João, Porto, Portugal, 8Instituto de Patologia e Imunologia Molecular da Universidade do Porto, Porto, Portugal
Background and Aims: Despite therapeutic advances in large vessel occlusion ischemic stroke (LVO-IS), less than 50% of patients regain functional independence. A comprehensive multi-omics approach was used to identify protein and small circulating RNA (csRNA) biomarkers for LVO-IS outcome.
Methods: We selected 78 consecutive LVO-IS patients who underwent successful mechanical thrombectomy (mTICI⩾2B). Label-free quantitative proteomics was performed on plasma at admission (T0) and 24h post-treatment (T2). To expand biomarker discovery, we performed csRNA sequencing in 38 of these patients, at both timepoints. Three-month functional outcome (good: mRS<3 or unchanged) served as endpoint. Limma and Boruta-algorithm were used to select key biomarkers. Machine learning was used to generate predictive models and performances evaluated using ROC analysis.
Results: We identified 37 (T0) and 49 (T2) significantly expressed proteins (p<0.05) between outcomes. We selected a biomarker panel at T0 (n=5) and T2 (n=8), achieving AUCs of 0.58-0.88 and 0.70-0.89, across four machine learning models. Using deep csRNA sequencing, we further identified 6 (T0) and 14 (T2) differently expressed miRNAs. Combining the top 4 AUC-performing proteins and miRNAs lead to an excellent discriminatory capacity: AUCs: 0.88-0.92 (T0); 0.86-0.90 (T2). Curiously, protein biomarkers were prominently involved in immune and coagulation pathways, while csRNAs in neuronal and synaptic function/growth and stress responses.
Conclusions: Early protein and miRNA changes disclosed promising biomarkers for pre-treatment stratification and 3-month prognosis. While proteomics alone yielded good predictive models, integration with csRNAs improved accuracy and reduced biomarker number. Protein biomarkers are associated to systemic response while csRNA to neuronal-related processes.

CVST SCORE- A NOVEL PROGNOSTICATION SCORE IN PATIENTS WITH STROKE DUE TO CEREBRAL VENOUS SINUS THROMBOSIS
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: PREVENTION, STROKE IN THE YOUNG.A. Vij1, A. Deshmukh2, T. Patil1
1Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College, Datta Meghe Institute of Higher Education and Research,Sawangi, Neurology, Wardha, India, 2Northen Ontario School of Medicine, Sudbury, Canada
Background and Aims: Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis (CVST) is a disease with variable outcomes. Multiple clinical and radiological factors affect patient outcomes in CVST. The aim of this study is to develop a novel clinico-radiological scoring system that will help to determine prognosis of patients with CVST.
Methods: In this single-centre prospective observational study, 40 patients with radiologically confirmed CVST were evaluated. CVST score was calculated with the following parameters: C- Clinical status (Glasgow Coma Scale); V- Volume of parenchymal lesion (infarction and edema); S- Seizures; T- Extent of thrombosis (number of cerebral venous sinuses affected). CVST score of 1-3 was considered low and a score of 4-9 was considered high.This CVST score was compared in patients with good outcome [Modified Rankin Scale(MRS)] (MRS 3 or less) versus those with poor outcome (MRS 4 or more) at discharge.
Results: CVST score has correlation with higher disability (MRS) during hospitalisation (p=0.035) and mortality (p= 0.013). Patients with a low CVST score (3 or less) (15 patients) had a 100% survival rate in comparison with patients with a high CVST score (25 patients; 72% survival rate) [95% confidence interval 5.6-8.3]. A high CVST score was correlated with high MRS grading at discharge demonstrating poor outcome.
Conclusions: CVST score is a novel prognostication tool in Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis. It is a significant predictor of in-hospital mortality and disability. Further prospective studies with larger sample size are needed for its validation.

YOUNG ADULTS WITH ISCHEMIC STROKE IN ARGENTINA: INSIGHTS FROM THE MULTICENTER JACARANDA REGISTRY
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: PREVENTION, STROKE IN THE YOUNG.F. González1, F. Tamagnini2, J. López3, J. Barber4, M. Alet5
1Hospital Británico, Neurology, Buenos Aires, Argentina, 2Clínica de Imágenes, Center For Neurosciences, Neuquén, Argentina, 3Sanatorio de los Arcos, Neurology, Buenos Aires, Argentina, 4Hospital Cesar Milstein, Neurology, Buenos Aires, Argentina, 5Fleni, Neurology, Buenos Aires, Argentina
Background and Aims: Young adults account for up to 15% of all ischemic strokes, yet data from Latin America remain scarce. Understanding their clinical profile and outcomes is essential to inform targeted interventions and public health strategies. We aimed to characterize demographics, vascular risk factors, stroke etiology, access to acute reperfusion therapies, and 90-day outcomes in Argentine patients aged 18–50 years with ischemic stroke.
Methods: We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study including consecutive patients aged 18–50 years with ischemic stroke, enrolled between January 2015 and December 2023 across 26 centers in Argentina. Primary outcomes were functional dependence (mRS 3–5), stroke recurrence, and all-cause mortality at 90 days.
Results: The registry included 1,391 ischemic stroke in young adults. Median age was 43 years (IQR 36–47), and 54.2% were male. The most prevalent risk factors were hypertension (31.1%) and smoking (29.3%). Median NIHSS on admission was 3 (IQR 1–8). Acute reperfusion therapy was administered in 19.4%. Stroke etiology remained undetermined in 50.9% of cases; within this group, 26.3% fulfilled ESUS criteria ESUS and 18.1% were associated with patent foramen ovale. Arterial dissection accounted for 57.2% of determined causes. At 90 days, functional dependence was observed in 12.1%, stroke recurrence in 3.7%, and mortality in 4.9%.
Conclusions: Ischemic stroke in young adults represents a significant clinical challenge. Despite generally mild presentations, functional dependence and mortality remain substantial. The high proportion of undetermined etiologies highlights the need for standardized diagnostic protocols in this population, whose strokes carry a disproportionate individual and societal burden due to their early onset.

C-statistics showed adequate model performance (AUC 0.72[95%CI 0.63-0.81, Figure 3].

Conclusions: The DIAS3 score demonstrate adequate performance to predict post-CVT epilepsy in a diverse international setting.

COMPARATIVE SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY VERSUS INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS IN PAEDIATRIC ISCHEMIC STROKE: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW OF LONG-TERM NEUROCOGNITIVE AND PSYCHOSOCIAL OUTCOMES
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: PREVENTION, STROKE IN THE YOUNG.N. Sharma1, D. Schachter2
1All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Neurocritical Care, New Delhi, India, 2Emory University, Stroke, Atlanta, United States of America
Background and Aims: Acute ischemic stroke in children is a devastating rarity, yet treatment largely extrapolates from adult protocols due to ethical constraints in paediatric trials. Mechanical thrombectomy(MT) and intravenous thrombolysis(IVT) are emerging options, but their comparative long-term outcomes remain underexplored in children.
To systematically evaluate safety, recanalization efficacy,and long-term outcomes-functional recovery (mRS 0-2),neurocognitive (PSOM), quality of life (PedsQL), psychosocial health (psRRQ), recurrence,and disability-free survival-of MT versus IVT in paediatric ischemic stroke.

Inclusion: comparative studies in patients <18 y treated with MT or IVT, N ⩾ 4 per arm, imaging-confirmed stroke, reported outcomes at ⩽1 month, 1-6 months, and > 6 months. Random-effects meta-analysis pooled ORs for binary outcomes; mean differences for continuous metrics.Heterogeneity assessed via 12.Risk of bias evaluated with RoB 2/NOS.

Results: Thirty-two studies(n=920; MT 610,IVT 310) included; 19 qualified for quantitative synthesis(> 6 mo).MT significantly improved recanalization(84% vs 54%; OR 4.30 [95% CI 2.90-6.40], R 28%) and functional independence at long-term follow-up (75% vs 61%; OR 1.95 [1.40-2.70], 1234%) (Figure 1). Complication rates were comparable (MT 4% vs IT 4.5%).
Conclusions: This systemic analysis of robust, peer-reviewed paediatric data demonstrates MT offers superior recanalization and functional outcomes in pediatric stroke, with promising neurocognitive and psychosocial recovery. Prospective multicenter trials will assist establishment of therapeutic guidelines.
EH039 / #868
COMPARATIVE EFFECTIVENESS OF SODIUM-GLUCOSE COTRANSPORTER-2 INHIBITORS VERSUS INCRETIN-BASED THERAPIES ON STROKE PREVENTION IN PATIENTS WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES: RETROSPECTIVE COHORT STUDY USING THE TRINETX DATABASE
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: PREVENTION, STROKE IN THE YOUNG.K.-C. Chang, Y.-W. Pai, M.-H. Chang
Taichung General Veterans Hospital, Taichung, Taiwan
Background and Aims: The impact of specific glucose-lowering drugs (GLDs) on stroke risk in type 2 diabetes remains unclear. We evaluated whether sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) reduce the risk of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke compared with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i).
Methods: This retrospective cohort study used data from the TriNetX Analytics Network, including patients with type 2 diabetes aged ⩾18 years (2015–2023), excluding those with prior stroke. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated stroke incidence after ⩾12 months of GLD use. Propensity score matching (PSM) was applied to balance the SGLT-2i, GLP-1RA, and DPP-4i cohorts.
Results: After PSM, our first cohort consisted of 216,966 patients treated with metformin and SGLT-2i and an equal number treated with metformin and DPP-4i. SGLT-2i was associated with a lower risk of total stroke (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.746, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.713–0.780), ischemic stroke (HR: 0.769, 95%CI: 0.734–0.806), and hemorrhagic stroke (HR: 0.565, 95%CI: 0.505–0.631) compared to DPP-4i. Our second cohort included 188,097 patients treated with metformin and SGLT-2i and another 188,097 treated with metformin and GLP-1RA. The risk of total and ischemic strokes was lower with the use of SGLT-2i than with GLP-1RA (HR: 0.945, 95%CI: 0.897–0.995; HR: 0.941, 95%CI: 0.891–0.994, respectively), but no difference was observed in the risk of hemorrhagic stroke.

Conclusions: In adults with type 2 diabetes, the use of SGLT-2i is associated with a lower risk of total, ischemic, and hemorrhagic stroke compared to DPP-4i, and a reduced risk of total and ischemic stroke, but not hemorrhagic stroke, when compared to GLP-1RA.

DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A RISK ASSESSMENT TOOL FOR ISCHEMIC STROKE IN CANCER PATIENTS
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: PREVENTION, STROKE IN THE YOUNG.T. Kawano1, Y. Gon1, T. Morishima2, T. Sasaki1, I. Miyashiro2, H. Mochizuki1
1University of Osaka, Neurology, Suita, Japan, 2Osaka International Cancer Institue, Osaka, Japan
Background and Aims: Cancer patients have an increased risk of ischemic stroke, which is associated with worse clinical outcomes and has an unpredictable onset. However, there is currently no reliable risk prediction model. We aimed to create a risk prediction model for ischemic stroke in cancer patients within the first 2 years after diagnosis of cancer.
Methods: A cohort of 26,717 cancer patients from the University of Osaka Hospital was used to develop the model. A cohort of 31,881 patients from Osaka International Cancer Institute was used for external validation. Data in the development cohort generated an AHANDS score for prediction ischemic stroke within 2 years after a cancer diagnosis: Age ⩾75 years, Hypertension, Atrial fibrillation, a high Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, an elevated D-dimer level, and cancer Stage IV or distant metastasis at the time of cancer diagnosis. Discrimination was assessed using the c-statistic. We compared the AHANDS and Khorana scores in the development cohort.
Results: Ischemic stroke occurred within 2 years of diagnosis of cancer in 163 patients (0.61%) in the development cohort and in 99 (0.31%) in the validation cohort. The AHANDS score performed better than the Khorana score in the development cohort (c-statistic 0.71 vs 0.54; p <0.0001). A similar result was obtained in the external validation cohort (c-statistic 0.75).
Conclusions: The AHANDS score had moderate discrimination ability in both the development and external validation cohorts. This score can help clinicians to initiate the most appropriate management for patients at the time of diagnosis of cancer.
EH041 / #885
10-YEAR STROKE INCIDENCE IN CHINA: COMBINED EFFECTS OF LIFESTYLE AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE PREDICTED RISK
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: PREVENTION, STROKE IN THE YOUNG.Q. Li, W. Li
National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases, Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College, Medical Research And Biometrics Center, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: Stroke imposes a substantial disease burden. This study aimed to investigate the combined effects of the 10-year predicted cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk and lifestyle on the 10-year actual stroke incidence.
Methods: Data from 14,189 participants in the Chinese Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology (PURE) study was analyzed. The 10-year predicted CVD risk was calculated using WHO's non-laboratory-based models and categorized into low (<5%), moderate (5% -<10%), and high (⩾10%) levels. A comprehensive healthy lifestyle score was created based on six indicators: BMI, smoking, alcohol consumption, physical activity, diet, and sleep duration. Multivariable Cox frailty models, with the study center as a random effect, were used to calculate hazard ratios.
Results: Stroke occurred in 5.59% (793/14,189) of participants over a median follow-up of 12.0 years. Each 1% increase in the 10-year predicted CVD risk was associated with an 11% increase in the 10-year stroke risk (HR 1.11, 95% CI 1.10-1.13). Each 1-point increase in the healthy lifestyle score reduced the 10-year stroke risk by 9% (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.85-0.97). Joint analysis showed that individuals with moderate-to-high 10-year predicted CVD risk and a healthy lifestyle score of 0-2 had the highest 10-year stroke risk compared to those with low 10-year predicted CVD risk and a healthy lifestyle score of 5-6 (HR 5.01, 95% CI 3.14-8.00).

Conclusions: The findings highlight a significant association between 10-year predicted CVD risk and stroke, with healthy lifestyles offering substantial protection, and combined high predicted CVD risk and poor lifestyles posing the greatest threat.

Background and Aims: Cryptogenic stroke (CS), representing ischemic strokes of unknown etiology, poses a significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Background and Aims: Developing clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) is resource-intensive. To ensure consistent guideline-based rehabilitation care in Singapore, the project aimed to develop the Singapore Stroke Rehabilitation Guidelines by adapting high-quality CPGs for stroke rehabilitation.
Methods: In line with recommendations from the Guidelines International Network, we used the ADAPTE framework (three phases of set-up, adaptation and finalization) to guide our methods. First, a guideline committee of experts was formed. Second, a high quality CPG (the Australian and New Zealand Living Clinical Guidelines for Stroke Management) was selected as the source guideline due to it being a living guideline and the use of the recommended Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach to rate the quality of evidence and determine the strength of recommendations. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS ON THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF DUAL-TASK TRAINING IN ENHANCING COGNITIVE AND MOTOR RECOVERY IN POST-STROKE REHABILITATION
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: REHABILITATION AND LIFE AFTER STROKE.N. Aderinto1, I. Abraham2, G. Olatunji2, E. Kokori2, I. Yusuf3, F. Adejumo4, J. Olatunbosun5, F. Akintepede1, D. Olawade6, A. Babalola7, O. Asifat8, E. Ogungbemi9, P. Bolaji10
1LADOKE AKINTOLA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY, Ogbomoso, Nigeria, 2³Department of Medicine and Surgery, University of Ilorin, Ilorin, Nigeria, 3Department of Medicine and Surgery, Obafemi Awolowo University, Ife, Nigeria, 4Department of Medicine and Surgery, Bowen University, Iwo, Nigeria, 5Lagos University Teaching Hospital, Lagos, Nigeria, 6Department of Allied and Public Health, School of Health, Sport and Bioscience, University of East London, London, United Kingdom, 7Kornberg School of Dentistry, Temple University, Philadelphia, United States of America, 8Georgia Southern University, Georgia, United States of America, 9Rostov State Medical University, Rostov-on-Don, Russian Federation, 10Dorset County Hospital NHS Foundation Trust UK, Dorchester, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Stroke is a major global cause of disability, impairing motor and cognitive functions and hindering independence. Dual-task training (DTT) is an emerging rehabilitation strategy. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluate the efficacy and safety of DTT in promoting cognitive and motor recovery after stroke.
Methods: We searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Directory of Open Access Journals from inception to December 2024 for studies evaluating DTT in adults (⩾18 years) with ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. Primary outcomes included gait speed, balance, and cognitive function. Secondary outcomes included functional independence and safety. Random-effects meta-analyses calculated pooled effect sizes, with heterogeneity assessed via I² statistics and publication bias evaluated using funnel plots and Egger’s test.
Results: Thirty-one studies involving 50 to 1,200 participants were included. DTT significantly improved gait speed (SMD: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.45–0.79; I² = 38%, p < 0.001) and balance (SMD: 0.54; 95% CI: 0.32–0.76; p < 0.001) compared to single-task training. Virtual reality (VR)-augmented DTT enhanced dual-task gait speed (SMD: 0.78; 95% CI: 0.50–1.06; p<0.001). Cognitive outcomes, including attention and executive function, improved significantly (SMD: 0.47; 95% CI: 0.25–0.69; p<0.001), with reduced cognitive-motor interference. DTT also enhanced ADLs (OR: 1.82; 95% CI: 1.35–2.46; p<0.001) and reduced fall risk (OR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.42–0.89; p=0.010). No serious adverse events were reported.
Conclusions: DTT is effective and safe for improving motor and cognitive recovery post-stroke, outperforming single-task interventions in gait, balance, cognitive function, and functional independence. Further RCTs are needed to optimize protocols and confirm long-term benefits across diverse stroke populations.

Background and Aims: Mental flexibility deficits, particularly in inhibition and set-shifting, are common among stroke survivors with temporal cortex lesions, significantly impacting executive functions. Conventional assessments rely on completion times and error counts, which provide limited insight into underlying cognitive processes and lack objective measurement. Eye-tracking technology offers a feasible method to obtain real-time, objective oculomotor metrics. This study explores the feasibility of integrating eye-tracking glasses with conventional assessment to objectively describe inhibition and set-shifting abilities in healthy adults, as a foundational step toward clinical application in post-stroke cognitive rehabilitation.
Methods: Eye movements on fixations, saccades, and pupil dilation were recorded using eye-tracking glasses in a group of healthy individuals performing the Trail Making Test Part B, which assesses mental flexibility. Data analysis focused on identifying eye movement patterns associated with cognitive load during task performance.
Results: Preliminary analysis revealed distinct patterns in oculomotor variables corresponding to mental flexibility. Increased fixation durations and higher fixation counts were observed during set-shifting transitions between numbers and letters. Longer saccadic latencies and increased pupil dilation were observed during response inhibition segments. Conclusions: This study demonstrated the feasibility of eye-tracking in describing inhibition and set-shifting in healthy individuals. The correlation of eye tracking metrics and mental flexibility suggested strong potential for enhancing the clinical reasoning in refining cognitive strategies for stroke survivors with greater accuracy and precision. Methods: Participants 5–45 days post-stroke were randomised to receive either aerobic training (n=105) or relaxation sessions (n=95) over four weeks. Methods: Adults (⩾18 years) discharged to home, inpatient rehabilitation facilities (IRF), or skilled nursing facilities (SNF) with a primary diagnosis of stroke, TBI, or SCI were identified from state inpatient databases of Florida, Georgia, Maryland, New York, and Washington (2016–2019). Conclusions: IRF utilization varies widely by condition, with consistent sociodemographic disparities in utilization across all conditions.

1Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education & Research, Chandigarh, Neurology, Chandigarh, India, 2Post Graduate Institute for Medical Education and Research, Department Of Neurology, Chandigarh, India, 3Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Neurology, Chandigarh, India, 4All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Neurology, New Delhi, India
Background and Aims: Large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke is a severe form of ischemic stroke with high morbidity and mortality. Early and accurate identification of LVO is critical for timely endovascular treatment. Neuroimaging markers offer potential for rapid diagnosis, prognostication, and treatment selection. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic utility of neuroimaging markers in LVO stroke.
Methods: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to March 2025. Studies reporting neuroimaging biomarkers—including CT angiography (CTA), CT perfusion (CTP), MRI diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), MR angiography (MRA), and advanced imaging metrics such as clot burden score, collateral grading, ASPECTS, and core/penumbra mismatch—in patients with confirmed LVO stroke were included. Data were synthesized using random-effects models to calculate pooled diagnostic accuracy, predictive value for recanalization, and association with clinical outcomes.
Results: A total of 62 studies (n = 11,438 patients) met inclusion criteria. High CTA clot burden score (OR 3.45; 95% CI 2.61–4.56) and good collateral circulation (OR 2.98; 95% CI 2.15–4.12) were strong predictors of favorable outcomes. Background and Aims: A comprehensive understanding of the burden of intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis (ICAS) among Asians remains limited. We aimed to describe and review the current body of literature on the prevalence of ICAS and its frequency in ischemic stroke across different Asian populations, taking into account the diagnostic modalities and criteria used to identify ICAS in these studies.
Methods: We performed a systematic scoping and rapid review of published studies reporting on the prevalence and frequency in ischemic stroke of ICAS across Asian populations.
Results: Of the 1272 identified citations, 109 were included in the review: 53 reported on prevalence, 55 on frequency in ischemic stroke, and one on both (Figure 1). Most studies were conducted in China and Hong Kong, Korea, and Japan. The reported prevalence of ICAS in Asia varied widely, from 3% to 89.4% (median 13%) (Figure 2), while frequency in ischemic stroke ranged from 7.9% to 82.4% (median 41.65%) (Figure 3). Magnetic resonance and ultrasonography were the most frequently used diagnostic modalities; most studies applied a stenosis cutoff of ⩾50%.

Conclusions: Our review supports the prevailing understanding of a relatively higher burden of ICAS among Asians, while also underscoring the substantial heterogeneity in reported prevalence and frequency in ischemic stroke of ICAS across Asian populations. The variability in diagnostic modalities and criteria used to identify ICAS likely influenced these rates. The concentration of studies in East Asia underscores the need for more research in other under-represented countries in Asia. The harmonization of diagnostic criteria and standardization of imaging protocols are needed.

Background and Aims: To identify the predominant cardiometabolic risk factors (CMRFs) mediating long-term PM2.5 exposure and stroke incidents, and assess the potential modification of CMRFs’ genetic susceptibility.
Methods: This study was based on the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China. PM2.5 concentrations during the follow-up period in 1km resolution were estimated by a satellite-based spatiotemporal model. Polygenic risk scores for stroke and CMRFs were constructed based on 534 stroke-related single nucleotide polymorphisms. Mediation analyses were employed to assess the mediating contributions of measured CMRFs at the first follow-up in the association between long-term PM2.5 and stroke in total and different genetic risk groups.
Results: During a median follow-up of 12.18 years, 2812 stroke cases of 38,702 participants occurred. Notably, the mediating effects of systolic BP showed an upward trend with genetic risk stratifications, for 15.70%, 19.85%, and 23.05% on total stroke, and 9.41%, 15.84%, and 29% on ischemic stroke.
Conclusions: This study highlighted the contributions of BPs and their genetic pathways in PM2.5 exposure-induced stroke pathogenesis and emphasized the importance of BP management integrated with reducing PM2.5 exposure for stroke prevention.

ASPIRIN'S ANTI-PLATELET REACTIVITY DIFFERS BETWEEN RECURRENT ISCHEMIC STROKE BETWEEN EXTRA AND INTRACRANIAL ATHEROSCLEROSIS
