Kyunghee University Hospital at Gangodng, Neurology, Seoul, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Ischemic stroke recur despite the use of antiplatelet agents. Various mechanisms are involved in recurrence due to intracranial and extracranial atherosclerosis (ICAS and ECAS). The high-on-aspirin platelet reactivity (HAPR) may differ between recurrent stroke due to ICAS and ECAS.
Methods: Patients with recurrent ischemic stroke as a result of large artery atherosclerosis despite the use of aspirin were consecutively enrolled. Ischemic stroke was classified as stroke due to ICAS or ECAS according to the location of culprit stenosis. An aspirin reaction unit (ARU)&gt;550 was defined as HAPR. HAPR was compared between the two groups and considering the mechanism of stroke in each groups. Factors associated with HAPR were investigated.
Results: Among the 190 patients with recurrent stroke (111 ICAS and 79 ECAS groups), 36 (18.3%) showed HAPR. ARU was higher in the ECAS than the ICAS group (492±83 vs. 465±78; p=0.028). The proportion of patients with HAPR was also higher in the ECAS than the ICAS group (27.8% vs. 12.6%; p=0.008). Male and stroke due to ECAS (reference = stroke due to ICAS; OR, 5.760; 95% CI 2.154 – 15.403; p&lt;0.001) was independently associated with HAPR. ARU level differed according to the stroke mechanisms; those with artery-to-artery embolism showed the highest ARU values. Artery-to-artery embolism was independently associated with HAPR in both ICAS and ECAS groups.
Conclusions: Recurrent stroke due to ECAS was more associated with HAPR than that due to ICAS. Artery-to-artery embolism was associated with HAPR in both recurrent ischemic stroke as a result of ICAS and ECAS.

1Haaglanden Medical Center, The Hague, Netherlands, 2Haaglanden Medical Centre, Neurology, The Hague, Netherlands
Background and Aims: Timing of neuroimaging in acute onset dizziness is a subject of debate. MRI of the brain is generally considered the best available reference standard. However, up to 20% of posterior circulation strokes may be missed if the MRI is performed within 48 hours. This study aims to determine the yield of late versus early MRI in patients with isolated acute onset continuous dizziness.
Methods: We performed a prospective multicenter cohort study in eleven centers in the Netherlands in which 810 patients were recruited. In this substudy we included 197 patients who underwent two MRI scans using a standardized protocol: one early MRI (less than 48 hours after presentation on emergency department (ED)) and one late MRI (more than 72 hours after presentation on ED). Late MRI was only performed if early MRI showed no central cause. We compared the number of central causes detected by both MRIs. These are preliminary results of a subset of the PROVIDE-study.
Results: Late MRI detected an additional two strokes, which were not detected on early MRI. This corresponds to a number needed to scan of 99 for detecting a central cause.
Conclusions: The additional yield of late MRI is low, as exemplified by a number needed to scan of almost 99 patients to detect one extra patient with stroke.

1Humanitas University, Milan, Italy, 2University of Calgary, Calgary, Canada, 3University Hospital of Tours, Tours, France, 4University of Calgary, Dept Of Neuroclinical Sciences, calgary, Canada, 5Ottawa Hospital, ottawa, Canada, 6University of British Columbia, Neurology, Vancouver, Canada, 7Interior Health, Kelowna, Canada, 8University of Toronto, Toronto, Canada, 9University of Saskatchewan, Saskatoon, Canada, 10University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, Canada, 11Dalhousie University, Halifax, Canada, 12University of Calgary, Department Of Clinical Neurosciences, Calgary, Canada
Background and Aims: We aim to evaluate whether 24-hour CT infarct density a) modifies the relationship between 24-hour CT infarct volume and functional outcomes and b) is associated with functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke (AIS).
Methods: Data are from the AcT trial (Alterplase vs. Tenecteplase in AIS within 4.5 hours). Patients with detected 24-hour CT infarct and no parenchymal hematoma were included. To capture within-lesion heterogeneity, “24-hour CT standardized infarct density” was calculated as mean Hounsfield Unit (HU)/standard deviation for every patient. Primary outcome was the 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (mRS). Effect modification of infarct density on the relationship between infarct volume and outcomes was evaluated using multiplicative interaction terms. Associations with outcomes were assessed with adjusted regression analyses.
Results: Of 1577 patients, 839 (53.2%) were included (median age 75 years [IQR=64-84], 414 ([9.3%] females. Median 24-hour CT infarct volume was 7.5 mL (IQR=1.6-28.0), and median 24-hour CT standardized infarct density was 4.8 standardized-HU (IQR=4.0-5.8). There was a significant interaction between 24-hour CT infarct volume and standardized infarct density on mRS (p-interaction=0.001) and mortality (p-interaction=0.014). Higher 24-hour CT standardized infarct density (i.e., less severe infarct degree) was associated with better 90-day mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 0.87 [95%CI=0.80-0.96] per 1-standardized-HU increase), whereas 24-hour CT infarct volume was not (acOR 0.96 [95%CI=0.90-1.01] per 5-mL increase).

Conclusions: The 24-hour CT infarct density modified the effect of infarct volume on functional outcomes. Less severe infarct degree was associated with better functional outcomes. CT infarct volume and density may provide complementary prognostic information.

Background and Aims: Complete reperfusion (TICI 3) after endovascular therapy (EVT) for large-vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke does not always halt ischemic damage. We quantified post-recanalisation infarct growth on diffusion-weighted MRI (DWI) and explored its determinants and clinical impact.
Methods: We retrospectively studied 189 consecutive LVO patients with baseline CT perfusion, “early” DWI ⩽24 h (median 1.7 h) and “delayed” DWI 24–168 h (median 92.8 h) after EVT. Infarct volumes were extracted by automated JLK-CTP/DWI software. Growth was the absolute volume change between scans. Predictors were assessed with robust linear regression; associations with 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) were tested using multivariable logistic regression and mediation analysis.

Results: Median infarct volume increased from 4.8 mL to 11.7 mL, yielding a median growth of 4.4 mL; 26 patients (13.8 %) showed lesion shrinkage. Larger baseline ischemic core (rCBF < 30 %) (β = 0.187 ± 0.025 mL per mL, p < 0.001) and higher admission glucose (β = 0.049 ± 0.018 mL per mg/dL, p = 0.007) independently predicted greater growth. Each decile increase in infarct growth lowered the odds of functional independence (mRS 0–2) at 90 days (adjusted OR 0.81, 95 % CI 0.68–0.95) and excellent outcome (mRS 0–1) (OR 0.80, 95 % CI 0.69–0.93). Infarct growth partially mediated the association between baseline core volume and 90-day mRS (p = 0.02). Models incorporating delayed DWI volume discriminated outcomes better than those using early DWI or CTP core alone (Figure).
Conclusions: Substantial infarct enlargement can occur hours to days after technically successful EVT, driven chiefly by larger baseline core and hyperglycaemia and translating into worse functional recovery. These findings highlight the need for adjunct neuroprotective strategies and support delayed DWI lesion volume as a robust surrogate end-point for future acute-stroke trials.

E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, NEUROIMAGING, IMPLEMENTATION & TRANSLATIONS, LARGE ARTERY DISEASE, HEALTH SERVICES.V. Altersberger1,2, J. Kaesmacher3,4, A. Mujanovic4, L. Churilov5, F. Werdiger1, G. Sharma6, J. Gralla3, U. Fischer7, B. Campbell6

Background and Aims: The most accurate magnetic resonance perfusion (MRP) parameter for estimating the ischaemic core is considered to be relative cerebral blood flow (rCBF) at <32%. However, due to physiological differences in CBF and ischaemic tolerance this threshold may differ in gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM).
Methods: Acute stroke patients with large vessel occlusion presenting at the University Hospital Bern between 2015-2022 who underwent MRP and MRI with T1 and diffusion MR were included. GM and WM were segmented in T1. Diffusion MR was used to segment the ischaemic core. rCBF thresholds (<14%–<46% at 2% increments) were compared to the ischaemic core segmented into GM and WM compartments. Volumetric agreement was assessed by reduced major axis regression analysis (RMA). Spatial agreement was assessed via receiver-operating-characteristic analysis.
Results: Of 186 patients included, volumetric agreement was best using rCBF<32% in the total brain (RMA-slope 1.02, CI95% 0.98-1.07), rCBF<36% in GM (RMA-slope 1.00, CI95%0.96-1.04), and rCBF<26% in WM (RMA-slope 1.00, CI95%0.94-1.05). Overall, rCBF <32% yielded the highest Youden index (0.43). For GM, highest and second-best highest Youden index were at rCBF<34% (0.43) and at rCBF<36% (0.42). For WM, rCBF<26%, rCBF<28%, and rCBF<30% yielded similar spatial agreement (Youden index 0.45). Greater than 10ml overestimation of the ischaemic core was reduced by 50% using to the combined threshold (rCBF<26%+rCBF<36%) compared to the overall rCBF<32%-threshold.
Conclusions: Using separate thresholds for gray and white matter improved the accuracy of ischaemic core estimates in our MRP cohort and might be used as a surrogate for CT perfusion.

Background and Aims: Stroke remains a leading cause of morbidity, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, where disparities in access to specialized care persist. Telestroke programs offer a scalable strategy to expand access to expert evaluation and reperfusion therapy. This study reports the initial outcomes from the first six months of telestroke implementation in seven hospitals across Brazil, all of which had no prior capacity for intravenous thrombolysis (IVT).
Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of telestroke consultations performed between month 1 and month 6 after implementation. Patient data included age, sex, initial National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), administration of IVT, post-IVT NIHSS, and the occurrence of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), classified according to ECASS II criteria.
Results: A total of 329 telestroke consultations were conducted, with 220 cases of ischemic stroke. IVT was administered in 107 patients (48.6%), while 113 received best medical management. The main contraindications for IVT were time window >270 minutes (49.5%) and mild, non-disabling symptoms (33.6%). Among those treated with IVT, the mean age was 62.3 years (±13), with 50.5% female. Median NIHSS before and after IVT was 9 and 1, respectively. ICH occurred in 8 cases (7.5%), predominantly ECASS II type (75%).
Conclusions: In neurologically underserved Brazilian hospitals, the introduction of telestroke enabled IVT administration where it was previously unavailable. These early results demonstrate the feasibility and potential impact of telestroke in expanding hyperacute stroke care in middle-income settings.

IMPACT OF ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGES IN CARDIOLOGICAL EVALUATION ON THE MANAGEMENT OF ISCHEMIC STROKE PATIENTS IN A STROKE UNIT: A COST-EFFECTIVENESS AND OUTCOME IMPROVEMENT ANALYSIS
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.J. Marta-Enguita1,2,3, P. De La Riva3,4,5, A. De Arce4,5, N. Diez4,5, F. Gonzalez4,5, J. Equiza4,5, I. Villanueva Benito4,5, C. Del Bosque Martin4,5, A. Lopez De Turiso5, R. Laspiur Gandara5, M. Martinez-Zabaleta4,5
1Hospital Universitario Marques de Valdecilla, Neurology Department, Santander, Spain, 2IIS Idival, Santander, Spain, 3RICORS-Ictus, ISCIII, Madrid, Spain, 4Hospital Universitario Donostia, San Sebastian-Donostia, Spain, 5IIS BioGipuzkoa, Stroke Research Lab, San Sebastian, Spain
Background and Aims: A comprehensive cardiological evaluation in patients with ischemic stroke (IS) is essential, and a multidisciplinary and early approach may be both beneficial and cost-effective in this population
Methods: This study evaluates the impact of modifying the cardiological evaluation protocol for patients with IS through a cost analysis and a comparative observational study of two periods: pre-modification (July 2020–December 2020) and post-modification (July 2022–July 2023). The implemented changes comprised (Figure 1): extending the evaluation window to include atrial assessment in urgent CT angiography, onsite cardiology evaluation in the stroke unit, bedside cardiac ultrasound within the first 24h, prolonged cardiac monitoring during hospitalization, and a home-based prolonged monitoring circuit managed by the stroke team.
Results: The implemented changes reduced the average hospital stay (6.54 days vs 7.37; p<0.05) and modified the profile of requested diagnostic tests (Figure 2), resulting in a cost savings of 1031€ each 100 patients (2020 n=305, 2022-23 n=596). Additionally, there was a significant increase in the detection rates of AF (19% vs. 6%, p < 0.01) and major cardioembolic sources, such as cardiac thrombus and severe left ventricular dysfunction (11.7% vs. 5.7%, p < 0.01), although the overall etiological profile of strokes showed minimal changes (Figure 3). Including the LA in acute CTA assesment enabled the detection of a definite thrombus in the lA or left atrial appendage in 2.01% of cases.

Conclusions: Organizational changes in the care of IS patients can shorten hospital stays, reduce costs, and improve early detection of cardiological conditions associated with an increased risk of early recurrence.
EH096 / #865
PREDICTORS OF MRI IMAGING IN A RAPID-ACCESS TIA AND MINOR STROKE CLINIC
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.D. Eveson1, K. Patel1, A. Samadder1, S. Roy1, S. Sunil1, M. Nadeer1, A. Mistri1, J. Minhas2, D. Swienton1, A. Frost1, T. Lebutt1
1University Hospitals Leicester NHS Trust, Leicester, United Kingdom, 2University of Leicester, Leicester, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: In the rapid-access TIA clinic, same-day MRI head imaging is often limited by capacity. The study aimed to identify clinical and demographic factors influencing MRI selection in this setting.
Methods: We analysed data from consecutive patients referred between 2012–2024 to a single-centre one-stop clinic for suspected TIA or minor stroke. All had at least one symptom plausibly related to focal cerebral dysfunction and were assessed within 2 days of symptom-onset by a senior neurovascular clinician. Patients with known MRI contraindications, intolerance, or NHS data opt-out were excluded. Symptom features, demographics, and investigation findings were analysed in a logistic regression model, with same-day MRI vs no MRI as the outcome.
Results: In 5,621 patients, MRI was significantly more likely to be conducted in patients presenting with symptoms attributable to the posterior circulation, longer symptom-duration, crescendo events and currently smoking. MRI was significantly less likely to be conducted in older patients, those with dementia, on anticoagulants, with atrial fibrillation, or abnormal neurological exam. No significant associations were found with sex, ethnicity, social deprivation, carotid status, or other medical history. In a subgroup with linked brain imaging data at the point of referral (n=2,706), prior imaging was associated with reduced MRI use, especially when the findings explained the clinical presentation or showed chronic infarction.
Conclusions: Same-day MRI selection in a TIA clinic is significantly influenced by symptom type, age, cognitive status and smoking. Prior imaging findings significantly impact MRI decisions, especially when diagnostically informative.
EH097 / #872
SCREENING FOR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION IN ELDERLY WOMEN (SAFE-W): INTERIM RESULTS
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.S. Chaturvedi, K. Grimes, M. Srivastava, G. Ramani, S. Gottlieb, P. Mehndiratta
University of Maryland School of Medicine, Baltimore, United States of America
Background and Aims: In the United States, women have higher rates of death and disability from stroke than men. Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a leading cause of stroke in older women. Early identification of AF in this group with subsequent anticoagulation can be a useful strategy to reduce the burden of stroke.
Methods: This prospective, clinical study enrolled women >70 years with no prior diagnosis of AF and no stroke or TIA in the past year. Patients scoring >/=4 on the CHA2DS2-VASc score, were monitored by means of a Zio patch. Patients and their physician were made aware if an AF diagnosis was made. Assessments were conducted via telephone at 6- and 12-months post-monitoring to evaluate health outcomes.
Results: Among 70 participants, the mean age was 76.3 years (SD ± 10.6). Demographics included 74.3% African American, 22.9% white, 1.4% Asian. The median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 5, with 32.1% of participants having a history of heart failure. The mean monitoring duration of 12.1 ± 3.2 days. Among the participants who completed monitoring, AF prevalence was 3.3%. For participants diagnosed with AF, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 6.5. Additionally, 90% had episodes of supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), 26.7% had ventricular tachycardia (VT), and 18.3% experienced atrial tachycardia (AT).
Conclusions: Screening high-risk women over age 70 years with a 2-week cardiac monitor is useful for identifying subclinical AF, with a number needed to screen of 30. Pending confirmation in larger studies, screening for AF could be an important element of health maintenance for women, similar to mammography and other screening methods.
EH098 / #1770
PERSON- AND FAMILY-CENTERED CARE FOR THE STROKE POPULATION: A QUALITATIVE DESCRIPTIVE STUDY
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.M. Premnazeer1, S. Munce2, M. Bayley3, M. Gill1, O. Scali1, J. Sessford1, J. Cameron1
1University of Toronto, Rehabilitation Science Institute, Toronto, Canada, 2Holland Bloorview Kids Rehabilitation Hospital, Bloorview Research Institute, Toronto, Canada, 3Toronto Rehabilitation Institute, Kite Research Institute, Toronto, Canada
Background and Aims: Most people with stroke (PWS) need support from caregivers across care settings and in the community. These transitions can impact the caregivers' health and the care they provide, highlighting the importance of continuity of care – connected support that meets the person’s needs and personal context. Person- and family-centered care (PFCC) is a model of health service delivery that aims to support both the PWS and their caregiver. To date, no PFCC model addresses continuity of care across the care continuum for the stroke population. This is the first study examining the perspectives and preferences of PWS and caregivers for PFCC across the care continuum.
Methods: A qualitative descriptive method was used. Interviews explored PWS and caregivers’ perspectives on PFCC across the care continuum. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.
Results: 20 PWS and 18 caregivers were interviewed separately. The overarching theme highlighted the role caregivers play in continuity of care, emphasizing their need for PFCC to support these efforts. Three themes describe how PFCC can support PWS and caregivers in their continuity of care endeavours: (1) Partnerships with healthcare professionals (HCPs) enable caregivers and PWS to optimize continuity of care; (2) HCPs, caregivers, and PWS co-create care plans; and (3) HCPs, caregivers, and PWS co-manage care plans across the care continuum.
Conclusions: A PFCC model that incorporates partnerships, co-creation and co-management of care plans with caregivers, PWS, and HCPs over time, can also address the need for improved continuity of care.

Background and Aims: Stroke is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality globally, with sub-Saharan Africa experiencing a disproportionately high burden due to limited access to organized acute care. The Tanzania Stroke Project (TSP) was initiated to establish acute stroke services at two large tertiary hospitals: Muhimbili National Hospital-Mloganzila and Bugando Medical Centre in collaboration with the Tanzanian Ministry of Health, World Stroke Organization, and Hospital Directors.
Methods: TSP implemented a three-tier approach from August 2023 to August 2024 including: Establishment of stroke registries, Training of healthcare workers (HCWs) and development of acute stroke protocols and dedicated stroke units.
Results: A total of 460 adults were enrolled in stroke registries (mean age 60±15 years). Haemorrhagic stroke was the most common type (59%). Hypertension was the most prevalent risk factor (81%). Over half (58%) presented more than 24 hours after symptom onset. Only 11% received swallowing screenings. Among patients with intracerebral haemorrhage, 11% and 47% achieved blood pressure and glucose control targets respectively. In-hospital mortality was 27%. HCW training participation was higher at Bugando (57%) than Muhimbili (23%) (p=0.002). Based on training and current evidence, stroke care protocols were developed, leading to the establishment of stroke units with a minimum of 8 beds at each facility. Full impact assessments are ongoing.
Conclusions: TSP represents the first structured implementation of stroke services in Tanzania. The project emphasizes the value of a tiered implementation strategy, strong stakeholder engagement, and the need for continuous training, quality improvement, and community awareness to improve outcomes.

SATISFACTION OF NON-NEUROLOGIST PHYSICIANS WITH TELEMEDICINE SUPPORT FOR ACUTE STROKE IN BRAZIL: A MULTICENTER STUDY
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.N. Ribeiro1, D. Zan2, N. Pertile2, J. Bastianello2, J.B. Clares De Andrade3
1Universidade Federal de São Paulo, São Paulo, Brazil, 2TeleAVC, Porto Alegre, Brazil, 3Universidade Federal de Sao Paulo, Health Informatics ; Neurology, São Paulo, Brazil
Background and Aims: Physician satisfaction plays a key role in the success of Telestroke programs, particularly among non-neurologists who manage acute stroke in facilities without in-house specialists. Their engagement is essential for sustained adherence to protocols. Collecting structured feedback from these professionals can guide improvements in platform usability, reduce response times, and enhance communication features. This study aimed to evaluate the satisfaction of non-neurologist physicians with telemedicine support for acute stroke within the Brazilian TeleAVC network.
Methods: A total of 92 non-neurologist physicians across 8 hospitals participating in the TeleAVC network were invited by email to complete a structured questionnaire. The network operated through a secure mobile platform offering protected communication, DICOM imaging visualization, audiovisual resources, and formal documentation of teleconsultations in the patient’s medical record. The questionnaire comprised 7 items rated on a 5-point Likert scale.
Results: Thirty-five physicians completed the survey. Participants had a mean age of 38.3 years (±8.9), with an average of 10.9 years (±8.5) since graduation; 62.9% were male, and 74.3% reported no prior telemedicine experience. Most respondents agreed or strongly agreed that telestroke was feasible (94.3%), easy to implement (91.4%), and beneficial for professional development (82.2%). High levels of satisfaction were reported regarding support received (91.4%), confidence in stroke management (77.1%), and self-assessed quality of care (88.6%). A total of 91.4% perceived improvements in local stroke care after telestroke implementation.
Conclusions: The integration of audiovisual tools, DICOM access, and documented teleconsultations contributed to high satisfaction, perceived usability, and self-reported professional growth among non-neurologist physicians in the Telestroke network.

INFLUENCING FACTORS IN HEALTH PROMOTING BEHAVIORS OF ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE PATIENTS
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.H. Lee1, C.K. Kim2
1Korea University Guro Hospital, Stroke Rapid Response Team, SEOUL, Korea, Republic of, 2Korea University Guro Hospital, Neurology, Seoul, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Effective health-promoting behaviors after acute ischemic stroke are critical for secondary prevention and recovery. This study aimed to evaluate the levels of health literacy, e-health literacy, stroke knowledge, educational needs, and health promotion behaviors among first-time acute ischemic stroke patients, and to identify key factors influencing their health-promoting behaviors.
Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted with 135 patients admitted to a stroke intensive care unit at a university-affiliated hospital in Seoul from November 2021 to June 2022. Data were collected using structured questionnaires assessing health literacy, e-health literacy, stroke knowledge, educational needs, and health behaviors. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson’s and Spearman’s correlation coefficients, Scheffé’s post-hoc tests, and hierarchical multiple regression using IBM SPSS 28.0.
Results: Health-promoting behaviors were significantly associated with BMI, smoking status, diabetes, and high-risk drinking. Higher scores were found among patients who were non-smokers, non-obese, non-diabetic, and not high-risk drinkers. Health-promoting behaviors correlated positively with stroke knowledge and educational needs and negatively with NIHSS scores at discharge. Hierarchical multiple regression analysis showed smoking, obesity, diabetes, stroke knowledge, and educational needs significantly predicted health promotion behaviors, explaining 32.8% of total variance.

Conclusions: To enhance health-promoting behaviors among acute ischemic stroke patients, personalized interventions targeting stroke education, smoking cessation, obesity management, and diabetes control are essential. These findings provide robust evidence for developing tailored educational programs and interventions aimed at improving patient outcomes through effective secondary stroke prevention strategies.

DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A PREHOSPITAL MACHINE LEARNING MODEL TO PREDICT STROKE TYPE IN SUSPECTED STROKE PATIENTS: A SECONDARY ANALYSIS OF THE INTERACT4 TRIAL
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.S. He1, J. Yang2
1The First Affiliated Hospital ofChengdu Medical College, Chengdu, China, 2Sichuan Provincial People's Hospital, Department Of Neurology, Chengdu, China
Background and Aims: It has been proven that prehospital blood pressure reduction could improve outcomes for hemorrhagic stroke patients, while it can be harmful for ischemic stroke patients. However, existing prehospital stroke type prediction tools face challenges such as high costs and low accuracy. We aim to develop and validate a machine learning model based on prehospital clinical characteristics for predicting ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke in prehospital settings.
Methods: We analyzed data of suspected stroke patients from INTERACT 4. The study group was divided into a derivation cohort (37 centers in western China, n = 1262) and an external validation cohort (14 centers in estern China, n = 989). Prehospital clinical characteristics were included as potential predictors. The outcome was stroke types defined by posthospital CT. Models were developed using machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, LASSO, random forest, support vector machine, gradient-boosted decision tree, Classification and Regression Trees). Prediction performances were quantified by area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity.
Results: The parameters associated with stroke type were gender, age, blood pressure, heart rate, history of diseases (ischemic stroke, coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and diabetes), and history of antiplatelet therapy. The final model demonstrated strong predictive ability, with AUCs of 0.791 (accuracy: 0.714, sensitivity: 0.755, specificity: 0.670) in the derivation cohort and 0.805 (accuracy: 0.874, sensitivity: 0.643, specificity: 0.897) in the validation cohort.
Conclusions: Our machine learning model based on prehospital clinical characteristics reliably predicts the specific stroke type (ischemic or hemorrhagic), supporting individualized prehospital management for hyperacute stroke patients.

EUROPEAN STROKE ORGANISATION VISION GUIDELINES: RECOMMENDATIONS FOR ASSESSMENT AND REHABILITATION OF VISUAL DISORDERS
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.F. Rowe1, L. Hepworth1, M. Coco-Martin2, C. Gillebert3, L. Vega2, A. Palmowski-Wolfe4, E. Papageorgiou5, S. Ryan6, K. Skorkovska7, A. Aamodt6
1University of Liverpool, Institute Of Population Health, Liverpool, United Kingdom, 2University of Valladolid, Valladolid, Spain, 3KU Leuven, Leuven, Belgium, 4University of Basel, Basel, Switzerland, 5University Hospital of Larissa, Larissa, Greece, 6Oslo University Hospital, Oslo, Norway, 7Masaryk University, Brno, Czech Republic
Background and Aims: Visual problems after stroke are common. The purpose of this European Stroke Organisation guideline is to provide evidence-based recommendations to assist clinicians in decision making around diagnosis and treatment on visual problems after stroke. We report the recommendations for visual disorders.
Methods: Through international discussion, and with independent peer review, we identified PICOs (Population/Intervention/Comparison/Outcomes) for review. For each, we performed a systematic literature review search with subsequent title/abstract screen followed by full text screen, completed independently by two authors. Data was extracted and risk of bias completed for each included study. Quality of evidence for each outcome measure was evaluated by GRADE (Grading quality of evidence and strength of recommendations).
Results: There are 13 PICOs for screening and management of visual disorders for adult stroke survivors. Early vision screening should be undertaken to detect these disorders. This is feasible/acceptable within 3-4 days post onset of stroke; most can be assessed within 1 week. Screening should be undertaken by specialist eye team assessment or at least by using a validated vision screening tool. Screening improves the detection rate of presence of visual disorders whilst specialist visual assessment further improves the accuracy of detection of visual impairment. We suggest individualised intervention targeted at the specific type of visual problem that has arisen. We suggest referral to specialist eye services for the targeted management of these disorders.
Conclusions: The intention is that these guidelines will be of use to any clinician working with stroke survivors.

EH105 / #1434
DEVELOPMENT OF A PATIENT-COMPLETED STRUCTURED MODIFIED RANKIN SCALE TOOL TO SUPPORT STANDARDIZED STROKE DISABILITY ASSESSMENT
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: HEALTH SERVICES & PRE-HOSPITAL CARE & NURSING.L. London1, N. Kamal2
1Dalhousie University, Industrial Engineering, Halifax, Canada, 2Dalhousie University, Department Of Industrial Engineering, Halifax, Canada
Background and Aims: The modified Rankin Scale (mRS) is the most widely used tool for assessing disability following stroke. Simple and clinically meaningful, its administration remains subjective and inconsistent especially in mid-range grades, where inter-rater reliability is lowest. Existing mRS grades focus only on mobility and daily tasks, overlooking other domains commonly affected by stroke, like communication and cognition. This project aims to develop a structured Clinical Assessment Tool (CAT) to support more consistent, holistic, and patient-accessible mRS grading.
Methods: The CAT was designed to align with existing mRS grades while enhancing structure and reproducibility. Grounded in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI), the tool evaluates four key domains: mobility (0-4), daily tasks (0-4), communication (0-2), and cognition (0-2). Each domain contributes to a cumulative score (0–12), which maps directly to mRS grades 0–5. The tool uses simplified text, visual cues, and a guided user interface to reduce cognitive load and enhance usability.
Results: The completed CAT introduces a structured scoring system with clearly defined contributions from each domain (Figure). It consists of one question per domain with multiple response options, using plain language and accessible visuals to support patient or caregiver self-completion. By addressing vague criteria and reducing reliance on clinician judgment, the tool offers a more consistent and inclusive approach to mRS grading. A validation study with stroke survivors is planned to assess real-world utility and accuracy.

Conclusions: This structured CAT modernizes mRS assessment by improving standardization, usability, and recovery representation. Future work will focus on clinical validation and integration into stroke care workflows .

1Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, China, 2Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular therapy (EVT), nearly 40% of large vessel occlusion (LVO)-related acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients experience suboptimal functional recovery, potentially due to residual distal microthrombi. Methods: We independently extracted data from six RCTs that enrolled patients with AIS who receive IAT following successful EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset, with a minimum follow-up of 90 days. Results: FMA-UE scores were 29.9±18.9 (acute/early subacute, n=156), 31.1±12.3 (late subacute, n=33), and 31.9±15.1 (chronic, n=33). TSRT correlated positively with μ (r=0.386, p<0.001), strongest in acute/early subacute (r=0.592) and chronic (r=0.410) groups. TSRT was negatively correlated with MAS (r=−0.317, p<0.001), stronger in the acute/early subacute group (r=−0.469). TSRT and μ together explained 72% of the variance in synergy/reflex FMA-UE subscores. TSRT alone explained 68.7% of the total FMA-UE score variance.
Conclusions: Results suggest a significant relationship between spasticity and upper limb motor impairment measured by the FMA-UE following stroke. TSRT and μ are potential key biomarkers for assessing and monitoring recovery at the impairment level in stroke rehabilitation.

1The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Kowloon, Hong Kong PRC, 2University of Maryland Baltimore, Baltimore, United States of America, 3sity of Maryland Rehabilitation & Orthopaedic Institute, Baltimore, United States of America, 4ltimore Veterans Affairs Medical Center and University of Maryland, Baltimore, United States of America

We aim to evaluate whether serum fibrinogen is associated with increased arterial stiffness in a Portuguese hypertensive population.
Methods: We studied 860 Portuguese hypertensive individuals (aged 52.0±8.0 years; 53.3% male). Pulse wave velocity (PWV) was determined using the Complior method. Background and Aims: Hypertension is a predictor of cognitive decline. Whether cognitive performance leads to hypertension remains uncertain. Our aim was to evaluate the role of cognitive function as a predictor of incident hypertension among Hispanic/Latino adults, a group with high rates of untreated hypertension.
Methods: Methods: We included 6,755 individuals from the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos who were hypertension-free at Visit 1. Cognitive function at Visit 1 (2008-2011) was measured using a global cognition score (GC), which comprised the averages of four z-transformed neurocognitive tests. Incident hypertension, defined as blood pressure ⩾130/80 mmHg or on treatment, was ascertained at Visit 2 (2014-2017). The association of GC with incident hypertension was investigated using regression analyses adjusted for the baseline sociodemographic characteristics. Pathway analyses assessed whether behavioral factors (obesity, smoking, physical activity [PA] not at goal, and low diet-quality) were pathway variables between GC and incident hypertension.
Results: Results: Median [IQR] age was 53[48-59] years, and 62% were females. Fifty-seven percent of individuals had incident hypertension. After adjustment for confounders, higher GC was associated with lower odds of hypertension (OR=0.86; 95% CI 0.74-0.99). PA not at goal and current smoking were pathway variables between GC and obesity which, in turn, led to hypertension. Low diet quality was associated with higher odds of obesity and hypertension, but was not a pathway variable between GC and incident hypertension.
Conclusions: Lower global cognitive scores predict incident hypertension six years later. Behavioral risk factors may contribute to the association of cognitive function with hypertension.

A NEW SCREENING PROCEDURE FOR SPATIAL NEGLECT TO REDUCE LEFT-RIGHT ASSESSMENT BIAS IN THE NIH-STROKE SCALE: RESULTS FROM A PROSPECTIVE CROSS-COUNTRY STUDY
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: COGNITION AND DEMENTIA, ANEURYSM/AVM INTERVENTION, NEUROCRITICAL CARE, SMALL VESSEL DISEASE.I. Celpacenko1, V. Matijosaitis1, H. Hjaltason2, T. Vanagas1, E. Ívarsson3, M. Klinke2
1Lithuanian University of Health Sciences, Neurology, Kaunas, Lithuania, 2University of Iceland, Reykjavik, Iceland, 3Landspitali University Hospital, Reykjavik, Iceland
Background and Aims: The National Institute of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) is widely used for stroke severity assessment, but it underestimates right-hemisphere deficits like spatial neglect (SN). This study evaluates a modified NIHSS Item 9 (n-NIHSS-9) for simultaneous screening of aphasia and SN.
Methods: A prospective study enrolled consecutive patients within seven days of stroke onset. The adapted n-NIHSS-9, using an A4-sized “Cookie Theft” picture, served as an index test for the dual assessment of aphasia and SN. Additional index tests included the Star Cancellation Test (SCT) and Line bisection test. The simplified Catherine Bergego Scale (sCBS) served as the reference standard.
Results: Analysis included 632 hemispheric stroke patients (51.7% male, mean age 70.4 years, SD = 12.88, range 24–103). Ischemic strokes accounted for 89.4% of cases. The overall prevalence of SN was 27.5% (left-sided 19.7% vs. right-sided neglect 7.8%). The n-NIHSS-9 demonstrated a sensitivity of 78.29% (95% CI: 70.18–85.07) and a specificity of 98.47% (95% CI: 98.11–99.64). Sensitivity was similar for left-sided (78.79%; 95% CI: 69.42–86.36) and right-sided SN (79.17%; 95% CI: 57.85–92.87). Overall accuracy was 93.65% (95% CI: 91.16–95.61) with a non-completion rate of 19.6%, primarily due to aphasia and impaired consciousness. The n-NIHSS-9 required <30 seconds to administer. In comparison, the sensitivity of SCT was 75.51% and Line bisection test 36.36%, with non-completion rates of 29.2% and 32.9%, respectively.
Conclusions: The n-NIHSS-9 is a practical and time-efficient tool for routine screening of SN, helping to reduce the bias in stroke severity scoring between left- and right-hemisphere strokes.

Background and Aims: Dedicated stroke care employing specialized multiprofessional teams reduces mortality/dependency after acute stroke. Telemedicine is frequently used to provide neurological expertise in hospitals without continuous inpatient Neurology service. However, the validity of teleneurological consultation has almost exclusively been evaluated during initial patient assessment and management but not in the setting of follow-up visits being important for determination of stroke etiology, risk assessment, and planning stroke aftercare.
VISIT-STROKE evaluated the quality of teleneurological follow-up visits compared to conventional on-site visits, focusing on guideline adherence and potential limitations or advantages of telemedicine.
Methods: A prospective multicenter study (10/2022–12/2024) involved 15 hospitals in four German TeleStroke Unit networks. The primary endpoint was the correct fulfillment of six quality indicators: etiological classification, NIHSS-based neurological examination, risk appraisal, diagnostic recommendations, secondary prevention, and rehabilitation planning, rated each by three blinded external neurovascular experts. Results: Among 518 patients, 501 received both visit types (median age 71y). Teleneurology outperformed onsite visits regarding etiological classification (96.8 vs 83%), neurological examination (99.4 vs 90.6%), risk assessment (98.6 vs. 79.4%), diagnostic recommendations (97.8 vs 77.2%), secondary prevention (98.0 vs 86.2%), and rehabilitation planning (99.2 vs 85.4%).
Conclusions: Teleneurology allows guideline-compliant follow-up assessment without any loss of quality compared to onsite follow-up visits.

NOVEL METABOLICALLY GLYCOENGINEERED NEURAL STEM CELLS TO TREAT ISCHEMIC BRAIN INJURY
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: COGNITION AND DEMENTIA, ANEURYSM/AVM INTERVENTION, NEUROCRITICAL CARE, SMALL VESSEL DISEASE.X. Jia, X. Liu, S. Marasini
University of Maryland School of Medicine, BALTIMORE, United States of America
Background and Aims: Cardiac arrest (CA)-induced brain injury leads to severe neurological deficits with limited treatments. Neural stem cell (NSC) transplantation shows therapeutic promise, but its effectiveness is limited by delivery challenges and cell viability after transplantation. We recently developed metabolic glycoengineering (MGE) to improve cell viability and ultimately boost the therapeutic efficacy of transplanted NSCs through modifying their glycans. This report evaluates the effects of different delivery routes for this innovative approach of using MGE-modified NSCs (MGE-NSCs) to treat ischemic brain injury post-CA.
Methods: MGE-NSC therapy was used to treat rats with 9min- or 11min-asphyxia CA, representing severe and very severe brain injury after CA, by comparing randomly selected intranasal and intracerebroventricular (ICV) delivery administered 3 hours after resuscitation. Neurological deficit scores (NDS), and neurobehavior tests were compared 3 days and 4 weeks after CA. Tracking of transplanted MGE-NSCs was evaluated by immunofluorescence staining.
Results: Both delivery methods supported neuron differentiation, angiogenesis, and synaptic plasticity. ICV delivery showed better early recovery outcomes, with improved NDSs shortly after treatment. However, at 4 weeks, the intranasal route outperformed ICV in late-stage recovery, improving locomotor function and reducing anxiety-/depression-related behaviors. Intranasal delivery also promoted broader MGE-NSC distribution, enhanced survival, and reduced microglia activation.
Conclusions: ICV was superior in short-term, while intranasal delivery was more effective in long-term recovery. These results highlight the potential of MGE-NSC therapy and the importance of tailoring delivery strategies for different recovery phases after CA-induced brain injury.

Background and Aims: Management of brain aneurysms (BA) has progressively shifted over time, with an increasing preference for minimally invasive approach. This study assessed a ten-year trend in neurosurgical interventions and in-hospital outcomes for unruptured BA in Kazakhstan.
Methods: National Inpatient Data for unruptured BA hospital admissions was analysed. Log-linear regression applied to compute the Average Annual Percent Change. Multinomial logistic regression was used to examine the association between the type of intervention and the outcomes (in-hospital mortality, no change, and improvement).
Results: Between 2014-2024, data from 698 medical institutions in Kazakhstan recorded 9,390 interventions for unruptured BAs. The mean patient age was 53.1±12.7 years, with 68.3% being female. Arterial hypertension was present in 24.5% of cases, and 86.3% were admitted electively. The average length of hospital stay was 9.4± 8.7days. Overall, surgical interventions demonstrated a significant upward trend, increasing by an average of 7.4% annually (95% CI: 0.95–13.24; p=0.028). Endovascular procedures rose significantly by 8.9% per year (95% CI: 2.17–14.92; p=0.014), while microsurgical procedures declined by 3.5% annually (95% CI: -10.40–3.28; p=0.269) (Figure1). Microsurgical treatment was associated with significantly higher odds of in-hospital mortality compared to endovascular treatment (RRR=4.32; 95% CI: 3.08–6.06; p<0.001). Older age (71–80 years) also significantly increased the odds of death (RRR=2.72; p=0.033), while gender showed no significant association with outcomes. Figure 1.

Conclusions: An upward trend in the rate of endovascular intervention was observed over the 10-year period in Kazakhstan, while microsurgical treatment and advanced age were associated with higher in-hospital mortality.

Background and Aims: Prediction of intracranial aneurysm (IA) rupture remains challenging due to limited understanding of the underlying pathophysiology. Previous studies have indicated the importance of inflammatory processes, particularly macrophage infiltration. This study aims to integrate morphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular data to better characterize inflammatory changes associated with aneurysm rupture.
Methods: Neurosurgically resected IA walls (ruptured and unruptured) were formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded. Control samples were obtained from the circle of Willis arteries of cadavers and were formalin-fixed and paraffin-embedded too. Histological analysis, immunohistochemistry (CD45R0, HLA-DR for M1, CD163 for M2 macrophages), and quantitative real-time PCR (CD163, MMP2, TIMP1) were performed. CD163 was higher in ruptured vs. unruptured IAs (p = 0.029), while MMP2 was paradoxically lower (p = 0.008).
Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate significant macrophage-driven inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling in IA walls. The observed shift in macrophage polarization and altered MMP2 expression suggest complex immunopathological dynamics preceding rupture.

Background and Aims: Rapid differentiation of stroke subtypes—acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH)—is critical for timely treatment. This systematic review and meta-analysis compares machine learning (ML) models utilizing diverse omics biomarkers combined with clinical data versus diagnostic imaging modalities (CT/MRI) for differentiating stroke subtypes.
Methods: Systematic searches of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Ovid, TRIP, and CINAHL databases were performed until March 31, 2025. Conclusions: ML models combining proteomic biomarkers or imaging modalities with clinical diagnosis show the highest accuracy in differentiating stroke subtypes. Proteomic biomarkers emerge as a compelling non-invasive alternative, nearly comparable to conventional imaging, underscoring their translational potential for clinical practice.

Background and Aims: Transient global amnesia (TGA) is an acute, self-limiting amnesia syndrome, characterized by temporary memory impairment without permanent neurological deficits. Its etiology is still unclear, though vascular factors, especially anatomical variants of the posterior cerebral artery (PCA), may contribute. This study examines the relationship between PCA types and hippocampal diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesions in TGA patients, and compares the occurrence of different PCA types in TGA patients versus a control cohort.
Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 372 patients with clinically confirmed TGA (2011-2021). DWI lesions in the hippocampus were assessed in relation to PCA types, determined from CT angiography or T2-weighted MRI sequences. A control cohort of 120 individuals was included. Statistical analysis was performed using chi-square tests and Fisher’s Exact Test.
Results: In the TGA cohort, specific fetal PCA types were significantly more frequent compared to the control group. The left fetal PCA type occurred in 32 TGA patients versus 3 controls (p = 0.0091), and the right fetal PCA type in 31 TGA patients versus 3 controls (p = 0.0143). Bilateral fetal PCA was also more frequent in TGA patients (12 vs. 0 cases, p = 0.0420) (also see Figure 1). Additionally, DWI lesions were associated with the presence of certain PCA variants in TGA patients.
Conclusions: Fetal PCA variants are more common in TGA patients compared to controls. These findings suggest that vascular anatomy, particularly the configuration of the posterior cerebral circulation, may contribute to the pathogenesis of TGA.

BLOOD-BASED INFLAMMATORY MARKERS IL-6 AND YKL-40 SHOW DIFFERENT KINETICS REGARDING THE OCCURRENCE OF STROKE-ASSOCIATED PNEUMONIA

1Germans Trias i Pujol Research Institute (IGTP), Neurosciences, Badalona, Spain, 2VIB-UAntwerp Center, Antwerp, Belgium, 3Hospital Germans Trias i Pujol, Neurology, Badalona, Spain, 4Vall d'Hebron Institute of Research (VHIR)-Universitat Autónoma de Barcelona, Neurovascular Research Laboratory, Barcelona, Spain, 5Institute de Biomedicine of Seville, IBiS/Hospital Universitario Virgen del Rocío/CSIC/University of Seville, Hospital Universitario Virgen Macarena, Neurology, Sevilla, Spain, 6Germans Trias i Pujol Hospital, Barcelona, Spain
Background and Aims: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is a common post-stroke complication, contributing to higher mortality rates and poorer functional outcomes. This multicentre study aimed to evaluate the expression profiles of inflammatory markers IL-6 and YKL-40 during the first 48 hours after stroke onset in both SAP and no SAP (NOSAP) ischemic stroke patients.
Methods: Prospective, multicentre study including ischemic stroke patients with moderate-severe stroke (NIHSS>4) within 24 hours after onset. SAP was diagnosed with modified CDC criteria. Blood samples were collected within 24 hours of stroke onset and between 24 and 48 hours. IL-6 and YKL-40 levels were measured using multiplex immunoassays or ELISA, and statistical analyses were performed with GraphPad Prism software.
Results: The study included 353 patients, of which 39 (11%) developed SAP. IL-6 levels were three times higher in SAP patients compared to NOSAP patients along both timepoints (p<0001). Stroke patients not developing SAP showed a slight increase of IL-6 levels over time (p=0.0238). YKL-40 levels decreased by 50% over time (comparing samples obtained within 24 hours to those obtained between 24 and 48 hours) in both SAP and NOSAP patients, p=0.0001).
Conclusions: The inverse early-phase trajectories of IL-6 (increasing) and YKL-40 (decreasing) after stroke suggest time-sensitive biomarker evaluation is critical for SAP prognostication. Different biomarkers might perform different to predict or detect SAP depending on time of measurement.

RECURRENT POSTERIOR CIRCULATION STROKES IN A YOUNG PATIENT: A DIAGNOSTIC DILEMMA
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: STROKE IN THE YOUNG AND UNCOMMON ETIOLOGIES, EARLY (YOUNG CAREER), BIOMARKERS.M.U. Mazhar, M. Mirza, M.A. Shahid
University Hospital Coventry and Warwickshire, Coventry, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Antiphospholipid antibody syndrome (APS) and vertebral artery dissection (VAD) are both recognized causes of stroke in young patients, though the coexistence of both in a single patient is rare. We will present a unique case of a young patient with both APS and VAD, highlighting the clinical challenges, diagnostic approach, and management considerations associated with this rare and complex presentation.
Methods: A 39-year-old man presented with headache, dizziness, and unsteady gait. CT confirmed an acute left cerebellar infarct. Given his young age, further workup was done where CTA showed left vertebral artery dissection. He was started on DAPT and discharged homer after a couple of days. Four days post-discharge, he re-presented with vertigo. MRI revealed new bilateral cerebellar infarcts. Blood tests showed elevated Cardiolipin and Beta-2 GP antibodies, raising suspicion for antiphospholipid syndrome (APLA). He had another stroke while inpatient affecting the brainstem. Given this rapid recurrence of strokes despite being on DAPT, he was referred to Haematology for confirmation of APLA and was started on Warfarin.
Results: The repeat Antibodies were positive confirming APLA. CT Angio already confirmed the presence of Vertebral artery dissection. Patient did not have any further strokes after initiation of warfarin.
Conclusions: This case highlights diagnostic and management challenges in a young patient with multiple strokes having dual pathologies. Initially the patient was treated on the lines of dissection but despite optimal management patient continued to have strokes. After further investigations, we confirmed presence of APLA along with VAD and therefore patient was started on warfarin which eventually treated both pathologies.

EARLY BLOOD PRESSURE MANAGEMENT AS A CONFOUNDER IN INTRACEREBRAL HAEMORRHAGE TRIALS: LESSONS FROM THE STOP-MSU TRIAL
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE, COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.C. Mutimer1, N. Yassi1, L. Churilov2, B. Campbell1, G. Donnan2, S. Davis1, H. Zhao1
1Royal Melbourne Hospital, Melbourne Brain Centre, Parkville, Australia, 2University of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia
Background and Aims: Contrary to expectations, the STOP-MSU trial of tranexamic acid (TXA) versus placebo in intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) <2h from onset did not find a beneficial effect on haematoma expansion (HE) at 24h. One confounder of this result may be acute blood pressure (BP) management and variability (BPV), for which data was not collected. We conducted a post-hoc analysis to investigate BP in the active and control arms and association with HE.
Methods: We included patients with adequate BP data enrolled in STOP-MSU. BP management followed local protocols. BPV was assessed using BP range (maximum – minimum) and standard deviation in the first 4-hours. We assessed the association between time-to-BP control and 24h-HE using logistic regression and tested for an interaction between time-to-BP control and treatment allocation.
Results: Of 201 enrolled patients, 151 were included (median age 66years, 43.1% female, 53.6% TXA, HE 34.8%). Median baseline systolic BP (SBP) was 167.5mmHg, and at 4-hours was reduced by ~13% (Figure 1). Patients randomised to TXA had numerically higher median baseline SBP (170 vs. 160mmHg, p=0.21), longer median time-to-BP control (⩽140mmHg; 4 vs. 3hours, p=0.35) with similar median BP reduction at 4-hours (20.5 vs. 23.5mmHg, p=0.81). BPV was similar between groups (standard deviation:15.9 vs.15.8mmHg, range:39.5 vs. 40mmHg). There was no significant interaction between time-to-BP control and randomisation group in relation to HE (p=0.65).

Conclusions: BP control was generally poor in STOP-MSU, which may have impacted the potential benefits of TXA. Our findings underscore the importance of integrating BP lowering into care bundles when designing future ICH trials.

E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE, COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.L. Prats-Sanchez1, Á. Lambea-Gil1, J. Martí-Fàbregas1, G. Ezcurra1, M. Guasch1, J.M. Fernandez-Vidal1, P. Camps-Renom2, A. Martínez-Domeño1, A. Ramos-Pachón1, I. Hic-Cat1
1Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau, Neurology, Barcelona, Spain, 2Hospital de La Santa Creu i Sant Pau, Stroke Unit, Neurology Department, Barcelona, Spain
Background and Aims: This study aimed to assess outcome differences in patients with intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) according to their history of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) as well as their pretreatment.
Methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted using the HIC-CAT population-based and consecutive database (March 2020–March 2022). We included ICH patients aged ⩾18 years admitted within 24 hours of symptom onset in Catalonia (Spain) who underwent a 3-month follow-up. A history of MACE—defined as prior ischemic stroke, ICH, or ischemic heart disease—was essential for analysis. The primary endpoint was a favorable functional outcome at 3 months (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0–2). Comparisons between patients with and without prior MACE were performed using logistic regression models, adjusting for age, NIHSS, intraventricular hemorrhage, ICH volume and location (supratentorial/infratentorial), and pre-ICH mRS score. Pretreatment interactions (antiplatelets, anticoagulants, and statins) were explored.
Results: Among 1,821 patients (mean age 72.2±14.0 years; 38% women), 23.9% had prior MACE (12.1% ischemic stroke, 7.2% ICH, and 10.8% ischemic heart disease). Prior MACE was associated with lower odds of achieving a favorable outcome (adjusted OR:0.61, 95%CI:0.47–0.79). We observed an interaction with anticoagulant use (interaction coefficient:1.56, p=0.012), suggesting that the use of anticoagulants in ICH patients with prior MACE increased the odds of an unfavorable outcome. No significant interactions were detected for antiplatelets or statins.
Conclusions: A history of MACE in patients with ICH is a significant predictor of 3-month functional outcome, and the concomitant use of oral anticoagulant appears to increase this risk.

SEX DIFFERENCES IN IMAGING FINDINGS AND LONG-TERM OUTCOMES OF PATIENTS WITH INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE, COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.Y. Arakaki1, K. Miwa1, M. Shiozawa1, A. Ogawa1, R. Inutuka1, S. Iwamoto1, S. Saito2, K. Toyoda1, M. Ihara2, M. Koga1
1National Cerebral and Cardiovascular Center, Department Of Cerebrovascular Medicine, Suita, Japan, 2National Cerebral and Cardiovascular Center, Department Of Neurology, Osaka, Japan
Background and Aims: Clinical features of sex differences in acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) are limited, including cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) findings on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
Methods: This was a retrospective study of supratentorial ICH from a prospectively collected single-center NCVC Stroke Registry (2010–2022). Outcomes of interest were ICH location (lobar or deep), SVD findings (white matter hyperintensities [WMH], cerebral microbleeds [CMBs], lacunes), hematoma volume, hematoma expansion (6 ml or 33% increase), and poor outcomes (modified Rankin scale [mRS] score ⩾ 4) at 90 days and 1 year. Results: A total of 1,865 patients with ICH were evaluated (mean age 72, 43.5% female). Conclusions: Among patients with acute ICH, no significant sex differences were observed in SVD findings and clinical outcomes, apart from the presence of lacunes and hematoma volume.

EXPLORING THE UNDERLYING MECHANISM OF HYPEROSMOLAR THERAPY IN THE DYNAMIC REGULATION OF CEREBRAL AQUAPORIN MEDIATED EDEMA IN INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE, COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.U. Mukherjee1, K. Dhalayat1, S. Chowdhury1, M. Hasan1, B. Ghosh1, A. Datta1, J. Roy2, P. Bhattacharya1
1National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, Ahmedabad, Pharmacology And Toxicology, Gandhinagar, India, 2Manipal Hospitals, Mukundapur Cluster, Neurology, Kolkata, India
Background and Aims: In intracerebral hemorrhage(ICH), hematoma expands leading to brain edema and secondary injury. This injury impairs the blood brain barrier(BBB) integrity and exacerbates neuronal loss. Limiting hematoma expansion and reducing brain edema are the prevalent therapeutic approaches. Hyperosmolar therapy using mannitol is prevailing clinical intervention; with rebound edema as a negative outcome. The role of mannitol in modulating the dynamic function and regulation of cerebral aquaporins(AQPs) may have a role in brain edema progression. Thus, deciphering the dynamic role of mannitol and AQPs expression towards progression of brain edema may help redefine the therapeutic regime of hyperosmolar therapy for better post-ICH outcome.
Methods: ICH was induced in Sprague Dawley(SD) rats using 0.5U of CollagenaseVIIS. Mannitol(1.5mg/kg) was administered intravenously at multiple time points post-ICH. The brain edema was assessed by extravasation studies, swelling index, brain water content and molecular studies. In-vivo fluorescent imaging was performed to access secondary neurodegeneration.
Results: The neuronal damage and cerebral edema were observed to be exacerbated in the ICH group as compared to the control, sham and mannitol groups. An increased blood brain barrier disruption was also observed in the ICH group. The fluorescence intensity of matrix metalloproteinases(MMPs) in the ICH group was observed to be enhanced as compared to the control groups, whereas mannitol treated animals exhibited lower MMP fluorescent intensity.
Conclusions: The present study will delve into the underlying mechanism of modulation of AQPs to prevent exacerbation of secondary brain injury and edema associated with ICH with a possibility of new therapeutic paradigm for hyperosmolar therapy.

VASOSPASM AND TOPOGRAPHY DISTRIBUTION OF DELAYED CEREBRAL INFARCTION IN ANEURYSMAL SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE: A SINGLE CENTER COHORT STUDY
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE, COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.I. Marques1, N. Vasconcellos2, C. Rouanet3, V. Lessa1, E. Rocha1, G. Sampaio4
1Federal University of São Paulo, Vascular Neurology, São Paulo, Brazil, 2Mayo Clinic, Vascular Neurology, Jacksonville, United States of America, 3Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Vascular Neurology, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 4UNIFESP-Escola Paulista de Medicina Head Clinical Trialist/Neurologia Hospital Israelita Albert Einstein, Neurology, Sao Paulo, Brazil
Background and Aims: Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) is a leading cause of poor outcomes in survivors of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and often results in established cortical infarcts. Vasospasm is one of the recognized contributors to DCI and serves as a clinical tool for risk stratification. Herein, we aim to investigate the spatial distribution of cerebral infarction, which remains understudied, and assess its association with arterial vasospasm.
Methods: Retrospective data from a Brazilian tertiary center (2016-2024) were assessed for demographic, clinical and radiological variables. Vasospasm was diagnosed via transcranial Doppler and/or digital subtraction angiography. DCI-related infarctions were identified on follow-up brain CT or MRI in areas unrelated to surgical procedures.
Results: Of 321 patients (median age 55 years [IQR 46-63], 74% female), 24% presented with poor grade SAH (WFNS 4-5), and 66% underwent clipping. DCI-related infarction occurred in 82 patients (25%). As cerebral infarction may occur in more than one location in each patient, the total number of territories affected by DCI was 125, with the following territory distribution: middle cerebral artery (73, 89%), anterior cerebral artery (32, 39%), posterior cerebral artery (11, 13%), internal carotid artery (5, 6%), and basilar artery (5, 6%). Only 68/125 infarction territories (54,4%) were co-localized with vasospasm, while 55/125 (44%) occurred without corresponding vasospasm.
Conclusions: DCI-related cerebral infarction occurred most frequently in the MCA territory, yet nearly half of infarctions developed without corresponding vasospasm. This reinforces that vasospasm represents just one component of DCI’s pathophysiology and advocates the need for multimodal monitoring strategies beyond vasospasm to prevent DCI-related infarction and morbidity.

TIMING OF ANTICOAGULATION THERAPY INITIATION AMONG NON-VALVULAR ATRIAL FIBRILLATION (NVAF) PATIENTS WITH PRIOR INTRACRANIAL HAEMORRHAGE

Background and Aims: Optimal timing of initiation or resumption of anticoagulation therapy (OAC) in patients with prior intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) is not well established. This study aimed to evaluate impact of OAC initiation timing on clinical outcomes in NVAF patients with ICH history.
Methods: Consecutive NVAF patients with (47.1%) or without (52.9%) OAC who survived index ICH between January 2018 and July 2022 in 16 public hospitals were identified and analysed. Background and Aims: To investigate whether the presence of the spot sign modifies the effects of early (⩽60 min), intensive (<140 mm Hg), and sustained (24-hour target stability) systolic blood pressure (SBP) control in acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).

EVALUATING THE CONSTRUCT VALIDITY AND TEST-RETEST RELIABILITY OF DUAL-TASK WALKING ASSESSMENTS IN PEOPLE WITH CHRONIC STROKE
E-POSTER HIGHLIGHTS: INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE, COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.C. Tsang1, T. Miller1, H. Ouyang2, M. Li1, M. Pang1, R. Chung1
1The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Department Of Rehabilitation Sciences, Hong Kong, Hong Kong PRC, 2Guangzhou Medical University, School Of Biomedical Engineering, Guangzhou, China
Background and Aims: Dual-task (DT) walking ability is important for successful return to community ambulation after stroke. However, the measurement properties of gait parameters (e.g., cadence, stride length, gait variability) used to assess cognitive-motor interference remain unknown. This study aimed to determine the validity and reliability of DT gait assessments in individuals with chronic stroke.
Methods: Test-retest reliability was determined using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC2,1). To establish construct validity, associations between DT mobility/cognitive performance and other assessments [i.e., Activities-Specific Balance Confidence (ABC), Mini-Balance Evaluation Systems Test (MiniBESTest), Fugl-Meyer Assessment for the lower extremity (FMA-LE), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), and Geriatric Depression Scale–Short Form (GDS-SF)] were assessed using Pearson’s r.
Results: Data from 87 participants with mild to moderate motor impairment (FMA-LE=25±0.5, range=15-34) were used to determine construct validity, with 32 participants completing the retest within 5-7 days of the initial assessment. Good to excellent reliability (ICC=0.79-0.99, p<0.001) was observed for all single-task and DT gait parameters. Most cognitive parameters showed moderate to good reliability (ICC=0.58–0.89, p<0.001). Correlations between motor impairment (FMA-LE) and gait parameters across all cognitive tasks were weak to moderate (r=0.34-0.56, p<0.01). Correlations between balance assessments and DT gait parameters ranged from weak to strong (MiniBESTest: r=-0.47-0.73; ABC: r=-0.22-0.57, p<0.05). Significant correlations between depression (GDS-SF) and gait parameters were weak (r=-0.30-0.33, p<0.05). No significant correlations were observed for MoCA scores.
Conclusions: Overall, during both level-ground and obstacle-crossing conditions, gait parameters were positively associated with motor function and balance and negatively associated with cognition and depression. Good reliability was also observed for most gait parameters.

Background and Aims: Lower mean Hounsfield unit (mHU) values, indicating greater CT hypodensity of perihematomal edema (PHE), have been proposed as a novel quantitative imaging marker in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Methods: We included participants with primary supratentorial ICH who had available CT scans at baseline and follow-up after 72-96 hours, and 90 and/or 180 days outcome data. We investigated (i) its change from baseline and (ii) its association with unfavorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6) in adjusted mixed-effects models, accounting for between-center and between-participant variability.
