ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.L. Gangas1,2,3, J. Marta-Enguita1,2,3,4, M. Castañon3,5, E. Lopez-Cancio3,4,5, M. De Lera Alfonso3,4,6, J.F. Arenillas3,4,6, A. Roel Garcia3,7, M. Castellanos3,4,7, M.D.M. Freijo3,4,8, A. Gomez3,8, P. De La Riva3,4,9, M. Martinez-Zabaleta3,10,11, H. Tejada Meza3,12, J. Marta-Moreno3,12, I. Beltran Rodriguez3,13, J. Timiraos Fernandez3,14
1Hospital Universitario Marques de Valdecilla, Neurology Department, Santander, Spain, 2IIS Idival, Santander, Spain, 3Research network in cerebrovascular diseases of the North of Spain (NORDICTUS), Valladolid, Spain, 4RICORS-Ictus, ISCIII, Madrid, Spain, 5Hospital Universitario Central de Asturias (HUCA), Neurology Department, Oviedo, Spain, 6Hospital Universitario Valladolid, Valladolid, Spain, 7Complejo Hospital Universitario A Coruña, A Coruña, Spain, 8Hospital Universitario Cruces, Bilbao, Spain, 9Hospital Universitario Donostia, San Sebastian, Spain, 10Hospital Universitario Donostia, San Sebastian-Donostia, Spain, 11IIS BioGipuzkoa, Stroke Research Lab, San Sebastian, Spain, 12Hospital Universitario Miguel Servet, Zaragoza, Spain, 13Complejo Asistencial Universitario de León, León, Spain, 14Hospital Universitario Alava, Vitoria-Gasteiz, Spain
Background and Aims: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a common complication after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in patients with ischemic stroke (IS) that lead to disabling deficits. The aim of this study was to assess clinical-demographic and radiological factors associated with HT following IS by developing a multivariate logistic regression model and an associated machine learning-based decision tree model to identify the most relevant factors in decision-making
Methods: A retrospective analysis of a multicentric (12 hospitals) prospective registry of IS patients treated with EVT from 1/1/17 to 31/12/21 (NORDICTUS registry, Spain). Univariate analyses were performed to explore potential determinants of HT. Subsequently, stepwise multivariate logistic regression was conducted to identify independent predictors, and a decision tree model was built using RapidMiner software (v9.10).
Results: A total of 5125 IS patients were analyzed. The multivariate logistic regression results showed that diabetes [OR(95%CI): 1.61(1.35-1.91)], endovascular procedure length (per minute)[ 1.01(1.00-10.1)], NIHSS 10-20 [1.69(1.37-2.08)], NIHSS ⩾20 [1.96(1.56-2.47)], and use of vit-K antagonists [1.38(1.11-1.71)] were associated with a higher risk of HT. Protect factors were ASPECTS⩾7 [0.41(0.33-0.51)], vertebral and basilar occlusions [0.20(0.10-0.37)], and known-onset stroke [0.81(0.70-0.94)]. AUC for this model was 0.67(0.65-0.68) (Figure 1). The ML-based decision tree revealed fasting glycemia after IS treatment (weight: 0.20), EVT procedure time (0.16), age (0.15), and NIHSS (0.09) as the most significant predictors of HT (Figure 2).

Conclusions: Our study identifies predictors of HT after EVT in IS focusing on variables with special importance in decision-making (glycemia, age, stroke severity and EVT length) through a machine learning-based approach.
EV007 / #3088
APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE ANALYSIS OF MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING FOR IDENTIFYING THE ETIOLOGY IN STROKE PATIENTS
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.I. Bozas1, I. Alfaro2, I. Daza-Perilla3, A. Frances1, A. Allende1, J.J. Martin4
1Sanatorio Allende, CORDOBA, Argentina, 2IATE, CORDOBA, Argentina, 3Center for Space Science and Technology, University of Maryland, Baltimore County, Baltimore, United States of America, 4Sanatorio Allende, Stroke Unit, CORDOBA, Argentina
Background and Aims: Objective: To develop a machine learning algorithm for the etiological classification of ischemic strokes through the analysis of brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Background: Current classification systems, such as TOAST, require multiple clinical variables to identify the cause of ischemic stroke. This study proposes an artificial intelligence model capable of analyzing MRI scans to identify early the underlying mechanisms of ischemic strokes, facilitating personalized treatment and improving healthcare resource management.
Methods: A Python-based algorithm was designed to process MRIs from stroke patients, using libraries such as NumPy, Pandas, Nibabel, and SciPy. Images were classified according to the TOAST system and sourced from Sanatorio Allende and the Stroke Outcome Optimization Project. DWI, ADC, and FLAIR sequences were selected and normalized to 130×130×150 pixels. A total of 1,180 images were randomly divided into 80% for training/validation (944) and 20% for testing (236). A supervised convolutional neural network was trained, and performance metrics were assessed.
Results: The model achieved an average accuracy of 0.43. Purity reached 1.00 for TOAST category 3, with recall values of 0.55 for category 1, 0.25 for category 2, and 0.26 for category 3.
Conclusions: Conclusions: Although initial performance was modest, accuracy improved with the inclusion of more examples. Sample imbalance and technological constraints impacted the results. It is expected that incorporating additional data, clinical metadata, and enhanced technical resources will significantly improve the model's performance and move it closer to clinical applicability.
EV008 / #2122
VALIDATING ICH VOLUME TOOLS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: ABC/2, SEMI-SEGMENTATION AND AI COMPARED
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.C. Menon1, K. Krishnan1, R. Dineen2, S.P. Parraguez2, N. Sprigg2, P. Bath2
1Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust, Division Of Medicine, Stroke, nottingham, United Kingdom, 2University of Nottingham, Nottingham, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Haematoma volume is a key prognostic indicator in intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) but is rarely measured routinely. The ABC/2 formula is widely used for its simplicity, though its accuracy is variable. Semi-automated segmentation and AI-based methods may offer better accuracy and reproducibility. To compare ICH and intraventricular haemorrhage (IVH) volume measurement across three methods—ABC/2 by eye, semi-automated segmentation, and an AI-based tool—using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) analysis.
Methods: Thirty CT scans of spontaneous ICH were analysed. Two raters—a newly trained registrar and an experienced consultant—independently measured ICH and IVH volumes using both ABC/2 and semi-automated segmentation. An AI tool independently segmented each scan. ICCs were calculated to assess inter-rater and inter-method agreement.
Results: Initially analysis of the first ten cases shows agreement between AI and human raters was excellent across both segmentation methods. ICC values ranged from 0.92 to 0.99 (all p < 0.01), with Cronbach’s alpha consistently >0.95, indicating high reliability and internal consistency. The newly trained registrar showed slightly lower consistency, as reflected in wider confidence intervals.
Conclusions: This study supports the reliability of semi-automated and AI-based tools for ICH and IVH volume estimation. Findings suggest these methods, including AI, could support routine clinical use and reduce variability in volume measurement, particularly where user experience varies. Given that haematoma volume is a strong prognostic indicator but is rarely measured in practice, integrating fast and reproducible tools into clinical workflows could help standardise care and make prognostication more accessible at the bedside.
EV009 / #835
KEY FEATURES AFFECTING REHABILITATION LENGTH OF STAY IN SINGAPORE: INSIGHTS FROM MACHINE LEARNING
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.K. Ngoh1, Y.S. Ong2, Y.S. Heng2, X. Zhang2, L.K. Hao2, K. Chua1
1Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Rehabilitation Medicine, Singapore, Singapore, 2TTSH OCEAN, Singapore, Singapore
Background and Aims: Accurate classification of Rehabilitation Length of Stay (RLOS) is crucial for optimizing resource allocation and improving patient outcomes. This project aims to develop and validate machine learning classifiers that utilize data from the first 72 hours from admission, to categorize patients into short (<3 weeks), normal (3-6 weeks), or long (>6 weeks) RLOS. Additionally, the project seeks to identify key predictors throughout the patient stay that influence these classifications.
Methods: A LightGBM classifier was developed to predict the RLOS categories using 10,486 records between Jan 2013 to Jun 2024 containing 63 data elements. These elements include demographics, admission information, clinical information, medications dispensed and laboratory results. The model was tuned using 10-fold cross-validation, and the optimal hyperparameters for the best model are n_estimators = 100 and learning_rate = 0.1 and num_leaves = 31.
Results: The model achieved an F1 score of 0.555 on test set. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis revealed the number of comorbidities, whether patients require speech therapy and psychological services, and patient’s age has the largest average magnitude of impact on the RLOS (see figure below).
Conclusions: In conclusion, the project developed machine learning classifiers to predict RLOS using early admission data. Key features include the number of comorbidities and type of services the patient had during the episode. Future work involves incorporating Functional Independence Measure scores into the classifier to enhance its predictive capabilities, improving the accuracy of RLOS predictions.

EV010 / #1069
MACHINE LEARNING-BASED PREDICTION OF SYMPTOMATIC HEMORRHAGIC TRANSFORMATION AFTER REPERFUSION THERAPY IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.M.S. Oh, S. Choi, M. Lee, B.-C. Lee
Hallym University Sacred Heart Hospital, Neurology, Anyang, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Symptomatic hemorrhagic transformation (sHT) is a critical complication after reperfusion therapy, including intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) and endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). We aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning (ML) model to predict sHT using variables available at hospital admission.
Methods: We analyzed AIS patients treated with IVT and/or EVT between June 2021 and June 2023 from a multicenter prospective stroke registry. A total of 5,043 patients were randomly split into training (80%) and validation (20%) cohorts. Five ML algorithms were trained to predict sHT—defined as hemorrhagic transformation with any neurological worsening—using 35 baseline variables imputed via k-nearest neighbors. Model performance was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC), F1-score, feature importance, and decision curve analysis.
Results: Among 5,043 patients (mean age 71±13 years, 59% male, median NIHSS 12 [IQR 16]), 63% underwent EVT alone and 37% received bridging therapy. Overall, 958 (19%) experienced sHT, more commonly in the bridging group (19%) than EVT alone (16%). The gradient-boosted decision tree model showed the best performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI, 0.81–0.87) and F1-score of 0.65 ± 0.004. Decision curve analysis demonstrated net clinical benefit, especially at lower treatment thresholds.
Conclusions: This ML-based model demonstrated promising accuracy and clinical utility for early prediction of sHT after reperfusion, supporting risk stratification in AIS management.
EV011 / #1659
SMART WEARABLE DEVICE FOR POST-STROKE DYSPHAGIA DETECTION: THE WESTRO STUDY
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.A.K. Pandit1, P. Tangri1, B. Arora1, D. Joshi2, S. Kumar2, S. Manchanda3
1All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Neurology, New Delhi, India, 2Indian Institute Of Technology Delhi, Department Of Biomedical Engineering, NEW DELHI, India, 3All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Radiology, NEW DELHI, India
Background and Aims: In around 50% of stroke survivors, dysphagia is observed as a detrimental condition. Swallowing dysfunction remains persistent in around 11-13% of stroke patients even after several months. In this study we aim at developing a wearable, non-invasive device for detecting swallowing dysfunction in stroke patients.
Methods: This is an exploratory study with a sample size of 10-cases (stroke patients with persistent swallowing difficulty from two weeks of onset of stroke or beyond) and 10-controls. The study was initiated after Institute Ethics Committee approval and CTRI registration (CTRI/2023/11/060345). 10 cases and 5 controls have been recruited till date on which our developed device has been tested simultaneously with video-fluoroscopy (VFS). Cases and controls were stepwise given liquid (diluted barium), then semi-solid (Microbar HD) and lastly solid (breadcrumbs coated with barium).
Results: The collected signals were processed using the Wavelet Scattering Transform (WST), which extracted robust, time-invariant features from both modalities, capturing relevant Spectro temporal information while ensuring resilience to noise and inter-subject variability. To manage the high-dimensional feature space, dimensionality reduction was performed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Multidimensional Scaling (MDS). These reduced feature sets were then used to train a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier to distinguish between healthy and dysphagic swallows. The SVM classifier achieved an overall accuracy of over 90%, with a sensitivity and specificity exceeding 88%, demonstrating strong agreement with VFS-based ground truth labels.
Conclusions: The device might provide with a non-invasive method for detecting swallowing dysfunction in stroke patients using wearable sensors and advanced machine learning techniques.
EV012 / #988
PREDICTING ATRIAL FIBRILLATION USING MACHINE LEARNING
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.D. Galotto, G. Milella, D.M. Mezzapesa, M. Caccamo, N. Marrone, S. Grimaldi, L. Parrulli, M. Petruzzellis
Policlinico di Bari, Neurology, Bari, Italy
Background and Aims: Cryptogenic stroke (CS) accounts for 45% of ischemic strokes, and in about 30% of these cases, atrial fibrillation (AF) is later identified. Longer cardiac monitoring improves AF detection but increases healthcare costs. To assess whether a Machine Learning (ML)-based classifier can help identify patients at higher risk of AF, improving cost-effectiveness in diagnosis.
Methods: We retrospectively analyzed clinical, echocardiographic, neuroimaging, and laboratory data from 236 CS patients admitted between February 2018 and September 2024. Mean follow-up was 16 months. AF was detected in 53 patients (22%): 34/63 with loop recorders (LR) and 19/173 without.
Results: The best-performing ML model (Gradient Boosting, AUC 0.936) identified left atrial dilation (>40 mm), elevated proBNP (>505 pg/ml), and female sex as predictors of AF. Diabetes mellitus and non-stenosing carotid plaques were associated with lower AF risk. The model showed good accuracy, identifying true negatives (90.4%) and true positives (80.0%), particularly in the first 10 months. High-risk patients, as classified by the model, developed AF more frequently and earlier during follow-up.

Conclusions: Our study supports the use of AI to develop predictive models for AF detection in CS patients, enabling individualized and cost-effective prevention strategies.
EV013 / #1867
CONCORDANCE BETWEEN PRE-THROMBECTOMY CORE VOLUME ESTIMATES AND POST-THROMBECTOMY INFARCT VOLUMES IN MCA STROKE PATIENTS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY ACROSS AUTOMATED SOFTWARE PLATFORMS
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.C. Rusu1, A. Harfoush,2, F. Elangi3, S. Lakshmi2, A. Liaretidou3, K. Chatterjee2
1Aintree University Hospital, AL, United Kingdom, 2Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Stroke And Elderly Medicine, Chester, United Kingdom, 3Mersey and West Lancashire Teaching Hospital, DR, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Accurate infarct core estimation in acute ischaemic stroke guides endovascular treatment decisions. Variability among computed tomography perfusion (CTP) software platforms in core volume estimation remains a concern. This study assessed the correlation and concordance between pre-thrombectomy core volumes estimated by different software and post-thrombectomy infarct volumes in middle cerebral artery (MCA) stroke patients.
Methods: We retrospectively evaluated MCA stroke patients with successful thrombectomy (TICI 2b or above) who underwent pre-thrombectomy CTP with core volume estimates from four automated software platforms: RAPID, Vitrea, Brainomix, and Cercare. Post-thrombectomy infarct volumes were automatically quantified by Brainomix from non-contrast CT scans performed within 48 hours post-procedure in patients without intracerebral haemorrhage. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between estimated core and infarct volumes. Additionally, proportions of cases where core volumes exceeded infarct volumes by >5 ml was assessed.

Results:RAPID AI core showed the strongest correlation with infarct volume (r = 0.55, p < 0.001), followed by Vitrea (r = 0.4) and Cercare (r = 0.37), with none for Brainomix (r = 0.01). RAPID had the highest rate of overestimation >5 ml (38%), significantly greater than Cercare (13%, p = 0.015) and Brainomix (20%, p = 0.043). Vitrea showed moderate overestimation (30%), though differences were not statistically significant. Cercare had the lowest rate. NIHSS was the strongest predictor of poor outcome (mRS 4–6) at discharge.
Conclusions: Variability in CTP core estimations compared to final infarct volumes was observed, with RAPID AI showing the strongest correlation but conservative estimates. These findings underscore the importance of nuanced interpretation of automated core volumes in clinical decision-making.
EV014 / #1096
PREDICTING CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE FROM TIA AND MINOR STROKE REFERRALS USING LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: A SINGLE-CENTRE COHORT STUDY
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.D. Eveson1, S. Roy2, K. Patel1, A. Samadder2, S. Sunil1, M. Nadeer1, D. Swienton1, J. Minhas1, A. Mistri1, T. Lebutt3, A. Frost3
1University Hospitals Leicester NHS Trust, Stroke Medicine, Leicester, United Kingdom, 2University Hospitals Leicester NHS Trust, Neurology, Leicester, United Kingdom, 3University Hospitals Leicester NHS Trust, Health Informatics, Leicester, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Over half of patients referred to TIA and minor stroke clinics do not receive a cerebrovascular diagnosis. AI-based decision support at the point of referral may improve triage by identifying non-cerebrovascular mimics (e.g., migraine, syncope) and expediting high-risk cases for urgent management.
Methods: Emergency department referral data from a rapid-access TIA clinic were used to fine-tune a large language model (LLM). Data containing presenting symptoms (as entered by the referring clinician), past medical history, medications, age, gender, and smoking status was provided to the model and then trained to classify cases as cerebrovascular or non-cerebrovascular based on the final diagnoses made by senior vascular neurologists. Only first-time clinic attendees without NHS research opt-out declaration were included. Fine-tuning was conducted over 12 epochs using an 80/20 validation/test split and 5-fold stratified cross-validation to prevent model overfitting. Multiple LLMs were tested to determine optimal fit.
Results: A total of 9,267 referrals were analysed. The ‘distilbert-base-uncased’ model from Hugging Face provided the best performance, with precision, recall, and F1-scores for non-cerebrovascular diagnoses of 0.73, 0.79, and 0.76, respectively, and for cerebrovascular diagnoses of 0.67, 0.60, and 0.63, respectively. Overall accuracy was 0.71, with a mean AUC of 0.69 (±0.02 SD). Notably, 12% of referrals had a >95% probability of a non-cerebrovascular diagnosis.
Conclusions: LLM-based analysis of referral data shows promise in supporting TIA and minor stroke triage. Further refinement is planned to enhance predictive accuracy.
EV015 / #2538
PUSHING THE FRONTIERS OF NEUROINTERVENTION: A SYSTEMATIC COMPARISON OF ROBOTIC-ASSISTED AND MANUAL ENDOVASCULAR TECHNIQUES
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.N. Sharma1, D. Schachter2
1All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Neurocritical Care, New Delhi, India, 2Emory University, Stroke, Atlanta, United States of America
Background and Aims: Background Robotic neurointervention is redefining the landscape of endovascular therapy and care. Yet, its clinical utility across cerebrovascular indications remains incompletely defined. Aims To evaluate procedural efficiency in performance, patient safety, and radiation exposure across robotic-assisted and manual interventional neuroradiology (INR) procedures in a stratified, indication-specific analysis.
Methods: A rigorous PRISMA-compliant review (Pubmed, Embase, Medline, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane; 2000-2025) identified 400 records, with 13 studies (n=538 procedures, ⩾4 patients/study) matching inclusion criteria. Both diagnostic and therapeutic interventions across all ages and pathologies were analysed. Outcomes: technical and clinical success, complications, radiation exposure, procedural time, and conversion to manual technique.
Results:Technical success for robotic procedures reached 93% (range 88-99%), with a minimal complication rate (0.7% and zero mortality.Manual conversion was required in 7%, primarily due to anatomical or device limitations. All studies reported some manual steps, reflecting current robotic constraints. Subgroup analysis (refer Table) confirmed robust outcomes across adults, pediatrics, aneurysm, stroke, and both diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. Notably, operator radiation exposure was reduced by up to 90% in robotic cases. Only one comparative study found longer procedural times for robotics, but no inferiority in safety or efficacy.

Conclusions: While robotic-assisted INR is not yet autonomous, it delivers competitive procedural efficacy with significantly reduced operator radiation thereby promising futuristic innovations. Unlike previous reviews, our analysis dissects outcomes by procedural type in adults as well as paediatric populations and highlights underreported system limitations. These insights support targeted adoption and inform future robotic design and randomized evaluation.

EV017 / #2253
MEDM-VL IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE DIAGNOSIS AND LVO IDENTIFICATION
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.X. Song1, S. Yang2, M. Li2, J. Wu1
1Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital, School of Clinical Medicine, Tsinghua Medicine, Tsinghua University, Department Of Neurology, Beijing, China, 2Tsinghua University, Department Of Electronic Engineering, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: Early diagnosis of stroke and the identification of large vessel occlusion (LVO) are critically important for administering reperfusion therapy in cases of acute ischemic stroke. Previous scales have typically relied on unimodal data, which limits their accuracy. This study aimed to develop a multimodal tool for stroke diagnosis and LVO identification.
Methods: Dataset: A dataset of consecutively collected stroke cases (n=896) and non-stroke cases (n=896) from the neurology emergency room at a comprehensive stroke center was used for model training and validation. We randomly divided the cases in a 4:1 ratio for training (n=1433) and validation (n=359). Of the stroke cases, 866 presented with ischemia and 30 with hemorrhage; among ischemic stroke, 160 patients have large vessel occlusions. MedM-VL was employed for multimodal pre-training and instruction tuning, functioning as a medical Large Vision-Language Model. Input: different data combinations were input, including CT images, electrical health records (EHR), EHR + CT image radiology report, and EHR+ CT images. Output: Stroke, Ischemia, and large vessel occlusion (LVO) (yes, no)
Results: The EHR + images group demonstrates the highest performance in identifying strokes, with an accuracy of 0.981. For ischemic stroke diagnosis, the EHR+radiology group has an accuracy of 0.970. Additionally, the model has equal accuracy in identifying LVO between EHR+CT images and EHR+CT image radiology report groups, with an accuracy of 0.785 and 0.791, respectively.

Conclusions: The accuracy of multimodal data is generally significantly higher than that of single-modality data in stroke diagnosis and LVO identification; MedM-VL is capable in CT image interpretation without radiology report.
EV018 / #2111
BRAIN-COMPUTER INTERFACE AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DETECTING COVERT CONSCIOUSNESS AFTER STROKE: PROTOCOL AND EARLY IMPLEMENTATION OF THE INTEGRATE STUDY
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.F. Vahidy1, O. Khan1, E. Baig1, H. Holland1, P. Perrin1, A. Bako1, T. Potter2
1TIRR Memorial Hermann, Houston, United States of America, 2Houston Methodist, Center For Health Data Science & Analytics, Houston, United States of America
Background and Aims: A subset of stroke survivors experience prolonged disorders of consciousness (DoC), including unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS) and minimally conscious state (MCS). Accurate differentiation between these states remains a major clinical challenge with profound implications for prognosis, care planning, and rehabilitation. The INTEGRATE study evaluates Axon-R, a novel brain-computer interface (BCI) integrating high-resolution EEG, artificial intelligence (AI), and augmented reality (AR) to enhance diagnostic precision, detect covert consciousness, and guide personalized neurorehabilitation.
Methods: INTEGRATE is a prospective, single-center observational study enrolling 30 inpatients with DoC following stroke or other severe brain injury. The Axon-R device captures EEG signals during therapy sessions, applying adaptive AI algorithms that classify neural responses and detect volitional brain activity. Augmented reality feedback is incorporated to support real-time patient engagement. Participants undergo repeated BCI-augmented physical, occupational, and speech rehabilitation sessions alongside standard assessments, including the Coma Recovery Scale–Revised (CRS-R), neuroimaging review, and behavioral observation. Stroke patients are the primary analysis group, with other brain injury patients serving as a comparison cohort. Safety, tolerability, and clinical workflow integration are systematically evaluated.
Results: Recruitment and device deployment are underway. Based on prior admissions to the DoC program, enrolled stroke patients are expected to have severe injury profiles (mean case mix index 2.75; Charlson Comorbidity Index 2.91). Among 35 prior stroke encounters, the mean CRS-R score improved from 10.6 on admission to 14.0 on discharge. Preliminary feasibility, tolerability, and neural signal detection data will be presented.
Conclusions: Axon-R may transform stroke rehabilitation by improving diagnostic accuracy, uncovering covert consciousness, and enabling precision neurorehabilitation pathways.

NAVIGATING COMPLEX ANEURYSMS: THE ROLE OF THE WOVEN ENDOBRIDGE IN MODERN NEUROVASCULAR CARE

1tbilisi state medical university, Cardiology, Tbiisi, Georgia, 2tbilisi state medical university, Neurology, Tbilisi, Georgia

The study aims to provide a systemic review of the outcomes of patients who underwent WEB devices for aneurysm treatment.
Methods: After analyzing 26 studies,the inclusion and exclusion criteria was applied, and narrowed down to 5 studies. A systematic review was performed using articles focusing on outcomes of patients who was treated using the Woven EndoBridge device from PubMed, Elsevier, and Neurology journals published between 2015-2025.

REVOLUTIONIZING NEUROSURGERY: THE IMPACT OF 3D PRINTING ON ARTERIOVENOUS MALFORMATION MODELING
ANEURYSM/AVM INTERVENTION.J. Annamalai1, D. Prakasan2, A.R. Anuz Khan2, J. Annamalai2
1tbilisi state medical university, Cardiology, Tbiisi, Georgia, 2tbilisi state medical university, Neurology, Tbilisi, Georgia
Background and Aims: Arteriovenous Malformation (AVM) is a rare, complex vascular anomaly that is caused by the tangling of the artery and vein that allows bypassing of the capillary system.Surgical treatment for AVMs is complex and technical due to the location, size, and potential for damage to brain tissue. This review aims to illustrate the significant advancements and precision in utilizing 3D printing technology for surgical planning in the treatment of AVMs.
Methods: This systemic narrative review used articles focusing on the development of 3D-printing technology in treating AVMs from PubMed,Google Scholar,Elsevier and Researchgate that were published between 2016-2024.
Results: After analyzing 30 studies from India, USA, UK, China, and Italy, inclusion and exclusion criteria were applied, and we narrowed it down to 11 studies in this review. The 49 patients before undergoing treatment for AVM, underwent reconstruction of their brains by integrating CTA, MRI, and DSA with MRV, a technique utilized for mapping the arteries that supply blood and the veins that drain it.This tool enhances the visibility of normal and abnormal blood vessels better, improving pre-surgical planning,which is shown to have a higher success rate.
Conclusions: This review showcases the significant impact of 3D printing on treating AVM. Emilio Aguinaldo College Medical Center Cavite, Dasmarinas, Philippines
Background and Aims: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) is a neurologic disease characterized by headache, vomiting, vision defects, altered sensorium, and seizures. Symmetrical vasogenic edema in the posterior cerebral hemispheric regions are the classic neuroimaging findings. Hypothesis on the cause of vasogenic edema underlying the clinical manifestations of PRES include cerebral hyperperfusion, vasospasm, and endothelial damage. It has been reported across all age groups in association with several conditions. In the Philippines, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) has been reported in patients with COVID-19, eclampsia, SLE, and two pediatric patients with post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis. PRES in patients with renal pathologies has been reported in association with chronic glomerulonephritis, SLE, non-dialytic CKD, and CKD patients on kidney replacement therapies. However, this syndrome is underrecognized in general, including in the CKD population. In this paper, we report two cases of PRES in CKD patients with hypertension.
Methods: The paper is a descriptive study using case series. Two chronic kidney disease patients with features consistent of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome were reviewed including hospital stay, imaging, and laboratory work up.
Results: Patient 1 had complete reversibility of symptoms one month after discharge. Patient 2 on follow-up telephone conversation after one year hospitalization, denied any seizure recurrence.
Conclusions: Since kidney disease is a strong clinical predictor of PRES, increased awareness of the association of this syndrome with kidney disorders will lead to early suspicion and direct treatment toward targeted management of PRES and its associated conditions to achieve maximum clinical and neurologic reversibility, prevent worse outcomes, and prevent PRES recurrence.

1on behalf of WSO - GENESIS Committee, Messina, Italy, 2WSO Operations Manager, Geneva, Switzerland, 3Neurology and Developmental Neurology at the Faculty for Special Education and Rehabilitation and Neuropsychology and Clinical Neuroscience at the Department of Psychology of the Faculty of Psychology at the University of Belgrade, Belgrade, Serbia, 4Aster Hospital Al Qusais and Muhaisnah, Dubai, United Arab Emirates, 5Hospital Moinhos de Vento, Neurology And Neurosurgery, Porto Alegre, Brazil, 6Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Nellore, Neurology, Nellore, India, 7The George Institute for Global Health, Sydney, Australia, 8Ministério de Saúde de Mozambique, Maputo, Mozambique, 9The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, Hong Kong PRC, 10MarcLind Health Consulting, Toronto, Canada, 11National Cerebral and Caridovascular Center, Department Of Neurology, Osaka, Japan, 12Epidemiology, University of Alabama, Birmingham, United States of America, 13Santa Maria della Misericordia Hospital University of Perugia, Neurology, Perugia, Italy, 14UHN - JS Sonshine Centre (U of Toronto), Neurology, Toronto, Canada
Background and Aims: While the global representation of women (W) in health sciences has improved, gender equity in medical leadership and professional recognition remains limited. Inequalities also persist in scientific research, evident in publishing, compensation, academic promotion, conference visibility, and leadership roles in societies and journals. This study retrospectively examined gender representation in leadership positions within the World Stroke Organization (WSO) from 2013 to 2024.
Methods: WSO annual reports were reviewed to collect data on gender and geographic origin of Executive Committee (ExCo) and Board of Directors (BoD) members.
Results: Over the 11-year period, 144 individuals held leadership roles—86 men (60%) and 58 women (40%). Women’s representation increased from 24% in 2013 to 50% in 2024 (Figure 1-2). Men predominantly occupied top ExCo roles such as “president” (83%), while women were more frequently assigned to roles like “secretary” (58%). On the BoD, the highest representation of women was among delegates from national and regional stroke societies (71%). Geographically, 74% of leaders were from high-income countries (36%W), 14% from upper-middle-income (55%W), and 12% from lower-middle-income countries (53%W). Women from Africa and Asia were underrepresented (27% and 34%, respectively) compared to Europe, the Americas, and Oceania (44–46%) (Image).

Conclusions: While global awareness and policies have supported increased inclusion of women in WSO leadership, significant gender disparities persist, especially in high-ranking roles. These disparities appear more culturally than economically driven. These preliminary findings highlight the need for further investigation into educational and professional pathways to better understand and address the remaining barriers to gender equity in international scientific leadership.
EV038 / #3070
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF THE TREATMENT OF ANOSOGNOSIA FOR HEMI-PLEGIA IN STROKE
AWARENESS.M.W. Kim, D.C. Kim, J. Park
The Catholic University of Korea, Seoul, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Anosognosia for hemiplegia (AHP) is a multifaceted syndrome in which stroke survivors fail to recognize motor impairments. Although AHP has significant clinical implications, rehabilitation strategies have remained fragmented and underexplored. This systematic review aimed to critically evaluate rehabilitation interventions for AHP published between 2006 and 2025, categorize intervention types, and assess clinical outcomes to inform future research and practice.
Methods: A structured search was conducted in the PubMed and PsycINFO databases on March 31, 2025, using predefined keywords related to stroke, anosognosia, and rehabilitation. The eligible studies included randomized controlled trials, case-control studies, and case studies. Following title, abstract, and full-text screening, nine studies focusing on rehabilitation interventions for AHP were selected and analyzed.
Results: The interventions reviewed included sensorimotor recalibration techniques, neuromodulatory approaches, error-based cognitive training, and self-observation in video replay strategies. Interventions emphasizing motor intention monitoring, error correction, and self-observation were more consistently associated with durable improvements in motor awareness than neglect-based spatial interventions were. However, many studies were limited by small sample sizes and a lack of standardized outcome measures. Assessment methodologies vary widely, highlighting the need for multidimensional theory-driven evaluation tools.
Conclusions: Effective rehabilitation for AHP requires strategies targeting disrupted self-monitoring and agency mechanisms, rather than spatial realignment alone. The video self-observation and error-based learning paradigms show particular promise. Future research should focus on controlled trials, longitudinal tracking, and the integration of individualized, mechanism-specific rehabilitation models to optimize outcomes for stroke survivors with AHP.

DEVELOPING AN ACRONYM FOR STROKE REHABILITATION SERVICES: A CO-DESIGN PROTOCOL
AWARENESS.R. Mascarenhas1, N. Chawala2, P.S. Akkunje3, D. Gandhi4, J. Solomon5, V. Montanaro6, G. Urimubenshi7, S. Kamalakannan8, G. Rehabilitation9
1Christian Medical College & Hospital, Neurology, Ludhiana, India, 2Manipal Accademy of Health sciences, Department Of Phydiotherapy, Manipal, India, 3KASTURBA MEDICAL COLLEGE, Department Of Audiology And Speech Language Pathology, MANGALORE, India, 4Christian Medical College & Hospital, Neurology & Physiotherapy, Ludhiana, India, 5Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Department Of Physiotherapy, Manipal, India, 6SARAH Network of Rehabilitation Hospitals, Neurology, Brasilia, Brazil, 7University of Rwanda, Physiotherapy, Kigali, Rwanda, 8Northumbria University, Department Of Social Work, Education, And Community Wellbeing, Newcastle Upon Tyne, United Kingdom, 9GLOBAL CONSORTIUM OF STROKE REHABILITATION, LUDHIANA, India
Background and Aims: Stroke rehabilitation services in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) are often impeded by a fragmented understanding of essential components. Acronyms can improve recall and stakeholder engagement. This protocol describes a co-design approach to develop an acronym that encapsulates core elements of comprehensive stroke rehabilitation
Methods: A multi-stakeholder co-design process will be employed across three phases: Evidence Synthesis and Mapping – A systematic review of the literature on stroke rehabilitation services will be conducted. Service components will be mapped against lived experience, clinical expertise, and current evidence. Survey Development and Distribution – An inductive analysis of the mapping approach will inform a structured survey. This will be distributed to stroke survivors and caregivers, who will rank service components by perceived importance and feasibility. Iterative Refinement – Guided by a modified Delphi method, potential acronym options will be generated from survey results and refined through successive feedback loops with all stakeholders until consensus is achieved.
Results: Inductive evidence synthesis will identify core rehabilitation domains, which will then be thematically grouped to form survey items. Survey responses will be analysed using a graph theory–based voting system to aggregate individual rankings into a consolidated priority list. Multiple acronym candidates will be co-created and iteratively refined through Delphi rounds. The final acronym will be selected once ⩾70% agreement indicates consensus.
Conclusions: The finalized acronym is expected to serve as a representation of comprehensive stroke rehabilitation services. By encapsulating key service components, it can enhance understanding among stakeholders, including healthcare providers and community members.
EV040 / #2337
INVESTIGATING CLOPIDOGREL RESISTANCE AMONGST RECURRENT ISCHAEMIC STROKE PATIENTS
AWARENESS.S. Mohammed, Z. Azeem, K. Musarrat, M. Moqsith
University Hospitals of Leicester, Leicester, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, with the majority caused by cerebral artery atherosclerosis. Antiplatelets remain the mainstay of treatment. Currently, patients with intracranial atherosclerosis are managed with short-term Dual Antiplatelet Therapy; Aspirin and Clopidogrel and then continued on Clopidogrel long term. An inadequate antiplatelet response is associated with increased risk of recurrent ischemic events. Emerging evidence shows that variations in the CYP2C19 gene results in reduced ability to convert Clopidogrel into its active form, leading to Clopidogrel resistance and this is especially prevalent in the south Asian population. This study aims to investigate the presence of ‘Clopidogrel failure’ amongst the cohort of patients diagnosed with a recurrent stroke.
Methods: Data was obtained from patients (N = 124) from the University Hospitals Leicester, U.K., over a 6-month period from the Sentinel Stroke National Audit Programme database and, were identified to have had a recurrent stroke whilst on Clopidogrel using the electronic patient record/electronic prescribing system. Patients on anticoagulants and those with Atrial fibrillation were excluded.
Results: Following an excel analysis of the cohort, the results demonstrate 62 patients (50%) as Clopidogrel failures.
Conclusions: This data shows that the Clopidogrel resistance rate is high, irrespective of the definition used and parameters measured. These findings highlight the clinical importance of Point-of-care testing for the CYP2C19 gene, which will enable an informed decision about antiplatelet choice. This in turn shall potentially lead to cost savings for the healthcare system.

Background and Aims: Epidemiological studies suggest that demographic, socioeconomic, and educational factors may influence time metrics in stroke care. We aimed to identify differences in stroke care depending on the neighbourhood in which the patient suffered a stroke.
Methods: Retrospective study of consecutive stroke codes during the year 2022 attended at home by regional emergency services (EMS). Each case was assigned values corresponding to the statistics of its neighbourhood published by the city council: aging (>65yo/<16yo) and overaging (>80yo/>65yo) indexes, proportion of >65yo leaving alone, average household size, average income, illiteracy rate, and vulnerability indexes (social welfare and equality, urban environment and mobility, education and culture, economy and employment, health). Conclusions: We found few significant yet weak correlations between socioeconomic level and stroke care in our setting. Neighbourhoods with higher proportion of >65yo living alone and socioeconomic vulnerability had the greatest attention delay and might benefit from specific measures for early stroke detection.
EV043 / #2046
UNMASKING TRUE STROKES HIDDEN BENEATH STROKE MIMICS: SIMULTANEOUS PRESENTATION OF SEVERE HYPOTHYROIDISM & ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE
AWARENESS.N. Sharma
All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Neurocritical Care, New Delhi, India
Background and Aims: Background: Stroke mimics account for nearly one-third of all suspected strokes, often delaying urgent intervention. Among these, metabolic disorders—especially severe hypothyroidism—pose a unique diagnostic challenge. This case explores how a presumed mimic concealed a genuine ischemic stroke, revealing the complex interplay between endocrine and cerebrovascular pathology.
Methods: Case Description Methods: An 83-year-old man with a history of hypothyroidism (post-radioablation), hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure presented with progressive left-sided weakness, dysphagia, and facial droop, five days after a fall. Neurologic examination revealed an NIHSS score of 3. Initial CT imaging showed no acute infarct. Thyroid function tests revealed severe hypothyroidism (TSH 79.22 uIU/mL, Free T4 0.25 ng/dL), raising suspicion for a stroke mimic. Further diagnostic workup included non-contrast brain MRI, transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography, and cardiac monitoring.
Results: MRI revealed a 15 mm acute infarct in the right corona radiata, confirming an ischemic stroke. Despite negative echocardiography, the patient’s age and infarct characteristics warranted the placement of an insertable loop recorder to monitor for occult atrial fibrillation. Treatment included increasing levothyroxine from 25 to 125 mcg daily, a 21-day course of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT), and long-term aspirin. The patient showed improvement in both neurological and metabolic parameters and was discharged with endocrinology and neurology follow-up.

Conclusions: Conclusion: Comprehensive evaluation—including endocrine, vascular, and cardiac assessment—is essential to avoid misdiagnosis and guide appropriate management in acute stroke presentations. Learning Points: Stroke mimics may coexist with true infarction. Hypothyroidism can obscure clinical and imaging findings. Multidisciplinary evaluation is key to accurate diagnosis.

CATCH ME IF YOU CAN- A CASE OF WANDERING PERMANENT PACEMAKER MIMICKING ACUTE NEUROVASCULAR SYNDROME

1Neurovascular Service, Medicine Of The Elderly, Dublin, Ireland, 2Neurovascular Service, Dublin, Ireland
Background and Aims: Cardiac pacemaker migration is a rare but serious complication that can lead to significant morbidity, including device dysfunction and systemic complications. Neurological symptoms associated with pacemaker migration often result from cerebral hypoperfusion caused by compromised cardiac output or lead displacement. This report highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic journey of a 93-year-old woman who presented with transient neurological symptoms due to pacemaker migration and lead dysfunction.
Methods: A 93-year-old woman with a background history of atrial fibrillation, hypertension, and complete heart block treated with permanent pacemaker (PPM) insertion presented with recurrent episodes of transient dysarthria and expressive aphasia. She was initially managed as a suspected transient ischemic attack. She admitted to some lightheadedness with the episodes. Imaging and physical examination revealed malposition of the pacemaker, which had migrated to the left breast and eroded through the pocket. The patient reported that the pacemaker frequently "moved around", which she believed was normal. The pacemaker remained functional, although its compromised positioning led to episodes of transient hypotension and inadequate cardiac output mimicking acute neurovascular syndrome.
Results: The patient underwent PPM removal, temporary pacing, and initiation of broad-spectrum antibiotics to mitigate the risk of bacterial endocarditis. After completing a course of antibiotics, a new PPM was successfully implanted in the correct position. The patient remained stable postoperatively, with no recurrence of neurological symptoms or further device-related complications.
Conclusions: This case highlights the significance of thorough evaluation for device-related complications in patients with neurological symptoms and implanted cardiac devices.

EFFICACY OF VALPROIC ACID AS A NEUROPROTECTIVE AGENT IN THE RODENT CEREBRAL ISCHEMIA-REPERFUSION MODELS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
BASIC SCIENCE.A. Imanzadeh1, A. Jamali1, F. Ahmadkhani1, S. Sadigh-Eteghad2, M. Farhoudi2, R. Beheshti1
1Tabriz University of Medical science, Student Research Committee, Tabriz, Iran, 2Tabriz University of Medical science, Neuroscience Research Center, Tabriz, Iran
Background and Aims: Emerging in vivo literature suggest that valproic acid (VPA) has neuroprotective properties.We aimed to give a comprehensive review of the efficacy and safety of VPA in the rodent cerebral ischemia-reperfusion model studies.
Methods: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase databases up to March 2025. We included in vivo studies that evaluated the efficacy of VPA using either the transient Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion (tMCAO) or Common Carotid Artery Occlusion models. Risk of bias in the included studies was independently assessed by two authors using the CAMARADES checklist. Data on infarct volume and neurological function from studies employing the tMCAO ischemia-reperfusion model were pooled for meta-analysis and reported as standardized mean differences ± SEM.
Results: VPA administration significantly reduced infarct volume in both Sprague-Dawley rats and mice compared to vehicle controls, with standardized mean differences of 2.63 ± 1.07 (CI: -4.71 to -0.54; p = 0.01; data measured in mm3 in Sprague-Dawley rats) and 3.72 ± 1.1 (CI: -5.87 to -1.57; p < 0.01; data measured by percentage of reduction in infarction volume in mice), respectively. In rats, VPA also improved neurological function, as shown by the enhanced Rotarod test (1.76 ± 0.33; CI: 1.12 to 2.39; p < 0.01; data measured in seconds); however, no significant improvement was observed in distance traveled (0.31 ± 0.33; CI: -0.33 to 0.96; p = 0.34; data measured in centimeters).
Conclusions: These findings indicate the potential strategies for employing Valproic acid to cure cerebral ischemic injury along with reperfusion therapy.

BASIC SCIENCE.J. García-Aranda1,2,3, P. Camps-Renom4, N. Puig4, B. Pérez1,2,3, C. Rodríguez2,5, J. Martínez2,5,6, S. Benitez7,8, F. Jiménez-Altayó1,2,3
1Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, Institute Of Neurosciences, Barcelona, Spain, 2Centro de Investigación Biomédica en Red de Enfermedades Cardiovasculares (CIBERCV), Instituto de Salud Carlos III, Madrid, Spain, 3Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, Department Of Pharmacology, Therapeutics, And Toxicology, Barcelona, Spain, 4Hospital de La Santa Creu i Sant Pau, Stroke Unit, Neurology Department, Barcelona, Spain, 5Institut de Recerca Sant Pau, Barcelona, Spain, 6Instituto de Investigaciones Biomédicas de Barcelona- Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (IIBB-CSIC), Barcelona, Spain, 7Institut De Recerca Sant Pau, Biochemistry, Barcelona, Spain, 8CIBER of Diabetes and Related Metabolic Diseases (CIBERDEM), Instituto de Salud Carlos III, Madrid, Spain
Background and Aims: Carotid atherosclerosis (CA) is the main cause of atherothrombotic stroke. We aimed to compare the inflammatory, oxidative, and lipid profile in serum from asymptomatic and recently symptomatic patients with CA. The serum-induced endothelial dysfunction in mice carotid arteries and the mechanisms involved were addressed.
Methods: Prospective study of consecutive patients with CA⩾50% who underwent endarterectomy in our center (2021-2024). Patients were divided into asymptomatic (CA-As, n=30) and symptomatic (CA-S, n=67) for ischemic stroke. Serum inflammatory markers (IL1ß, IL6, IL8, SAA, CRP, sICAM-1, sVCAM-1), lipid profile, apolipoproteins, Lp(a), and oxidized LDL were quantified by ELISA and autoanalyzer. Serum oxidative parameters (superoxide anion, nitric oxide, antioxidant capacity) were measured by HPLC and colorimetric determinations. Vascular function was evaluated using wire myography in carotid arteries isolated from male C57BL/6 mice (2-4 months old, n=35) following incubation with serum. Vasodilatory responses to acetylcholine (ACh) and the nitric oxide donor sodium nitroprusside (NP) were assessed.
Results: CA-S patients showed higher serum levels of IL-6 (p=0.017) and CRP (p=0.023), as well as lower concentrations of HDL-C (p=0.017) and apoA-I (p<0.001) compared to CA-As patients, with no significant differences in oxidative stress parameters. Incubation of mouse carotid arteries with serum from CA patients induced endothelial dysfunction similarly in symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals, since ACh-induced relaxations were impaired, whereas in the presence of NP remained unaffected.
Conclusions: Serum from CA-S and CA-As patients promotes endothelial dysfunction in carotid arteries. This effect is comparable between groups, despite the higher levels of inflammatory markers and lower content of HDL observed in CA-S serum.
EV048 / #2360
SENEGENIN MITIGATES CEREBRAL ISCHEMIA-REPERFUSION INJURY BY INHIBITING CGAS-STING-DRIVEN NEUROINFLAMMATION AND CELL DEATH PATHWAYS
BASIC SCIENCE.C. Chauhan, R. Kaundal
National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER-Raebareli), Pharmacology And Toxicology, Lucknow, India
Background and Aims: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and long-term disability, with limited effective treatments. Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury induces oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and programmed cell death, exacerbating neuronal damage. The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is increasingly recognized as a central regulator of microglial activation and inflammation after stroke. However, pharmacological modulators of this pathway remain scarce. This study explores the neuroprotective effects of senegenin, a bioactive compound from Polygala tenuifolia, focusing on its impact on cGAS-STING signaling and associated pathological processes.
Methods: In vivo, rats underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) for 2 hours followed by reperfusion, and were treated intravenously with senegenin (1, 3, or 10 mg/kg). Neurological function, infarct volume, brain edema, and neuronal survival were assessed. In vitro, LPS-stimulated N9 microglial cells modeled post-ischemic inflammation. Oxidative stress, neuroinflammatory markers, cGAS-STING activation, pyroptosis, and apoptosis were evaluated using Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and ELISA.
Results: Senegenin improved neurological outcomes, reduced infarct size and edema, and preserved neuronal integrity. It restored redox balance by increasing GSH and SOD while decreasing MDA and nitrite levels. Senegenin inhibited DNA damage, microglial activation, and cGAS-STING pathway activation, suppressing TNF-α, IL-6, COX2, and iNOS expression. It also downregulated the NF-κB/NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD axis and reduced apoptosis, evidenced by increased Bcl-2, decreased Bax, and fewer TUNEL-positive cells.
Conclusions: Senegenin confers neuroprotection in ischemic stroke by targeting oxidative stress, cGAS-STING–mediated neuroinflammation, pyroptosis, and apoptosis, suggesting therapeutic potential for stroke intervention.

Background and Aims: Despite growing evidence of the role of genetic factors in ischemic stroke (IS), Latin American populations—particularly the genetically diverse and highly admixed Brazilian population—remain critically underrepresented in global genomic consortia. This underrepresentation restricts the generalizability of findings from large-scale studies such as MEGASTROKE and GIGASTROKE and limits the implementation of precision medicine in the region. The ÁRTEMIS-BRAZIL study aims to address this gap by assessing the prevalence and clinical relevance of known stroke-associated polymorphisms in Brazilians, characterizing regional genomic and ancestry patterns, and investigating pharmacogenomic and retinal microvascular markers for stroke risk stratification, prevention, and prognosis.

BASIC SCIENCE.T. Rackoll, A. Bannach-Brown, S. Vojvodic, M. Karmakar, S. Mccann
Berlin Institute of Health at Charite, Berlin, Germany
Background and Aims: Despite increasing efforts to promote open data practices, data sharing in biomedical research remains limited. When data are shared, they are often difficult to find, access, or reuse—especially in evidence synthesis, where locating relevant data is often time-consuming and incomplete. Furthermore, the non-publication of null or negative results introduces bias and contributes to research waste. This project aims to develop ODC-Stroke, a cloud-based, community-driven platform tailored to preclinical ischaemic stroke research. It supports FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and facilitates more effective data sharing and synthesis.
Methods: We propose ODC-Stroke as a secure platform with flexible access controls for uploading, sharing, and publishing data. Researchers can manage data visibility and assign DOIs to published datasets for citation and reuse. The platform supports both single-lab and multi-site collaborations and is designed to incorporate unpublished data into systematic reviews. Development is conducted in collaboration with the stroke research community to define common data elements (CDEs) and integrate data sharing with evidence synthesis workflows.
Results: ODC-Stroke enables improved data discoverability, standardization, and reuse. By supporting the inclusion of unpublished data and promoting the use of CDEs, it reduces publication bias and enhances the quality and comprehensiveness of systematic reviews. The platform will foster reproducibility and collaboration across research groups.
Conclusions: ODC-Stroke will be a robust resource for preclinical stroke research, promoting open science and improving data integrity. By enabling FAIR data practices, it enhances evidence synthesis and contributes to more reliable, transparent, and impactful stroke research.

Results: The Kruskal-Wallis test revealed a significant difference in D-Dimer levels between the etiological groups(p = 0.007),with significantly higher values in the CE group compared to the other groups.Regression analysis showed no correlation between D-Dimer levels and age,suggesting that the biomarker is primarily influenced by etiology rather than patient age.In contrast,no significant differences were observed in Fibrinogen levels (p = 0.116).
Conclusions: The results suggest that D-Dimer could serve as a useful biomarker for distinguishing between cardioembolic stroke and other etiologies,with potential diagnostic value in ischemic stroke.However,given the presence of confounding factors,further studies in a larger population and real-world clinical settings are necessary to validate these biomarkers.

Background and Aims: Elevated homocysteine levels are associated with an increased risk of stroke. Low vitamin B12 (cobalamin) levels can lead to increased homocysteine levels. Methods: From the Clotbase International Registry, 100 blood clot samples from patients with AIS were studied. Components were measured using Orbit Image Analysis software, and statistical analysis was performed, with results reported as median values (%) and interquartile ranges.

There was a strong trend of higher SAHH expression in patients with atrial fibrillation (n=37, 16.2%[8.3–25.6]) compared to those without AF (n=62, 10.2% [3.9–18.8]), (U=915,p=0.07). CBWD2 expression was significantly higher in clots that were removed in 1 pass (n=67, 51.3%[28.5–65.2]) compared to >1 pass (n=33, 36%[17.3-55]), (U=765,p=0.01). The First Pass Effect (FPE) group showed a significantly higher expression of CBWD2 (n=62, 50.7%[24.2–65.2]), compared to the non-FPE group (n=38, 36.1%[17.5–57.3]), (U=879,p=0.03). No significant correlation between CBWD2 and homocysteine levels in AIS clots was found.
Conclusions: Higher SAHH levels were observed in female and AF populations, and elevated CBWD2 expression was associated with better stroke outcomes. Further investigation of the link between CBWD2 and potentially vitamin B12, and patient outcome could be beneficial. Acknowledgements:CÚRAM:Research Ireland:13/RC/2073 P2,SENSOME

DERIVING A SIMPLE CLINICAL PREDICTIVE SCORE FOR POSTERIOR CIRCULATION ISCHEMIC STROKE
BIOMARKERS.Y. Imam1, R. Singh2, P. Chandra2, I. Hakeem2, Z. Bhutta2, D. Deleu2
1Weil Cornell Medicne, Neurology, Doha, Qatar, 2Hamad medical Corporation, Doha, Qatar
Background and Aims: Background: Posterior circulation ischemic stroke (PCS) is frequently under-recognized due to its atypical presentations and lower visibility in standard stroke scales. We aimed to develop a weighted clinical scoring system (PCS-SCORE) that reliably identifies patients at high risk of PCS based on bedside findings.
Methods: We analyzed 5163 patients (1571 with PCS) from a prospectively maintained stroke registry. Multivariable logistic regression and lasso modeling identified key predictors, which were weighted based on effect size and clinical relevance. The final score (0–9 points) includes diabetes (1), hypertension (1), male sex (1), double/blurred vision (2), vertigo with vomiting (2), and incoordination (2).
Results: At a cutoff >3, the PCS-SCORE achieved 87.9% specificity and 43.4% sensitivity (AUC 0.76). A higher threshold of >4 further improved specificity to 94.4% (sensitivity 27.9%). This strong rule-in capacity enables confident identification of high-risk PCS cases while reducing unnecessary imaging in low-probability scenarios.
Conclusions: Conclusion: The PCS-SCORE is a practical and specific tool for early detection of PCS,While the sensitivity of the score is modest at higher thresholds, its specificity exceeds 94%, making it an effective tool to confidently identify true cases of posterior circulation stroke. In clinical environments where diagnostic certainty is prioritized over screening breadth — such as prehospital triage, rural centers, or overwhelmed EDs — this rule-in capability ensures that high-risk patients are fast-tracked for imaging and intervention. Prospective validation is underway.

EV070 / #618
LDL/HDL RATIO AND POST-RECURRENT STROKE DISABILITY: INSIGHTS FROM A MEXICAN COHORT
BIOMARKERS.V. Lopez Diaz, C. Diaz Garza, I. Armendariz Betancourt, P. Delgado Garzón
Tecnologico de Monterrey, School of Medicine and Health Sciences, Neurology, Monterrey, Mexico
Background and Aims: The LDL-C/HDL-C ratio refers to the relationship between low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C). This ratio has been established as a predictor of stroke and is considered a novel indicator of atherosclerotic cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease risk, as it simultaneously accounts for the levels of both cholesterol types.
Methods: A retrospective cohort study included 40 patients with recurrent cerebral infarction (November 2023–February 2025). Data collected included demographics, Rankin scores after each infarction, lipid profiles, and medical histories. Patients were divided into two groups based on their LDL-C/HDL-C ratio: Group 1 (<3.4) and Group 2 (>3.5). Statistical analysis assessed the association between the ratio and functional outcome at discharge.
Results: The cohort (60% male, mean age 64) had a high prevalence of hypertension (77%), with frequent comorbidities such as type 2 diabetes (42%), alcoholism (35%), and substance abuse (7%). At discharge, 39.5% had a Rankin ⩽2 and 60.5% ⩾3. A significant positive correlation was found between the LDL/HDL ratio and Rankin scores (Spearman’s Rho = 0.4, p = 0.02). Univariable linear regression confirmed this association, and ROC analysis identified a cutoff of 1.9 (AUC = 0.78), with 100% sensitivity and 53% specificity.

Conclusions: A higher LDL/HDL ratio was linked to greater disability post-recurrent infarction, although it accounted for only 18% outcome variability. Notably, a ratio of 1.9 was associated with poor prognosis in this Mexican cohort, lower than thresholds reported in other populations. Including the LDL/HDL ratio in future predictive models may enhance risk stratification and support more personalized clinical strategies.

Methods: A prospective registry of IS patients attended in our Stroke Unit from 01/08/2022-30/08/2023 was analyzed. Patients without previous AF and absence of atherothrombotic or other determined causes were included. IGFBP2 was measured by ELISA in serum samples collected within 24h after IS. Logistic regression and ROC curve analysis were performed.

Including IGFBP2 as a predictor improved the discriminatory power of validated AF prediction scales (Figure 3: integrated discrimination index: +9.8% for STAF score, +10.2% for AF-ESUS score).

Conclusions: Circulating IGFBP2 emerges as a promising biomarker of AF in IS patients, comparable to NT-proBNP, improving AF prediction when incorporated into validated scoring scales.

Background and Aims: This study aims to investigate the relationship between stress hyperglycemia and prognosis in ischemic stroke patients.
Methods: A total of 1047 patients admitted with acute ischemic stroke between August 2017 and December 2022 were included in this study. Demographic data, risk factors, admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) scores, early neurological deterioration, mortality, follow-up modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores were retrospectively analyzed. Patients with active infection on admission were excluded. Stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) was calculated by dividing the fasting plasma glucose on admission by the glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level (mmol/L/%). ROC analysis identified a SHR of 1.05 as best cutoff value to discriminate favorable and unfavorable functional outcomes. According to SHR, patients were divided into 2 groups (group 1; SHR <1.05, group 2; SHR ⩾1.05).
Results: There were 704 patients (67%) who met the inclusion criteria, and 404 patients (57.3%, mean age 69.71 ± 13.16, female; 184, 45.5 %) had SHR⩾1.05. Admission NIHSS>4, early neurological deterioration, mortality and follow-up mRS>3 were higher in group 2. In logistic regression analysis, active smoking and worse outcome (follow-up mRS score>3) were associated with higher SHR.
Conclusions: These results support the association of stress hyperglycemia with unfavorable functional outcome in patients with acute ischemic stroke, which is consistent with previous studies suggesting that stress hyperglycemia is a predictor of stroke prognosis.

Background and Aims: CYP2C19 Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (SNPs) may affect Clopidogrel metabolism from its pro-drug to active metabolite. Few studies concurrently assessed the influence of pharmacogenetics factors on HTPR status and clinical outcomes in ischaemic cerebrovascular disease (CVD) patients, with no prevalence data on CYP2C19 LOF SNPs in CVD patients in Ireland.
Methods: 103 patients ⩽ 4 weeks of TIA/ischaemic stroke on Aspirin (N=22) or Clopidogrel (N=29) monotherapy, or Aspirin+Clopidogrel (N=48) / Aspirin+Dipyridamole (N=4) therapy were recruited to the prospective Optimal Antiplatelet Therapy in TIA and Ischaemic Stroke-International pilot observational study. Clopidogrel-treated patients (Clopidogrel monotherapy or Aspirin+Clopidogrel) were categorised into subgroups with/without Clopidogrel-HTPR on ‘high shear-stress’ (PFA-100® INNOVANCE PFA P2Y), and ‘low shear-stress’ (VerifyNow® PRUTest and PL-12/AGGRESTAR® ADP) assays.
Results: 94 patients have undergone pharmacogenetics analysis to date: 29% (N=27) were Intermediate-Poor, 37% (N=35) Normal and 34% (N=32) Rapid-Ultrarapid Metabolisers. Despite being classified as predicted Intermediate-Poor Metabolisers, 7/21 (33%) Clopidogrel-treated patients did not have Clopidogrel-HTPR on the ‘CE-approved’ PFA-100 or VerifyNow assays, and 3/21 (14%) did not exhibit Clopidogrel-HTPR on any of the 3 platforms.
Conclusions: Almost 1/3 of our CVD study population in Ireland have CYP2C19 LOF SNPs. Further studies should combine pharmacogenetics and HTPR-status to guide antiplatelet therapy because up to 33% of CVD patients predicted to be Intermediate-Poor Metabolisers have adequate P2Y12-inhibition on Clopidogrel.

Background and Aims: Platelets are central to acute ischemic stroke (AIS) pathophysiology. CXCL4 release marks early platelet activation. We previously reported elevated CXCL4 in arterial blood from the ischemic territory during endovascular thrombectomy. Here, we assessed whether venous CXCL4 concentrations could serve as a prognostic biomarker in AIS.
Methods: In a prospective, monocentric, observational study, 128 patients with moderate to severe AIS (NIHSS ⩾ 6 and/or indication for mechanical recanalization) were enrolled. Venous blood was collected within 24 h of symptom onset to measure CXCL4 plasma concentrations (ELISA) and thrombocyte counts. Functional outcome was assessed by telephone interview using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at 3 months (±14 days); poor outcome was defined as mRS ⩾ 3. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, ASPECTS on admission, NIHSS on admission, and recanalization therapy.

CXCL4 levels did not differ significantly between poor and good outcome groups (113.5 ng/ml [IQR 67.7–160.6] vs. 114.5 ng/ml [IQR 85.6–146.1]; p=0.87) or between survivors and non-survivors (113.8 ng/ml [IQR 66.2–185.0] vs. 113.5 ng/ml [IQR 74.6–147.9]; p=0.86). Conclusions: Venous CXCL4 levels are not associated with poor outcome or mortality in AIS, raising questions about whether thrombo-inflammatory processes in cerebral arteries are adequately reflected in systemic circulation.

APOLIPOPROTEIN DISCORDANCE BETTER REFLECTS INTRACRANIAL ATHEROSCLEROSIS THAN TRADITIONAL LIPID BIOMARKERS
BIOMARKERS.D. Kook1, T. Ok2, K. Seo3
1Gangnam Severance Hospital, Yonsei University College of Medicine, Neurology, Seoul, Korea, Republic of, 2National Health Insurance Service Ilsan Hospital, Neurology, Goyang, Korea, Republic of, 3Gangnam Severance Hospital, Radiology, Seoul, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Apolipoprotein B (ApoB) better reflects atherogenic particle number than LDL-C, and apolipoprotein A1 (ApoA1) more accurately represents HDL-C function. We evaluated whether discordance between apolipoproteins and traditional lipid markers is linked to greater intracranial atherosclerosis.
Methods: A total of 2,894 patients were classified into a discordance group (n = 388) and a control group, based on the median values of LDL-C, HDL-C, ApoB, and ApoA1. The discordance group included patients with low LDL-C but high ApoB and/or high HDL-C but low ApoA1. Atherosclerosis severity was assessed using the number of stenotic intracranial arteries and the degree of stenosis. Covariates included age, sex, body mass index, alcohol, smoking, hypertension, and diabetes. Statistical comparisons and ordinal logistic regression were performed.
Results: The discordance group had lower levels of ApoA1 (median 1.20 [1.11–1.26] g/L vs. 1.32 [1.12–1.49] g/L) and higher levels of ApoB (1.00 [0.93–1.12] g/L vs. 0.94 [0.77–1.16] g/L). While HDL-C was higher in the discordance group (1.19 [0.96–1.27] mmol/L vs. 1.14 [0.96–1.42] mmol/L), LDL-C was lower (2.61 [2.30–2.93] mmol/L vs. 2.85 [2.20–3.44] mmol/L). The number of stenotic intracranial vessels was significantly higher in the discordance group (p=0.0459). Based on stenosis severity, the discordance group had 26.8% with no stenosis, 43.0% with mild stenosis, and 30.2% with severe stenosis, compared to 35.8%, 35.5%, and 28.7% in the control group, respectively (p=0.013).
Conclusions: Apolipoproteins reflect the atherosclerosis severity more accurately than traditional lipid markers. These findings support the clinical utility of apolipoprotein measurement and its potential role as a therapeutic target in at-risk patients.

BIOFLUID EXTRACELLULAR VESICLE PROTEOMICS: A NOVEL NON-INVASIVE APPROACH TO CAD DETECTION
BIOMARKERS.P. Sharma1, K. Inampudi2, A. Roy2, R. Dhamija1
1Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences, Neurology, Delhi, India, 2All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Delhi, India
Background and Aims: Aim: To identify early biomarkers of plasma, saliva, and urine exosome proteins associated with coronary artery disease (CAD). Background: Biofluid exosomes, or small extracellular vesicles (sEVs), are a promising source of biomarkers for CAD, a chronic inflammatory condition that often remains asymptomatic until it results in angina, myocardial infarction, or death.
Methods: The sEVs were isolated from the plasma, saliva, and urine of 22 CAD patients aged 18-65, along with matched healthy controls, using differential ultracentrifugation. Characterization techniques included nanoparticle tracking analysis, Western blotting (exosome markers of Flotilin-1, TSG-101, CD63, and CD9), and transmission electron microscopy. Mass spectrometry was employed to identify differentially expressed proteins. Identified protein interaction networks were analyzed using STRING and Cytoscape, followed by gene enrichment analysis. A subset of proteins was validated via ELISA in larger sample sizes.
Results: We identified 2,976, 506, and 508 proteins using MS, with 115, 19, and 22 proteins showing differential expression in sEVs from plasma, saliva, and urine, respectively. We focused on proteins with a significant fold difference of ⩾ 2, a peptide match of ⩾ 2, and a p-value of < 0.05 in CAD. Notable differences were found in Apolipoprotein AI, AII, APOB, and APOC I/II. We identified both common and unique differentially expressed proteins, which were involved in regulating biological processes, metabolic processes, cell communication, cellular component movement, defense response, and transport.
Conclusions: Cystatin S was significantly expressed in saliva sEVs, while decreased levels of uromodulin in urine sEVs were validated in CAD patients.
EV078 / #2152
ADVANCES IN METABOLOMICS OF BIOMARKERS FOR ISCHEMIC STROKE: FROM BENCH TO CLINIC
BIOMARKERS.J. Sun1, C. Xiao2, J. Zhang1, F. Lin1, Y. Li1, L. Zhang1, W. Chen3
1The Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University, Department Of cerebrovascular Disease, Zhuhai, China, 2Macau University of Science and Technology, School Of Pharmacy, Macau, China, 3The Fifth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University, Department Of Pharmacy, Zhuhai, China
Background and Aims: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a neurological impairment caused by cerebral vascular occlusion, which accounts for 87% of stroke. Recent studies have shown that changes in the abundance of metabolites can directly reveal the cellular phenotypes and identify their clinical implications of stroke diagnosis and therapy. This study aimed to systematically identify the relationship between biomarkers and mechanisms of IS.
Methods: We reviewed articles on IS metabolites from 2005 to 2024, extracted metabolites with significant changes, and constructed a metabolite database based on 128 literatures, including 125 differential metabolites detected in MCAO mouse model, 246 in MCAO rat model, and 764 in IS patient samples. Differential metabolites from various samples were then screened and classified into positive and negative categories based on their correlation with stroke prognosis.
Results: 3 positive metabolites and 2 negative metabolites were identified. Glutamic acid, glycerol and 1-octadecanoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (LysoPC(18:0)) were further recognized as potential biomarkers. Imbalances in metabolic pathways such as alanine, asparate and glutamate metabolism as well as citrate cycle (TCA cycle) were analyzed. These imbalances may impact the pathogenesis of IS by altering biological processes including excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, inflammation, and energy metabolism.
Conclusions: This cross-species analysis reveals reproducible biomarkers and metabolic pathways in IS, providing valuable targets and strategies for prediction, diagnosis, and prognostic assessment.

EV079 / #172
SOLUBLE P-SELECTIN, AN EARLY DIAGNOSTIC MARKER FOR POSTPARTUM CEREBRAL VENOUS THROMBOSIS
BIOMARKERS.K.-V. T P1, G.B. Kulkarni2, P. Mailankody2, S. Nashi2, S. C3, M. Philip4, S.S. K5
1National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Department Of Neurochemistry, Bengaluru, India, 2National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Department Of Neurology, Bengaluru, India, 3Vani Vilas Hospital, Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute, Department Of Obstetrics & Gynecology, Bengaluru, India, 4National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Department Of Biostatistics, Bengaluru, India, 5National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Department Of Transfusion Medicine & Haematology, Bengaluru, India
Background and Aims: Thrombosis of veins and sinuses in the brain during the postpartum period is called postpartum cerebral venous thrombosis (PCVT). It contributes significantly to maternal morbidity. PCVT is 10-12 times more frequent in India than in the West. The absence of specific signs and symptoms in PCVT has delayed diagnosis and led to poor patient outcomes. The etiology of PCVT is unclear. There are no recognizable diagnostic biomarkers for this disease. The study aims to investigate soluble P-selectin (sP-sel) as a non-invasive early diagnostic marker for PCVT.
Methods: 20/50(40%) confirmed PCVT patients were recruited from Emergency and Casualty of NIMHANS. 50/100(50%) age- and postpartum-matched women without PCVT were recruited from Vani Vilas Hospital as controls. After obtaining informed consent, 2 ml of EDTA blood was collected from study subjects and centrifuged to obtain platelet-poor plasma. The plasma sP-sel levels were measured using commercially available human sP-sel ELISA kits.
Results: The sP-sel levels were measured in 20/50(40%) PCVT patients and 25/50(50%) controls. The PCVT patients showed significantly high plasma sP-sel levels compared to postpartum controls (102±48ng/l vs 50.4±15.2ng/l; p < 0.0001; 95%CI=72.6-30.6). The diagnostic performance of sP-sel assessed by the area under the ROC score was found to be 0.88 (95% CI 0.77–0.99; cut-off = 77.5 ng/l). The plasma sP-Sel level had 95% specificity (PPV-0.45) and 77% sensitivity (NPV-0.99) to predict the risk for PCVT.
Conclusions: Elevated sP-sel in plasma showed high levels of diagnostic performance and can be a biomarker for early diagnostics of PCVT. We acknowledge ICMR, India, for funding this project.

IMPLEMENTATION OF CARDIAC CT ANGIOGRAPHY IN ACUTE STROKE IMAGING: A SURVEY OF CANADIAN STROKE PHYSICIANS, CARDIAC RADIOLOGISTS ON CURRENT PRESPECTIVES AND FEASABILITY
CARDIOEMBOLISM.J. Deo, I. Aljabri, H. Al Hasni, D. Dabreo, G. Dhillon, A. Al Subhi, J.G. Boyd, S. Jalini
Queen’s University, Kingston, Canada
Background and Aims: There is growing interest for using cardiac CT angiography (cCTA) during stroke imaging for detection of cardiac emboli, with promising early results. However, studies are limited to single centres. We aimed to conduct a cross-disciplinary survey of Canadian stroke physicians, cardiac and neuro-radiologists to determine the practicality and barriers of implementation of this imaging modality nationwide.
Methods: Online subspeciality-specific surveys were designed and distributed to professional members of the Canadian Stroke Consortium, as well as academic radiology departments in Canada. Questions focused on local practices, potential barriers, and interest in further research.
Results: 141 participants have been recruited (73 neurologists, 33 cardiac and 35 neuro-radiologists). Amongst neurologists, 70% felt that cCTA is useful for identifying cardiac thrombi and 89% are willing to participate in further research. However, only 33% felt this could be done successfully, with reporting of cCTA being the most common preceived barrier. Interestingly, 76% of cardiac radiologists were willing to participate in further studies with concerns about 24h/7days call as the most common barrier (45%). Amongst neuroradiologists, 80% are willing to participate but 12% worry about cCTA limiting accuracy for neurodiagnostication.
Conclusions: Most neurologists, cardiac and neuro-radiologists are willing to participate in further studies on cCTA, with notable subspecilaty differences with regards to perceived implementation feasibility. Surprisingly, neurologists are the ones who believe this is least feasible due to the perception that radiologist won’t participate. Hyperacute cardiac reporting is the most common barrier according to all specialities. Removing the need for immediate reporting of cardiac imaging may improve widespread implementation feasibility.

CARDIOEMBOLISM.P. Fiori1,2, G. Capaldo3, A. Silvestri3, F. Botticella4, G. Manganelli4, V. Pellecchia4, F. Volpe5, A. Bellizzi6, G. Esposito7, A. Monaco3
1v. Maddalena, Neurology, Ariano irpino (AV), Italy, 2S. Ottone Frangipane Hospital, ASL Avellino, University of Campania "Luigi Vanvitelli", Neurology, Ariano irpino (AV), Italy, 3S.
