Ottone Frangipane Hospital, Laboratory, Ariano irpino (AV), Italy
Background and Aims: Cardiovascular reactivity (CR) was defined by beat indices, ratio or difference between heart rate and pulse rate. A value <1 or >1 were considered as negative (NCR) or positive CR (PCR), respectively [Fiori P., et al, 2020]. The aim of the current study was to examine CR, hematological, hemodynamic and radiological patterns in Acute Ischaemic Syndrome (AIS).
Methods: We recruited 75 AIS, 53 PCR AIS, 22 NCR AIS. Beyond ischaemic core, lesional load was calculated according to Fazekas’ criteria. Moreover, we considered juxtacortical ischaemic lesions and microbleeds, evaluated as rare (1:1-3), sporadic (2:3-6), multiple (3:>6) at FLAIR-T2 and SWI-Weighted-MRI sequences.

However, PCR =>1,5 had the same rate of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation compared to NCR, while NCR had the highest rate of conduction blocks compared to the other patients. Correlations were present among RMN findings and MBP and Albuminuria in NCR patients.
Conclusions: Autonomic Nervous System function reflects individual vulnerability to environmental perturbations and capacity to cope with stressors. Our previous study suggested a central genesis of dysrhythmia. NCR is a negative predictive parameter in AIS. The correlations with MBP and albuminuria stand for an allostatic load, leading to homeostatic imbalance, followed by a cascade of multiple negative events, triggering irreversible, ischaemic damage.

ENDOVASCULAR THERAPY VERSUS MEDICAL MANAGEMENT IN PATIENTS WITH ISOLATED INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY OCCLUSION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
CARDIOEMBOLISM.J. Franco1, M.L.D.B. Maximiano2, O. Gonçalves3, L. Falcão4, F. Ribeiro5, P. Magalhães6, A. Silva7, H. Filho8, A. Neto9, N. Bezerra10
1Pontifical University of Paraná, Faculty Of Medicine, Curitiba, Brazil, 2Federal Fluminense University, Department Of Medicine, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 3Universidade Federal do Piauí, Teresina, Brazil, 4Bahiana School of Medicine, Salvador, Brazil, 5Barão de Mauá University Center, Ribeirão Preto, Brazil, 6Institute of Medical Education, Ribeirão Preto, Brazil, 7University of Pernambuco, Pernambuco, Brazil, 8University of Fortaleza, Fortaleza, Brazil, 9University Estadual do Centro Oeste, Guarapuava, Brazil, 10University Center of Maranhão, São Luís, Brazil
Background and Aims: The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in patients with isolated internal carotid artery occlusion (IICAO) remains uncertain, as this subgroup has been excluded or underrepresented in major randomized trials. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate whether EVT offers superior outcomes compared to medical management (MM) in patients with IICAO.
Methods: A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through January 2025, following PRISMA guidelines. Studies comparing EVT versus MM in patients with IICAO were included. Outcomes analyzed included 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0–2), excellent outcome (mRS 0–1), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), 90-day mortality, and early neurological improvement (ENI). Pooled risk ratios (RR) were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed using the I² statistic.
Results: Five studies including 819 patients (401 EVT, 418 MM) were analyzed. EVT did not significantly improve functional independence (RR 1.09; 95% CI 0.94–1.26; I² = 0%), excellent outcome (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.70–1.35), or 90-day mortality (RR 1.03; 95% CI 0.73–1.45). However, EVT was associated with higher rates of ENI (RR 1.64; 95% CI 1.25–2.14; I² = 0%) without a significant increase in sICH (RR 1.62; 95% CI 0.65–4.03).
Conclusions: In patients with IICAO, EVT was associated with early neurological improvement, though no differences were observed in long-term outcomes or safety. These findings may inform future trial design and support the need for further investigation in this underexplored subgroup.

MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM REVIEW AND PREDICTIVE MODELLING TO IMPROVE DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY IN CRYPTOGENIC STROKE
CARDIOEMBOLISM.N. Gyimah-Kessie1, K. Chatterjee2, S. Flynn3, E. Mason-Whitehead3
1Glan Clwyd Hospital, UJ, United Kingdom, 2Countess of Chester Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, Stroke And Elderly Medicine, Chester, United Kingdom, 3University of Chester, Chester Medical School, BJ, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Cryptogenic stroke (CS), defined as ischaemic stroke with no determined aetiology after standard investigation, presents challenges in guiding secondary prevention. This project aimed to assess whether multidisciplinary team (MDT) review could reduce CS diagnoses by identifying missed or misclassified aetiologies.
Methods: This retrospective cohort study utilised data collected from DECRYPT MDT meetings conducted at the Countess of Chester Hospital, UK, both pre- and post-pandemic, from 2019 to 2021. Patients initially diagnosed with CS underwent case review by a multidisciplinary panel comprising stroke physicians, neurologists, cardiologists, neuroradiologists, and acute care consultants. Investigations assessed included brain imaging, ECG, echocardiography, and vascular imaging. Logistic regression modelling was used to predict cardioembolic stroke based on clinical and radiological features. All patients were followed for a minimum of three years to evaluate outcomes including recurrence and mortality.

Results: Among 124 cases reviewed, true CS was confirmed in only 25% after MDT evaluation. Cardioembolism was the most common identified cause (24%), followed by large artery atherosclerosis (17%) and other defined aetiologies (20%). The predictive model achieved 83% sensitivity and 83% specificity for identifying cardioembolic stroke (Fig 1), with an area under the ROC curve of 0.88. Stroke recurrence was highest in CS patients (42%), while cardioembolic cases had the highest mortality (38%) despite no recurrence.
Conclusions: MDT review significantly improved diagnostic accuracy, enabling reclassification of stroke aetiology and supporting better-informed treatment decisions. Predictive modelling offers clinical utility in identifying cardioembolic stroke, though further validation in larger, diverse cohorts is required.

SEQUENTIAL BILATERAL MIDDLE CEREBRAL ARTERY OCCLUSIONS IN CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE
CARDIOEMBOLISM.L. Kaoutzani1, W. Woodall1, M. Shah2, K. Garcia2, A. Bruno2, S. Rahimi1
1Wellstar Medical College of Georgia Health, Neurosurgery, Augusta, United States of America, 2Wellstar Medical College of Georgia Health, Neurology, Augusta, United States of America
Background and Aims: Stroke remains the second leading cause of death with ischemic stroke being the most common type. Risk factors for ischemic stroke include but are not limited to age, sex, race, hypertension, atrial fibrillation, smoking, diet and physical inactivity. Congestive heart failure (CHF) increases the risk for intracardiac thrombus formation and cardioembolic stroke. For large vessel occlusion stroke, intravenous thrombolytics and mechanical thrombectomy are the standards of care. We present a patient with successful recanalization of sequential bilateral middle cerebral artery (MCA) occlusions
Methods: A 55 year old male was hospitalized for CHF exacerbation and developed sudden right sided weakness and aphasia. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed left MCA occlusion in the M1 segment.
Results: He underwent diagnostic cerebral angiogram and mechanical thrombectomy. At the end of the procedure there was recanalization of the left MCA occlusion with TICI-2b flow. Within two hours following the thrombectomy he was noted to dvelop right MCA territory deficits. Repeat CTA showed right MCA occlusion in the M1 segment. He underwent a second diagnostic cerebral angiogram and mechanical thrombectomy. At the end of the procedure there was recanalization of the right MCA occlusion with TICI-3 flow. Transthoracic echocardiogram revealed a left ventricular thrombus and left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 15%.
Conclusions: Ischemic stroke remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Patients with CHF who experience ischemic stroke have worse outcomes. This case report documents a rare event of a patient with CHF experiencing sequential bilateral strokes within four hours of each other.

Background and Aims: Ischaemic strokes (IS) resulting from cardiac tumours offers significant potential for research into the pathogenesis, diagnosis, therapy and outcomes of the disease. Patient T., aged 50, presented to the hospital with complaints of numbness on the left side of the trunk. The patient’s condition deteriorated the day before admission when numbness was suddenly noticed. However, the symptoms partially regressed during the day. The following day, the patient noted a recurrence of facial and trunk numbness on the left side.
Methods: MRI of the brain revealed a focus of IS in the basin of the right middle cerebral artery (Fig. 1). Examination revealed left-sided hemihypesthesia. Conclusions: Consequently, valve myxoma is a rare condition that places patients at elevated risk of stroke and other cardiovascular incidents. The early detection and management of the tumour are of paramount importance, a process that can be facilitated by echocardiography.

THE PRACTICAL 1-2-3-4-DAY RULE FOR STARTING DOACS AFTER ENDOVASCULAR THERAPY; THE FUKUOKA STROKE REGISTRY
CARDIOEMBOLISM.S. Kimura1, R. Matsuo2,3, N. Sahara2,4, T. Mizoguchi1, Y. Imamura1, N. Tagawa1, K. Mori1, T. Kuwashiro1, H. Sugimori1, K. Nakamura4, Y. Wakisaka3,4, M. Kamouchi2,3, T. Ago3,4
1National Hospital Organization Kyushu Medical Center, Cerebrovascular Medicine And Neurology, Fukuoka, Japan, 2Kyushu University, Department Of Health Care Administration And Management, Graduate School Of Medical Sciences, Fukuoka, Japan, 3Kyushu University, Center For Cohort Studies, Fukuoka, Japan, 4Kyushu University, Department Of Medicine And Clinical Science, Fukuoka, Japan
Background and Aims: The optimal timing for initiating direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) after endovascular therapy (EVT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) due to non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) remains uncertain. This study evaluated the impact of an early, severity-based DOAC initiation strategy—known as the “1-2-3-4-day rule” (Kimura, Stroke 2022)—on outcomes after EVT.
Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 409 patients (median age: 79 years; 51.3% women) from a multicenter registry who had anterior circulation AIS due to NVAF, underwent EVT within 24 hours of admission, and initiated DOAC therapy during hospitalization between January 2013 and March 2023. The group “early DOAC initiation" was defined by NIHSS score at admission: within 2 days for mild (0–7), 3 days for moderate (8–15), and 4 days for severe stroke (⩾16). Outcomes—including recurrent stroke and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) after 24 hours post-EVT—were compared between early and non-early initiation groups. Among 270 patients with pre-stroke modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–1, the association between early initiation and favorable functional outcome (mRS 0–2) at 90 days was assessed using adjusted Poisson regression.
Results: Recurrent stroke rates were similar between groups (early: 2.3% vs. non-early: 3.6%, p=0.44), and only one sICH occurred in the early group. Among functionally independent patients, early initiation was significantly associated with favorable outcomes (63.4% vs. 40.6%; adjusted risk ratio: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.05–1.66).
Conclusions: The "1-2-3-4-day rule" may be applicable after EVT, and early initiation of DOACs was associated with favorable functional outcomes after EVT.

TRANSCRIPTOME ANALYSIS IDENTIFIED SPP1+ MONOCYTES AS A KEY IN EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX FORMATION IN THROMBI
CARDIOEMBOLISM.T. Kitano1, T. Sasaki2, T. Matsui3, K. Todo4, H. Nakamura3, S. Okazaki5, M. Sakaguchi6, M. Yokoe7, H. Kishima3, H. Mochizuki2
1Osaka University, Neurology, Osaka, Japan, 2University of Osaka, Neurology, Suita, Japan, 3University of Osaka, Osaka, Japan, 4Tokyo Women’s Medical University, Department Of Neurology, Tokyo, Japan, 5NHO Osaka National Hospital, Neurology, Osaka, Japan, 6Osaka General Medical Center, Osaka, Japan, 7Toyonaka Municipal Hospital, Osaka, Japan
Background and Aims: Thrombi follow various natural courses. They are known to become harder over time and may persist long-term; some of them can also undergo early spontaneous dissolution and disappearance. Hindering thrombus stability may contribute to the treatment of thrombosis and the prevention of embolisms. However, the detailed mechanisms underlying thrombus maturation remain unclear.
Methods: We compared the RNA expression in three thrombi retrieved from cerebral vessels via thrombectomy with that in simultaneously sampled blood. The results were validated using immunohistochemistry on 66 thrombi retrieved from patients with cerebral embolism. Single-cell RNA sequencing data of thrombi from pulmonary arteries was utilized to uncover the molecular mechanisms.
Results: A total of 1,121 genes were upregulated in thrombi. Pathway enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses revealed upregulation of extracellular matrix formation and identified SPP1 as a hub gene. Immunohistochemistry revealed that expression level of osteopontin (the transcript of SPP1) positively correlated to that of collagen type VI in thrombi. Osteopontin was expressed primarily by monocytes/macrophages in the thrombi, particularly in older ones. Among these 66 patients, the presence of collagen type VI in the thrombus was marginally associated with longer puncture-to-reperfusion time and more passes before reperfusion, indicating that those thrombi were resistant to thrombectomy. Single-cell RNA sequencing of thrombi identified a subpopulation of monocytes/macrophages which highly express SPP1. These SPP1-high monocytes/macrophages highly expressed genes related to the extracellular matrix and communicated closely with fibroblasts.

Conclusions: Collectively, our findings indicate that SPP1-high monocytes/macrophages play a crucial role in thrombus maturation.

EV089 / #2550
IS THERE A ROLE FOR PRIOR ANTITHROMBOTIC TREATMENT IN THE FUNCTIONAL OUTCOME AND SEVERITY OF ATRIAL FIBRILLATION RELATED ISCHEMIC STROKE?
CARDIOEMBOLISM.J. Moreno, A. Mercado, C. Huamani, J. Garcia, K. Enriquez, I. Reyes, V. Cano, A. Arauz
Instituto Nacional de Neurologia y Neurocirugia, Stroke Clinic, Mexico City, Mexico
Background and Aims: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a prevalent and high- risk modifiable factor of ischemic stroke (IS). Despite its recognized role in stroke prevention, several patients do not receive adequate antithrombotic treatment because of age, comorbidities, or the perception of frailty. Although the benefits of antithrombotic therapy for stroke prevention have been well established, its impact on functional outcomes remains uncertain.
Methods: This retrospective, observational, and analytical study included patients with AF-related IS admitted between January 2010 and December 2023. Antithrombotic therapy before IS (anticoagulant, antiplatelet or none) was assessed as the exposure variable. The primary outcome was functional status at 90 days, as assessed using the modified Rankin Scale score (mRS ⩽2 indicating favorable outcome). The secondary outcomes included stroke severity on admission (NIHSS ⩾16 = severe stroke), large vessel occlusion (LVO), symptomatic hemorrhagic transformation (sHT) and mortality.
Results: A total of 291 (median age:61 years; 55% women) participants were included. Among these, 60.8% had a known diagnosis of AF before the event, whereas 49.2% were not on anticoagulants despite having high CHA2DS2-VASc scores. Patients receiving anticoagulants before IS had a higher likelihood of favorable outcomes at 90 days compared to those without prior treatment (OR 2.60; CI:1.21-5.60). However, no significant differences were observed in stroke severity at admission among the treatment groups.
Conclusions: Anticoagulant therapy is underutilized in patients with AF despite its benefits. In addition to stroke prevention, anticoagulant therapy appears to improve post-stroke functional outcomes, highlighting its importance in managing high-risk patients with AF.

FOCUSED CARDIAC ULTRASOUND FOR NEUROLOGIST. AN INTERNATIONAL MULTICENTER VALIDATION STUDY
CARDIOEMBOLISM.J. Pagola1, P. Lochner2, R. Lincenik3, G. Fiore4, F.A. Montellano5, V. Gonzalez6, V. Pavlicek2, J. Alvarez-Cienfuegos7, S. Mora7, R. Muñoz8, A. Vera8, A. Ruiz9, J. Gonzalez-Mirelis9, J. Rodriguez-Pardo De Donlebún10, E. Pérez David10, J. Garcia-Sanchez11, L. Ruiz Gomez11, L. Amaya12, E. Carrión12, T. Rodriguez-Ares13, C. Abou13, M. Paya14, L. Guerra14, A. De Arce15, A. Benegas15, V. Reskovic16
1Vall d’Hebron Hospital, Stroke Unit. Neurology Department, Barcelona, Spain, 2UKS – Universitätsklinikum des Saarlandes, Homburg, Germany, 3North West Anglia Foundation NHS Trust Peterborough City Hospital, Peterborough, United Kingdom, 4Careggi University Hospital, Florence, Italy, 5Universitätsklinikum Würzburg, Würzburg, Germany, 6Vall d’Hebron Hospital, Cardiology Department, Barcelona, Spain, 7Hospital Universitari de Girona Dr. Josep Trueta, Girona, Spain, 8Hospital Universitario Navarra, Pamplona, Spain, 9Hospital Universitario Puerta de Hierro Majadahonda, Madrid, Spain, 10Hospital Universitario La Paz , Madrid, Spain, 11Hospital Universitario de Basurto, Bilbao, Spain, 12Hospital Universitario Torrecardenas, Almeria, Spain, 13Hospital Universitario Lucus Augusti, Lugo, Spain, 14Complejo Hospitalario Universitario de Albacete, Albacete, Spain, 15Hospital Universitario Complejo Donostia, San Sebastian, Spain, 16University Hospital Centre Zagreb, Zagreb, Croatia
Background and Aims: Up to 30% of ischemic strokes have an embolic origin. Focused cardiac ultrasound (FoCUS) can be applied as a screening tool for advanced diagnostic evaluations.This study aimed to validate neurologists’ ability to perform FOCUS and to detect sources of stroke embolism.
Methods: International multicenter, prospective, validation study involving consecutive enrollment of acute stroke patients. Neurologists and cardiologists independently performed the FoCUS protocol blinded. FoCUS examination was 2D TTE examination with color Doppler assessment. A training program for neurologists was carried out. A twenty video cases questionnaire was given to evaluate the ability to recognize sources of cardioembolic stroke
Results: A total of 432 paired studies involving 216 patients were conducted in 12 Centers. For neurologist and cardiologist there was no difference in detection of Left Ventricle (LV) dysfunction: 7.4% vs 7.9% (p=0.834); LV dilation 2.8% vs 2.3% (p=0.766); VC 7.2% vs 9.1% (p=0.501); Right Ventricle dysfunction 0.9% vs 0.9% (p=0.999); Pericardial effusion 0.5% vs 1.9% (p=0.212). In patients with optimal thoracic window (n=183) the concordance was Kappa 0.640 for LV dysfunction, Kappa was 0.589 for LV dilation and Kappa was 0.226 for VC collapsibility The neurologist’s performance in detecting embolic sources demonstrated a sensitivity of 93.82% and a specificity of 92.92%. The identification of the type of embolic source: LV akinesia 88%, LV dysfunction 83%, complex aortic plaque 88%, and mitral stenosis 55%.
Conclusions: Properly trained neurologists could reliably perform a FoCUS exam, particularly for the assessment of LV function and LV dilation. Neurologists showed high validity to identified embolic sources by FoCUS.
EV091 / #584
OPTIMAL TARGET OF BLOOD PRESSURE AND ASSOCIATED VARIABLES IN EARLY STAGE OF ACUTE CARDIOEMBOLIC ISCHEMIC STROKE
CARDIOEMBOLISM.M.-S. Park1, H. Kim2, H. Kim1, J.-T. Kim1, K. Choi1, J.-M. Kim1, S. Lee2
1Chonnam National University Medical School & Hospital, Neurology, Gwangju, Korea, Republic of, 2Chonnam National University Medical School, Forensic Medicine, Gwangju, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Cardioembolic stroke (CES) patients show distinct hemodynamic patterns compared to other ischemic stroke subtypes, questioning whether permitting high blood pressure (BP) as guideline in the early phase is appropriate for CES. This study investigates the impact of BP parameters on outcomes in CES patients.
Methods: In this retrospective study, 2441 CES patients admitted within 48 hours of symptom onset at a tertiary stroke center between January 2011 and December 2023 were analyzed. Patients were classified into normotensive (ystolic BP during the first 48 hours. BPV indices—including standard deviation, successive variation, coefficient of variation, and average real variability—were calculated and categorized into quartiles. Primary outcomes were early neurological deterioration (END) during hospitalization and favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0–2) at 3 months. Secondary outcomes included hemorrhagic transformation (HT), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), composite vascular events, and all-cause mortality.
Results: The hypertensive group had a significantly higher incidence of END (23.8% vs. 14.9%, p systolic BP was independently associated with END (OR 1.49, p=0.001) and poor 3-month outcomes (OR 0.76, p=0.013). Among BPV indices, higher standard deviation was associated with increased END risk.
Conclusions: Our findings suggest that higher BP tolerance in CES, as currently recommended by guidelines, is associated with poor functional outcomes, highlighting the need for more tailored BP management strategies in this specific stroke subtype.
EV092 / #1905
DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF TRANS FORAMINAL APPROACH IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF RIGHT TO LEFT SHUNT BY TRANS CRANIAL DOPPLER
CARDIOEMBOLISM.M. Pradeep, D. Embramadathil, S. Lakshmi
Eumed Super Speciality Hospital, Stroke & Neurovascular Sonology, Palakkad, Kerala, India
Background and Aims: Although most patients with a patent foramen ovale (PFO) are asymptomatic, a large size PFO can cause significant right to left shunting(RLS), especially with Valsalva maneuvre. This can lead to paradoxical embolization and stroke. Trans temporal window contrast TCD is used routinely to monitor the presence of right to left shunt and also to quantify the shunt. In the absence of a temporal window it is not possible to perform TCD using the temporal window. In such a situation trans forminal insonation using the sub occipital window may be a useful alternative to detect RLS.How ever data regarding the sub occipital approach is scarce. Aim. To compare the efficacy of the trans foraminal approach with the trans temporal approach in the detection of right to left shunt by TCD.
Methods: TCD bubble test was performed in the sitting position with a head frame with Valsalva maneuvre using agitated saline. Intracranial arteries monitored were the M1 MCA & Basilar artery. Micro embolic signals were quantified.
Results: 220 patients were included in the study .100 % of the patients showing micro emboli signals with MCA insonation also showed micro embolic signals on Basilar artery insonation. Quantification of micro embolic signals were matching both insonations.
Conclusions: There was a perfect agreement between the trans temporal & trans foraminal approaches regarding the detection of right to left shunt. The trans foraminal approach is a definte alternative to detect RLS in patients with out a trans temporal window.
EV093 / #1756
CONTINUATION OF ANTICOAGULANT TREATMENT IN THE ACUTE PHASE OF CARDIOEMBOLIC ISCHEMIC STROKE
CARDIOEMBOLISM.R. Rigual1, M. Blanco-Bañares2, M. Lorenzo-Dieguez1, J. Rodriguez-Pardo De Donlebún1, G. Ruiz-Ares1, S. Fernández-Fernández3, J. Roa-Escobar4, A. García-Torres5, S. García-Madrona6, A. De Felipe5, S. Trillo-Senin7, C. Ramos7, R. Terrero-Carpio8, E. Escolar-Escamilla8, B. Fuentes1
1Hospital La Paz Institute for Health Research, IdiPAZ, Universidad Autonoma de Madrid, Neurology, Madrid, Spain, 2Hospital La Paz Institute for Health Research, IdiPAZ, Universidad Autonoma de Madrid, Laboratory Medicine Department, Madrid, Spain, 3Hospital La Paz Institute for Health Research, IdiPAZ, Universidad Autonoma de Madrid, Radiology, Madrid, Spain, 4Fundación Jiménez Diaz University Hospital, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, Neurology, Madrid, Spain, 5Fundación Jiménez Díaz University Hospital, Neurology, Madrid, Spain, 6Ramón y Cajal University Hospital, Instituto Ramón y Cajal de Investigación Sanitaria, Universidad de Alcalá, Neurology, Madrid, Spain, 7La Princesa University Hospital, IIS-IP, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, Neurology, Madrid, Spain, 8Getafe University Hospital, European University of Madrid, Neurology, Madrid, Spain
Background and Aims: There is no consensus for continuation or disruption anticoagulant treatment in the acute phase of ischemic stroke in patients previously under anticoagulation due to cardioembolic source. Our aim is to compare safety and clinical outcomes in these patients.
Methods: Prospective, observational and multicentric study of patients admitted in the acute phase of ischemic stroke and major cardioembolic source treated with anticoagulation at admission. We compared safety and clinical outcomes (ischemic stroke [IS] recurrence, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage [ICH] or composite vascular event [IS/ICH/systemic embolism/major extracranial bleeding]) at discharge and at 90 days follow-up, depending on the continuation or disruption of anticoagulation upon admission.
Results: We included 227 patients; anticoagulation was continued in 117 (51.5 %). These patients had lower NIHSS scores and higher ASPECTS at admission, and lower rate of past ICH, large vessel occlusion and mechanical thrombectomy treatment. Patients in whom anticoagulation was continued presented lower IS recurrence rates at 90 days (5.1% vs 12.7%, p=0.044) and lower incidence rate of composite event at 90 days (10.3% vs 22.7%, p=0.011). There were no significant differences in hemorrhagic incidence rates. In the multivariate analysis, anticoagulation continuation was independently associated with lower odds of ischemic recurrence at 90 days [OR 0.088 (95% CI 0.020 TO 0.398); p=0.002] and composite event at 90 days [OR 0.235 (95% CI 0.093 to 0.591); p=0.002].
Conclusions: The continuation of anticoagulation treatment in the acute phase of cardioembolic stroke could protect for new vascular events driven by the reduction of ischemic events without increase the hemorrhagic risk.
EV094 / #1600
SIGNS OF LEFT HEART ENLARGEMENT IN COMMON CAROTID DOPPLER STUDIES
CARDIOEMBOLISM.A. Sanchez Huertas1, S. García-Pastor2, N. Morato-Martín1, M. Gómez-Fábrega1, M. Alonso De Leciñana1, B. Fuentes1, R. Rigual1, C. Hervás1, L. Casado-Fernández1, E. De Celis1, G. Ruiz-Ares1, J. Rodriguez-Pardo De Donlebún1
1Hospital La Paz Institute for Health Research, IdiPAZ, Universidad Autonoma de Madrid, Neurology, Madrid, Spain, 2Rey Juan Carlos University Hospital, Universidad Autonoma de Madrid, Intensive Care Unit, Móstoles, Spain
Background and Aims: Carotid Doppler Ultrasound (CDU), together with cardiac evaluation, are fundamental complementary tests in transient ischemic attack (TIA) clinics. We aimed to evaluate whether the velocimetric analysis of CDU can help identify indirect signs of left atrial (LA) or left ventricle (LV) dilation for a more expedite cardiac assessment.
Methods: Retrospective observational study of outpatients attended at our TIA clinic for CDU with transthoracic echocardiogram performed ±6 months from CDU. Patients with ⩾50% stenosis in any carotid, known atrial fibrillation or any previous cardioembolic source were excluded. The study consisted of an exploratory cohort (2021 outpatients) comparing systolic common carotid CDU parameters (peak systolic velocity [PSV], systolic upstroke and downstroke times) with LV indexed volume, and diastolic parameters (peak diastolic velocity, diastolic relaxation time [DRT] and end diastolic velocity [EDV]) with LA indexed volume. Generated hypotheses were confirmed in a validation cohort (2022-2023 outpatients).
Results: Exploratory cohort included 38 patients (76 carotids). After adjusting for age, only DRT was directly correlated with LA (r = .356, p <.001) and LV (r = .415, p <.001) volumes. Validation cohort included 78 patients (156 carotids). After adjusting for age, direct correlations of DRT with LA (r = .393, p =.001) and LV (r = .304, p =.007) volumes were confirmed. Median DRT was 467ms for normal LA, 492ms for mild and 592ms for moderate-severe LA dilation. DRT showed an AUC of .848 (p<.001) for moderate-severe LA dilation.
Conclusions: Diastolic relaxation time measured by common carotid doppler might be useful for identifying patients with left heart enlargement.
EV095 / #2483
IMPORTANCE OF ROUTINE CARDIAC ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY TO DIAGNOSE SYMPTOMATIC PATENT FORAMEN OVALE IN CRYPTOGENIC STROKE: EXPERIENCE FROM A STROKE CENTRE IN KENYA
CARDIOEMBOLISM.N. Mongare, H. Kariuki, D. Singh Sokhi
Aga Khan University, Nairobi, Kenya
Background and Aims: Patent foramen ovale (PFO) are a rare but recognised cause of acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) in up to 15% of cryptogenic cases. The Risk of Paradoxical Embolism score (ROPE) looks at PFO characteristics to inform if definitive treatment is PFO closure for preventing recurrent stroke. However, some international guidelines do not recommend routine cardiac echocardiography in all stroke patients, and data on PFO in young-onset stroke from Africa is limited. We describe the burden of young-onset stroke attributable to PFOs in our stroke centre in Nairobi where routine echocardiography is performed in all AIS cases.
Methods: In a sub-analysis of a previously published study on young-onset AIS patients aged 18-65 years admitted between 2010-2022, we identified patients in whom a PFO was detected and deemed causal based on the ROPE score. All patients underwent standardized stroke workup, including transthoracic followed by transoesophageal echocardiography with bubble contrast studies.
Results: Of 388 stroke patients [61.9% (240/388) male; median age 49 years], 11 patients (2.8%) had symptomatic PFO. Median (interquartile range) age was 41 (28-57) years, with 8/11 (72.2%) being female. Over half (6/11, 67%) had high ROPE scores (median score 7). Only two of these patients underwent PFO closure, both done overseas due to lack of local facilities at the time of diagnosis. The remainder continued on best medical therapy.
Conclusions: Routine echocardiography gives a small but significant yield of symptomatic PFOs in AIS especially in younger patients in our cohort. However, resource limitations limit PFO closure and highlight a gap in regional stroke care.
EV096 / #2646
COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA FOLLOWING STROKE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF PREVALENCE, PREDICTORS, AND OUTCOMES
COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.A.A. Al Sakkaf
Seiyoun University, Hadhramout, Yemen
Background and Aims: Cognitive decline and dementia are prevalent but often overlooked consequences of stroke, with major implications for recovery and quality of life. Despite its clinical significance, post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remains underdiagnosed, and evidence on modifiable risk factors is fragmented. This review synthesizes available evidence to guide early detection and intervention Objective:
To determine the prevalence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes of cognitive impairment and dementia after stroke, with subgroup analyses by stroke type, geographic region, and assessment tools.
Methods: We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science (from inception to January 2025) using PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies included prospective/retrospective cohorts or RCTs with ⩾3 months follow-up, assessing cognitive outcomes using standardized tools (e.g., MoCA, MMSE). Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Data were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis (PROSPERO protocol)
Results: From 3,425 records, 78 studies met inclusion criteria. Pooled estimates showed 28% (95% CI: 22–34%) of stroke survivors developed PSCI within 1 year, increasing to 40% (95% CI: 35–45%) after recurrent strokes. Strong predictors included:
- Non-modifiable: Older age (OR=1.8, 1.4–2.3), left hemispheric infarcts (OR=2.1, 1.7–2.6).
- Modifiable: Hypertension (OR=1.5, 1.2–1.9), diabetes (OR=1.6, 1.3–2.0), and pre-stroke cognitive decline (OR=3.2, 2.5–4.0).
Conclusions: PSCI affects over one-third of stroke survivors, with modifiable vascular risks contributing significantly. Routine cognitive screening post-stroke and targeted management of hypertension/diabetes may reduce incidence. Study limitations include heterogeneity in assessment tools and underrepresentation of low-income populations.
EV097 / #1917
IMPAIRED CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW AND ELEVATED ARTERIAL STIFFNESS AFTER STROKE: IMPLICATIONS FOR COGNITIVE HEALTH
COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.S. Billinger, B. Bartsch, T. Baldridge, A. Britton-Carpenter, A. Engler
University of Kansas Medical Center, Neurology, Kansas City, United States of America
Background and Aims: Cerebrovascular dysfunction may contribute to cognitive decline in individuals with stroke. This study aimed to compare resting middle cerebral artery blood velocity (MCAv) and hemodynamic measures between people with chronic stroke and age- and sex-matched controls, and to explore associations between MCAv and global cognition in stroke.
Methods: Nineteen individuals with chronic stroke (20.5+/-17.9 months post-stroke; 71.2+/-6.2 years) were age and sex-matched to neurologically healthy controls (70.2+/-6.7years, p=0.63). Resting MCAv (mean, systolic, diastolic), and blood pressure were assessed using transcranial Doppler ultrasound and beat-to-beat finger plethysmography. We assessed pulse wave velocity (PWV), a marker of arterial stiffness, using applanation tonometry. Cognitive performance was measured using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Correlations between MCAv and MoCA were examined only in the stroke group.
Results: Controls demonstrated significantly higher MCAv mean (p=0.02), systolic (p=0.04), and diastolic velocity (p=0.002) compared to individuals with stroke, which could be indicative of reduced cerebral perfusion capacity and vascular reserve. PWV was significantly higher in the stroke group (p = 0.004). No differences were observed in any blood pressure measures (p>0.2). Among participants with stroke, systolic MCAv showed a strong positive correlation with MoCA scores (r = 0.629, p = 0.003), while diastolic velocity showed a weaker, non-significant association (r=0.36, p=0.12).
Conclusions: Stroke survivors exhibit lower resting cerebral blood flow and higher peripheral arterial stiffness compared to matched controls. These findings suggest that monitoring and targeting both cerebrovascular function and arterial stiffness may be critical components of post-stroke care to preserve cognitive health.
EV098 / #81
RAPID INSTRUCTED TASK LEARNING IS IMPAIRED AFTER STROKE AND ASSOCIATED WITH IMPAIRMENTS IN PREPOTENT INHIBITION AND PROCESSING SPEED
COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.R. Binyamin Netser, L. Smuelof, A. Shkedy-Rabani
Ben Gurion University, Brain And Cognition, Beer Sheva, Israel
Background and Aims: Motor rehabilitation plays a pivotal role in motor recovery following stroke. Effective rehabilitation requires patients to follow instructions accurately, a task that can be complicated due to cognitive impairments that are associated with stroke, such as decreased attention and inhibition. Rapid instructed task learning (RITL), a crucial cognitive process for learning novel tasks through instructions, has not been directly studied in older adults or individuals with stroke. This study aimed to evaluate RITL in individuals with chronic stroke and investigate its cognitive determinants.
Methods: The study involved 31 individuals with chronic stroke and 36 age-matched healthy controls. All participants underwent a computerized cognitive assessment that included an anti-saccade task to measure prepotent inhibition and processing speed. RITL and proactive inhibition were assessed using a stimulus-response association task (NEXT).
Results: The results demonstrated that individuals with chronic stroke exhibited significant impairments in RITL, along with reduced prepotent inhibition and slower processing speed, compared to the control group. Correlation analyses revealed a strong association between RITL performance and measures of prepotent inhibition and processing speed.
Conclusions: This study highlights that individuals with stroke show compromised RITL, which may be linked to their deficits in prepotent inhibition and processing speed. These findings suggest that cognitive impairments impacting RITL could potentially hinder the efficacy of motor rehabilitation. Future research should explore the causal impact of RITL deficits on rehabilitation outcomes and overall motor recovery to better tailor rehabilitation strategies for stroke survivors.
EV099 / #891
INCIDENTALLY DISCOVERED STROKE LESIONS IN PATIENTS WITH DEMENTIA
COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.A.-H. Cho1, S.-J. Park1, D.-W. Ryu1, K.-H. Cho2, S.-M. Wang3, S.-H. Kim3, H.K. Lim3
1Catholic University of Korea, Yeouido St.Mary’s Hospital, Neurology, SEOUL, Korea, Republic of, 2Korea university college of medicine, Neurology, Seoul, Korea, Republic of, 3Catholic University of Korea, Yeouido St.Mary’s Hospital, Psychiatry, SEOUL, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: The elderly patients with dementia may also have vascular risk factors, which make them vulnerable to stroke. We report cases of stroke discovered incidentally in patients with dementic illness.
Methods: Between January 2023 and March 2025, we enrolled cases with incidental stroke lesions who underwent Brain MRI during routine dementia evaluations. Demographic, clinical and radiological findings on MRI were reviewed. The presence of vascular risk factors, stroke subtypes, severity of dementia, diagnosis of dementic illness were investigated. Descriptive analysis was performed.
Results: A total of 10 patients were enrolled in this study. Mean age was 79 and 5 were male. Regarding the diagnosis of demetic illness, 7 patients had mild cognitive impairment or dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease (AD), and 3 had vascular cognitive impairment. In 7 patients, amyloid PET-CT were performed for dementia evaluation. The MRI showed tiny acute ischemic infarct in a single vascular territory in 4 patients, tiny acute ischemic infarcts in multiple vascular territories in 5 and cortical superficial siderosis in one. The TOAST subtypes were cardioembolism in one, small vessel occlusion in two, cryptogenic in two, other causes in two, undetermined due to incomplete stroke work-up in 3. All had more than one vascular risk factors. However, there was not any clinical symptom which is relevant to the stroke lesion.
Conclusions: Silent stroke lesions could be incidentally discovered during dementia evaluations. The lesions were small and mostly located in multiple vascular territories. For those dementia patients with incidental stroke, stroke etiologic documentation and secondary stroke preventions are required.

EVALUATING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF A COGNITIVE REHABILITATION INTERVENTION OR REPETITIVE TRANSCRANIAL MAGNETIC STIMULATION (RTMS) FOR IMPROVING POST-STROKE FUNCTIONAL DEFICITS DUE TO COGNITION: A STUDY PROTOCOL

Background and Aims: Post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) affects up to 60% of stroke survivors globally within the first year. PCSI significantly impacts daily functioning, maintain employment, and social participation. Effective interventions to improve outcomes are desperately needed.Aim: To determine the effectiveness of the Symptom-Targeted Approach to Cognitive Rehabilitation for Indian Stroke Survivors (STAR-IS) and/or rTMS (neuromodulation) on functional cognitive outcomes in individuals with PSCI at three-months post-stroke.
Methods: A novel 2x2 factorial, assessor-blinded, randomized controlled trial (RCT) will be conducted in two phases. A Vanguard phase(n=40) at two Indian sites will assess feasibility of recruitment, retention, and intervention adherence. Findings will inform necessary modifications before implementation of the Main study which will proceed as a continuation of the Vanguard if methodological changes are minimal. 468 participants across six Indian sites (including vanguard sites) will be randomized into four arms (117 per arm): STAR-IS + rTMS + Standard Care, STAR-IS + Standard Care, rTMS + Standard Care, and Standard Care. The study is powered at 80% to detect a 20% improvement in Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM) scores for cognition-affected tasks one-month post-intervention.
Results: This study will report feasibility and effectiveness data on the STAR-IS and rTMS in improving cognitive-related functional outcomes in stroke survivors.
Conclusions: This study is designed to efficiently provide data on interventions that could improve the lives of stroke survivors. Simultaneous study of interventions (STAR-IS or rTMS), design (2x2 factorial of rehabilitation and neuromodulation), and implementation (Vanguard + Main study to more rapidly provide results) contribute to an efficient and innovative trial.
EV101 / #995
CONTEXTUALIZING THE STRATEGY-BASED COGNITIVE REHABILITATION INTERVENTION FOR INDIAN STROKE SURVIVORS
COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.D. Dawar1,2, J. Pandian3, L. Turkstra2, J. Bosch2
1Christian Medical College and Hospital, Ludhiana, Punjab, Neurology Department, Ludhiana, India, 2McMaster University, Hamilton, Canada, 3Christian Medical College, Punjab, India
Background and Aims: The Symptom Targeted Approach to Rehabilitation after Concussion (STAR-C) is a strategy-based cognitive rehabilitation intervention originally developed to help U.S. military personnel and veterans with mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) manage everyday cognitive challenges. This study focuses on adapting the intervention to enhance the cultural and contextual suitability for India stroke survivors. Aim: To describe the process for adapting the STAR intervention for the Indian context.
Methods: The adaptation process will use the ADAPT process model. A dedicated adaptation team comprising rehabilitation professionals and patient partners will execute and lead the adaptation process. We will first assess the rationale for intervention and assess how well it fits with the Indian context. We will also evaluate the need for the intervention within the target population and identify any contextual difference between original and adapted version that could influence its implementation and effectiveness.
Results: The study is currently in the adaptation phase. Institutional ethics approval has been obtained, and initial steps—such as forming the adaptation team and developing the engagement plan—have been completed. Ongoing adaptations are being guided by contextual factors and preliminary feedback. Adaptation process learnings, including key challenges, contributions of the adaptation team, and proposed modifications, will be shared at the conference.
Conclusions: There is a critical need for post stroke cognitive interventions that are culturally appropriate. This is the first study to consider implementation factors that may influence post-stroke cognitive intervention delivery within India healthcare context. Once adapted, the STAR-IS will be piloted tested to assess its feasibility and acceptability.
EV102 / #913
COGNITIVE RECOVERY AFTER POST-STROKE DELIRIUM [RECOVER] A PROOF-OF-CONCEPT STUDY FOR A REPEATED MULTIMODAL COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT
COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.L. Geiger1, S. Klütz1, C. Mychajliw2,3, C. Gäbele2,3, A. Jooß1,4, C. Single1, U. Ziemann1,4, K. Feil1, A. Mengel1,4
1University Hospital Tübingen, Department Of Neurology & Stroke, Tübingen, Germany, 2University Hospital for Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, Geriatric Department, Tübingen, Germany, 3TuCAN, Tübingen Cognitive Assessment for Neuropsychiatric Disorders, Tübingen, Germany, 4Hertie Institute for Clinical Brain Research, Tübingen, Germany
Background and Aims: Post-stroke delirium (PSD) is a severe complication in acute stroke patients, associated with longer hospital stays, higher mortality, and increased disability. Behavioral studies on cognitive functioning showed significantly poorer cognitive outcomes in both PSD and non-PSD stroke patients compared to healthy controls. Thus, the distinction between “stroke-related” and “PSD-related” cognitive impairments remains unclear. Memory functions are often affected and highly disabling but comprehensive studies, including task-based functional MRI, on PSD are very limited.
Methods: This longitudinal proof-of-concept study investigates the short- and long-term effects of stroke and PSD on cognitive outcome. Post-stroke cognitive function (PSCF) will be assessed using a multimodal approach, including a multi-domain neuropsychological app (TuCAN) to facilitate a standardized, rapid testing, particularly for long-term outcomes, as well as task-based functional MRI, during the acute and post-acute phases and at 3-month follow-up. Forty acute stroke patients will be divided into a PSD group and a non-PSD control group. In the context of the proof-of-concept study, the eligibility of a modified working-memory task, an app-based neuropsychological assessment, and a multimodal MRI protocol will be evaluated. The primary endpoint is a between-group comparison of cognitive outcome, defined as global PSCF at 3 months follow-up.
Results: Preliminary results on the feasibility of the study protocol and the primary endpoint will be presented.
Conclusions: This protocol provides a comprehensive multimodal assessment for investigating PSCF in PSD vs. non-PSD patients. Findings from this study, may enhance our understanding of the contribution of PSD to long-term cognitive impairment after stroke.
EV103 / #779
THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF CILOSTAZOL AND GINKGO BILOBA ON COGNITIVE DECLINE IN SMALL VESSEL DISEASE WITHOUT ACUTE INFARCTION
COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.Y.S. Ha1, K.O. Lee2, M.W. Kim3
1Presbyterian Medical Center, Department Of Neurology, Jeonju, Korea, Republic of, 2CHA Bundang Medical Center, CHA Univerisity College of Medicine, Department Of Neurology, Jeonju, Korea, Republic of, 3Presbyterian Medical Center, Department Of Nuclear Medicine, Jeonju, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) can lead to progressive cognitive and motor speech impairments even in the absence of acute infarcts. This study presents a case of recurrent lacunar infarction without new lesions on neuroimaging, highlighting a therapeutic strategy targeting amyloid pathology and protein homeostasis.
Methods: A 64-year-old woman with a history of two previous lacunar infarctions presented with worsening dysarthria and sudden cognitive decline. Despite symptom progression, diffusion-weighted MRI showed no acute lesions. Amyloid-PET revealed diffuse cortical and basal ganglia amyloid deposition, and FDG-PET indicated hypometabolism in the frontal and temporal lobes. The patient was treated with cilostazol (200 mg/day) and Ginkgo biloba extract (160 mg/day). Clinical, neuropsychological, and imaging assessments were conducted over a five-year follow-up.
Results: Initial examination showed severe dysarthria, mild dysphagia, and cognitive impairment (MMSE 25, CDR 1). COGNITION AND DEMENTIA.H. Ouyang1, T. Miller2, C. Tsang2, M. Li2, R. Chung2, M. Pang2
1Guangzhou Medical University, School Of Biomedical Engineering, Guangzhou, China, 2The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Department Of Rehabilitation Sciences, Hong Kong, Hong Kong PRC

Conclusions: Among the various DT walking scenarios assessed, stride length, cadence, and cadence variability DTE showed the greatest accuracy in differentiating between groups. These findings may assist clinicians in identifying the most suitable gait parameters to assess DTE among people with stroke during complex walking tasks and may provide important insight for the appropriate stratification of gait and cognitive tasks according to stroke history and severity.

Background and Aims: Crossed aphasia (CA) is a rare phenomenon characterized by language impairment resulting from a lesion in the right cerebral hemisphere of right-handed individuals, despite the predominance of language function localization in the left hemisphere in the majority of population. Its prevalence ranges from 0.4-3.5% of all aphasic cases in right-handed individuals without any family history of sinistrality.
Methods: We report a case of CA following a right hemispheric stroke in a right-handed male.

Language deficits were noted in comprehension, verbal fluency, and writing, while repetition, naming, and reading were preserved, thus consistent with mixed transcortical aphasia. Impairments in working memory, executive function, and calculation were also identified, whereas attention and visuospatial abilities remained intact. Head MRI revealed multiple infarcts in the right hemisphere, involving the corona radiata, lateral periventricular region, frontal and parietal lobe (Figure 1). A diagnosis of CA in ischemic stroke was made. He was initiated on dual antiplatelet therapy (Aspilet and Clopidogrel), speech therapy, and transcranial magnetic stimulation. The patient demonstrated improvement in aphasia at the one-week follow-up.

Conclusions: Albeit rare, aphasia may occur following a right hemispheric stroke, thus showing the complexity of speech pathology and highlighting the need for individualized treatment strategies in language rehabilitation.

LUS was performed in patients with suspected infection, analyzing 11 sonographic patterns across 12 lung zones: dominant A/B/C profiles, B-lines [0, 1–2, 3–5, >5], consolidation, sliding, air bronchogram, and effusion.
Results: Among 14 patients with clinical suspicion of pneumonia, 8 (57%) fulfilled mCDC criteria. Consolidation was present in 4/8 (50%) of CDC-confirmed SAP cases and in 0/6 of non-SAP. Pattern C appeared in 3/8 (38%) SAP patients and in 0/6 non-SAP. Total B-line counts and distribution overlapped between groups.. A rule combining consolidation or pattern C yielded 100% specificity and 50% sensitivity. Adding >5 B-lines improved sensitivity to 75% (6/8), but reduced specificity to 17% (1/6). Notably, >5 B-lines were found in 62.5% (5 out of 8) of SAP cases and in 83.3% (5 out of 6) of non-SAP, suggesting this pattern may reflect non-infectious pulmonary changes such as fluid overload or atelectasis.
Conclusions: Lung ultrasound detects early, evolving pulmonary changes in stroke patients with SAP. Consolidation and pattern C remain highly specific markers. Combining them with >5 B-lines may enhance sensitivity, though interpretation requires clinical context. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Conclusions: Stroke poses a major health burden in Tanzania, with high prevalence, mortality and delayed presentation. These findings highlight urgent gaps in prevention and acute care, supporting the need for a national stroke registry to guide evidence-based interventions.

BAYESIAN BETA BINOMIAL META ANALYSIS OF ENDOVASCULAR THERAPY FOR DISTAL AND MEDIUM VESSEL OCCLUSION STROKE: A NOVEL APPROACH TO EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS
EARLY (YOUNG) CAREER.Y. Pathan, S. Golkonda, J. Olive, A. Tariq, V. Fernandes, M.A. Patni
Ras Al Khaimah Medical And Health Sciences University, Medicine, Ras Al Khaimah, United Arab Emirates
Background and Aims: The role of Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in large vessel occlusion in acute ischemic stroke is well established but its efficacy and safety for medium and distal vessel occlusions (DMVO) remain unclear. The aim of this study is to systematically evaluate the effectiveness of EVT in patients with DMVO ischemic strokes.
Methods: This prospective Bayesian meta-analysis evaluated randomized controlled trials on endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for distal medium vessel occlusion (DMVO). Given the context of very few available RCTs and assessment of rare events, a Beta binomial bayesian approach was adopted. Data were analyzed using R (bayesplot, rstan, ggplot2). Risk of bias was assessed using RoB-2. Sensitivity analyses with alternative priors tested robustness.
Results: Three RCTs were analyzed, including 601 subjects in the EVT plus BMT cohort and 620 in BMT alone. The pooled posterior log odds ratio for favorable mRS was 0.04 (95% CrI: -0.27 to 0.34). The estimated pooled rate of successful reperfusion (modified TICI 2b–3) was approximately 73.4% across the included trials. The rate of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage was significantly higher in the EVT group (pooled posterior LOR: 0.77; 95% CrI: 0.07 to 1.53). Despite high reperfusion rates, the meta-analysis didn’t provide conclusive evidence of improved functional outcomes with EVT, awaiting further trials to establish its role in DMVOs.

Conclusions: No significant difference in benifit was noted between the groups, however EVT plus BMT was associated with an increase in sICH when compared with BMT alone. The wide selection criteria, low NIHSS and old patient groups could have attributed to these results.

1Jose R. Reyes Memorial Medical Center, Department Of Neurology, Manila City, Philippines, 2De La Salle Medical and Health Sciences Institute, Section Of Neurology, Department Of Internal Medicine, Dasmarinas City, Philippines, 3Far Eastern University - Dr. Nicanor Reyes Medical Foundation, Section Of Neurology, Department Of Internal Medicine, Quezon City, Philippines, 4University of Santo Tomas Hospital, Department Of Neuroscience And Behavioral Medicine, Manila City, Philippines, 5University of Missouri, Stroke Institute And Department Of Neurology, Columbia, United States of America
Background and Aims: Despite the rapidly increasing prevalence of electronic cigarette (EC) use, its effects on cerebrovascular health remain unclear. This pilot study is the first to explore the impact of chronic EC vaping on cerebrovascular function.
Methods: This case-control study included 60 participants: 30 long-term EC users and 30 controls with no history of EC use. Cerebrovascular function was assessed using the breath holding index (BHI), a transcranial Doppler-based measure of cerebral vasomotor reactivity, and a preclinical marker for cerebrovascular disease.
Results: Long-term EC vapers exhibited lower BHI values compared to controls (p < .001), with long-term EC use found to be significantly associated with impaired BHI values {odds ratio (OR) 4.26 [95% confidence interval (CI) 2.03–8.52]; p < .001}, even after adjusting for (1) changes in mean arterial pressure (OR 1.37 [95% CI 1.11–3.95]; p = .007), (2) age and sex (OR 1.42 [95% CI 1.03–3.21]; p = .002), and (3) patterns of EC use (OR 1.21 [95% CI 1.03–3.21]; p = .039). Frequency of EC use was independently associated with impaired BHI (OR 1.28 [95% CI 1.02–2.66]; p = .035).
Conclusions: This study suggests an association between long-term EC vaping and impaired cerebrovascular function, as assessed by BHI. Larger prospective studies employing more definitive measures of cerebral vasomotor reactivity are needed to confirm these findings.

ANTITHROMBOTIC THERAPY IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION AND MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION: AN 8-YEAR ANALYSIS OF PRESCRIPTION TRENDS AND GUIDELINE ADHERENCE
EARLY (YOUNG) CAREER.K. Pereverzeva
Ryazan State Medical University, Ryazan, Russian Federation
Background and Aims: Prescribing antithrombotic therapy (ATT) for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and myocardial infarction (MI) remains a complex and evolving challenge in clinical practice. Aim: To evaluate trends in ATT prescriptions at hospital discharge for patients with AF and MI from 2016 to 2023, and to assess adherence to relevant clinical guidelines.
Methods: We conducted a retrospective analysis of data from 813 patients, stratified by year of hospitalization. Guideline adherence was assessed according to the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines before 2020 and the Russian Society of Cardiology (RSC) guidelines thereafter.
Results: The use of oral anticoagulants (OACs) increased from 16.3% (2016–2017) to 87.9% (2022–2023). In non-PCI patients, the combination of OAC and antiplatelet therapy was prescribed in 10.2% (2016–2017) and 13.5% (2018–2019) of cases. Among post-PCI patients, the use of triple therapy rose from 9.1% (2016–2017) to 51.0% (2018–2019), in line with ESC guidelines. From 2020 onward, the appropriate combination of OAC and antiplatelet therapy in non-PCI patients increased from 17.2% (2020–2021) to 27.5% (2022–2023). In patients with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) after PCI, triple therapy was prescribed in 48.7% (2020–2021) and 72.5% (2022–2023) of cases, consistent with RSC guidelines. In ST-elevation MI (STEMI) patients post-PCI, the OAC-antiplatelet combination was used in 13.3% (2020–2021) and 8.6% (2022–2023), also in accordance with recommendations.
Conclusions: This study highlights a persistent gap between clinical practice and guideline-recommended antithrombotic strategies for patients with AF and MI at hospital discharge, especially regarding combination therapy.

EARLY (YOUNG) CAREER.F. Smith, J. Beauchamp, C. Katigbak
UTHealth Houston Cizik School of Nursing, Research, Houston, United States of America
Background and Aims: Hispanic/Latino-a/x individuals in the United States (U.S.) are projected to experience the greatest increase in overall stroke prevalence among all ethnic groups. They are also more likely to arrive at the hospital later than White individuals following the onset of stroke symptoms. This review aimed to synthesize existing evidence on acute stroke care-seeking behaviors within the context of Hispanic cultural influences.
Methods: An integrative review was conducted in September 2024, using the search terms stroke, Hispanic or Latin, culture, emergency, and care seeking. Full-text, English-language publications indexed in PubMed, CINAHL, and Web of Science were reviewed. Studies were included if they examined emergency stroke care-seeking behaviors and explored aspects of Hispanic/Latino-a/x culture within the U.S.
Results: A total of 66 publications were initially identified, of which seven met the pre-defined inclusion criteria. All studies included were published after 2006, with six utilizing quantitative methodological approaches. Substantial heterogeneity was observed in the sociocultural constructs assessed across studies, with sociodemographics variables being the most consistently examined. Care-seeking behaviors were measured using various data collection instruments, including the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System questionnaire and the National Health Interview Survey.
Conclusions: Since 2006, research on care-seeking behaviors for stroke among the U.S. Hispanic/Latino-a/x population has expanded, with findings indicating that limited English proficiency, first-generation immigrant status, and lower household income are associated with delayed timeliness to seeking emergency stroke care. This review highlights the need for more comprehensive investigations into the cultural determinants that influence stroke-related care-seeking behaviors within Hispanic/Latino-a/x communities.

MULTIMORBIDITY CLUSTERS AND STROKE MORTALITY: A MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH USING ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORDS
EPIDEMIOLOGY.T. Asatryan1, Y. Hbid2, A. Douiri3
1King’s College London, London, United Kingdom, 2Imperial College London, London, United Kingdom, 3King’s College London, Population Health Department, London, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Stroke is a leading cause of premature mortality worldwide. As multimorbidity further complicates post-stroke care— contributing to reduced quality of life and worse outcomes, we aimed to explore multimorbidity among stroke patients and its impact on all-cause stroke mortality.
Methods: We used electronic health records from 9,846 incident stroke cases in South London (2005–2022), including data on 33 long-term conditions. To explore multimorbidity patterns, we identified the top comorbidities associated with stroke mortality using the Random Forest method, followed by Classification and Regression Tree (CART) analysis to define comorbidity clusters. Each cluster’s hazard ratio (HR) was estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model, adjusted for age, sex, ethnicity, and deprivation level (IMD 2019). Survival differences between clusters were assessed using Kaplan–Meier curves and post hoc pairwise log-rank tests. Bootstrapping was used to internally validate Random Forest performance and assess the stability of variable importance across resampled datasets, while the hyperparameters and robustness of the CART model were evaluated through nested 10-fold cross-validation.
Results: The adjusted HRs for clusters significantly associated with stroke mortality were: cancer and heart failure (aHR 1.74; 95%CI: 1.16–2.60); cancer and peripheral artery disease (1.66; [1.07–2.57]); and COPD and hypertension (1.52; [1.10–2.10]). Clusters including chronic kidney disease (CKD) with heart failure and moderate obesity (1.37; [0.91–2.10]), and CKD with coronary heart disease (1.30; [0.90–1.86]) were not statistically significant.
Conclusions: These findings suggest statistically and clinically meaningful multimorbidity patterns: stroke patients with non-cardiometabolic conditions, particularly cancer and COPD, faced significantly higher mortality risks, highlighting the need for targeted, condition-specific preventive strategies.

EPIDEMIOLOGY.H.-Y. Hsu, Y.-M. Chiu
Tungs’ Taichung MetroHarbor Hospital, Neurology, Taichung, Taiwan
Background and Aims: Patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) have significant adverse impacts on survival throughout the life course. Among these patients, those with prior ischemic stroke (IS) demonstrate significantly higher rates of future thromboembolism and mortality compared to AF patients without IS. The lifetime risk and disease burden of AF and IS across the entire lifespan are rarely quantified in an easily understandable way.
Methods: Using Taiwan’s National Health Insurance database (1999-2021), we estimated survival functions for AF patients with and without IS, extrapolating to lifetime using a rolling-over algorithm. We simulated matched referents from vital statistics to calculate life expectancy (LE) and loss of LE (LoLE).
Results: From 1999 to 2021, 619,147 new AF cases were identified. Among these patients, 112,154 (18.11%) patients had previous IS. Conclusions: Atrial fibrillation significantly reduces life expectancy, with more pronounced effects in patients with prior IS. These findings highlight the substantial impact of stroke on survival outcomes in AF patients and underscore the importance of effective stroke prevention strategies in AF patients.

ASSOCIATIONS OF BODY ROUNDNESS INDEX WITH ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES: THE PROSPECTIVE URBAN RURAL EPIDEMIOLOGY (PURE)-CHINA STUDY
EPIDEMIOLOGY.X. Liu, W. Li
National Center for Cardiovascular Diseases, Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College, Medical Research And Biometrics Center, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: To determine the impact of body roundness index (BRI) on cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and mortality in Chinese adults.
Methods: The PURE-China study recruited 47931 participants aged 35-70 years from 12 provinces of China between 2005 and 2009. The BRI was calculated based on height and waist circumference. The primary outcomes were major CVD events (stroke, myocardial infarction( MI), or heart failure( HF)), CVD mortality, and all-cause mortality. Cox proportional hazards frailty models and restricted cubic splines were used to analyze the associations between BRI and the primary outcomes.
Results: Of 45864 participants included in this study, we documented 2659 deaths( 960 CVD deaths) and 4280 major CVD events( 2828 stroke, 1134 MI and 318 HF) with a median follow-up of 11.9 years. A monotonic increasing dose-response association was observed between BRI and CVD risk, while BRI and all-cause mortality and CVD mortality exhibited a U-shaped relationship, with the nadir at a BRI of 3.27 and 3.01 respectively. In full adjusted model, one standard deviation(SD) increase in BRI was related to a higher risk of major CVD events (HR=1.18, 95%CI:1.15-1.22), stroke (HR=1.19, 95%CI:1.15-1.23), MI (HR=1.20, 95%CI:1.14-1.27). For mortality, participants were stratified by the U-curve nadir into low- and high-BRI groups. In the low-BRI group, each SD increase was associated with reduced all-cause mortality (HR=0.86, 95%CI:0.74-0.99) and CVD mortality (HR=0.82, 95%CI:0.61-1.10). Conversely, in the high-BRI group, each SD increase predicted higher all-cause mortality (HR=1.15, 95%CI:1.09-1.22) and CVD mortality (HR=1.27, 95%CI:1.18-1.37).
Conclusions: BRI were significantly associated with the risk of CVD and mortality.

Background and Aims: Climatic factors have been increasingly recognized as potential modifiers of stroke epidemiology. However, data from sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce. This study aimed to investigate the association between weather parameters and stroke
Methods: A retrospective review of medical records from three referral hospitals in Douala between 2011, and 2020. Adults aged ⩾18 years with neuroimaging-confirmed ischemic (I-stroke) or hemorrhagic stroke (H-stroke) were included. Weather data (temperature, humidity, wind speed, precipitation, atmospheric pressure, and sunshine duration) were obtained from the national meteorological agency (ASECNA). Statistical analysis involved multivariate logistic regression to identify weather-related factors associated with stroke occurrence and outcomes.

Conclusions: In Douala, stroke occurrence and outcomes are influenced by seasonal and meteorological factors. Public health strategies and clinical protocols should integrate weather awareness to improve stroke prevention and management, particularly in tropical environments with distinct seasonal patterns.

Methods: All patients admitted to the neurology ward between January 2023 and March 2025 were included. Demographic profile, risk factors, clinical features, type and extent of stroke, complications and outcome were noted. Outcome was assessed according to modified Rankins score(mRS) at discharge, with poor outcome mRS 4-6. Predictors of mortality and poor outcome were calculated. Statistical analysis was carried out using SPSS software.
Results: The study included 346 patients, aged 3 to 97 years (55.88±16.91) with 218(63%) males. Ischemic stroke was most common(58.1%) followed by hemorrhagic stroke(37.5) and venous stroke(4.4%). Nearly 63(18.2%) patients had recurrent stroke. The GCS score at admission was 12.47±3.22 (3-15). Ischemic stroke was most commonly due to atherosclerosis(65.8%), though 17.1% were cardioembolic, 6% tuberculous meningitis-related, 5% secondary to vasculitis and 3.5% cryptogenic. Twenty three patients had atrial fibrillation. Thirty two(9.2%) patients died, while 31% had good outcome (mRS 0-3). GCS<9, male sex, age>60 years, high admission leucocyte counts, high HbA1c levels and comorbidities were predictors of poor outcome. Poor GCS, older age and comorbidities were independent predictors of poor outcome.
Conclusions: Nearly 37% patients had hemorrhagic stroke, and overall mortality was 9.2%.

ASSOCIATION BETWEEN AMBIENT TEMPERATURE AND RISK OF ISCHAEMIC STROKE: AN OBSERVATIONAL COHORT STUDY
EPIDEMIOLOGY.R. Matsuo1, H. Motomura1, F. Irie1, Y. Wakisaka2, M. Kamouchi1, T. Ago2
1Kyushu University, Department Of Health Care Administration And Management, Graduate School Of Medical Sciences, Fukuoka, Japan, 2Kyushu University, Department Of Medicine And Clinical Science, Graduate School Of Medical Sciences, Fukuoka, Japan
Background and Aims: The influence of ambient temperature on the risk of stroke has remained unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between ambient temperature and the risk of ischaemic stroke from various aetiologies.
Methods: We investigated the onset of acute ischaemic stroke in the prospective stroke registry conducted from October 2007–September 2019 in Fukuoka, Japan. Stroke aetiology was classified into cardioembolism (CE), large-artery atherosclerosis (LAA), small-vessel occlusion (SVO), and other aetiologies. Hourly, maximum, and minimum temperature data were obtained from the Japan Meteorological Agency. After controlling for the nonlinear and delayed effects of daily average temperature, we employed a quasi-Poisson generalised additive model with the natural logarithm of daily stroke counts as a function of predictors, including temperature metrics and humidity.
Results: A total of 17,755 patients with acute ischaemic stroke (mean age ± SD: 73.1 ± 12.6 years; 41.4% female) were included in the analysis. Lower temperatures were associated with an increased risk of CE and LAA but not with that of SVO. Conversely, higher temperatures were associated with a decreased risk of CE, whereas no association was found with LAA or SVO. The association was observed within 5 days before stroke onset for LAA but after a longer period for CE. The risk of CE increased with rising variability in daily temperature preceding stroke onset.
Conclusions: We observed distinct associations between ambient temperature and the risk of ischaemic stroke, contingent upon stroke aetiology, temperature levels, exposure duration, and patient characteristics.

A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF CAUSAL PATHWAYS OF SOCIOECONOMIC INEQUALITIES IN STROKE
EPIDEMIOLOGY.C. Pantoja1, L. Liu1, M. Soley-Bori1, W. Kalansooriya1, E. Emmet1, A. Douiri1, Y. Wang1, A. Bhalla2, A. Khanolkar1, D. Parmar1, S. Landau3, M. O’Connell1, C. Wolfe1, I. Marshall1
1King’s College London, Population Health Department, London, United Kingdom, 2Guys and St Thomas NHS Foundation Trust, London, United Kingdom, 3King’s College London, Institute Of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience, London, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Socioeconomic status (SES) strongly influences stroke incidence, disability, and mortality, but the causal mechanisms remain unclear. This systematic review synthesises evidence from studies using causal mediation approaches to quantify pathways driving SES-related stroke inequalities.
Methods: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematically reviewed observational studies applying causal mediation methods to assess pathways between SES and stroke outcomes (PROSPERO CRD42024554285). Searches in PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar identified relevant studies. Data extraction captured study settings, SES indicators, stroke outcomes, and mediators. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E, and evidence certainty was evaluated with an adapted GRADE approach.
Results: From 11,196 records, 17 studies from predominantly high-income countries met inclusion criteria. Hypertension emerged as the strongest mediator of stroke risk (14-28% mediation, moderate certainty), while smoking showed substantial effects (up to 19.9%, very low certainty). For post-stroke inequalities at three months, stroke severity was the primary mediator (38-94%), which itself was influenced by cardiovascular risk factors. Lower SES patients had reduced access to thrombolysis and stroke units, mediating 2.7-5% of short-term outcome inequalities, primarily due to greater geographical distance to specialized centers (48%). Longer-term inequalities (⩾6 months) were mediated by hypertension, smoking, diabetes, and healthcare access.
Conclusions: This review identifies modifiable pathways through which SES influences stroke risk and outcomes. Targeted interventions for hypertension management, smoking cessation, and equitable acute care access could substantially reduce SES-related stroke inequalities. Further research is needed in low/middle-income countries and on emerging pathways including early-life SES, environmental exposures, and care quality.

Background and Aims: Conducting acute stroke trials presents unique challenges that impact the success and efficiency of these studies. This research explores major obstacles in recruitment and trial management, aiming to provide actionable recommendations for improving these areas.

Methods: The study participants were stroke patients admitted during the period of June 2023 to December 2024. Relevant data was recorded by reviewing the patients and their medical records. NIHSS (National Institute of Health Stroke Scale) and mRS (modified Rankin scale) scores were calculated.
Results: Of the 706 stroke patients, 69% were male. The mean age was 59.6 ± 12.8 years. Ischemic stroke was most common (84.4%). Posterior circulation strokes (51.4%) were more frequent. ICAD was seen in 49.3%. Commonest risk factor was hypertension (64%). Mean NIHSS was 7.99 ± 7.05. The mRS improved from 2.62 ± 1.49 at admission to 1.61 ± 1.29 after three months. Thrombolysis and thrombectomy were performed in only 6.6% and 3%, respectively.
Conclusions: This study reveals a distinct clinical pattern of stroke in the Kongu district, with a higher prevalence of ischemic strokes and a predominance of small vessel disease. Notably, posterior circulation strokes were more common—a finding that contrasts with international literature. The mean patient age of 59.6 years suggests an earlier onset compared to Western populations. Additionally, the low rates of thrombolysis and thrombectomy highlight the ongoing challenges in acute stroke intervention access in resource-limited settings. Despite this, significant functional recovery was observed over three months, as reflected by the improvement in mRS scores.

INCIDENCE, RISK FACTORS, AND OUTCOMES OF STROKE FOLLOWING HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
EPIDEMIOLOGY.P.N.K. Pitchan Velammal1, T. Dhasakeerthi2, H.S. Veerachamy1
1Tirunelveli Medical College, Tirunelveli, India, 2UAMS, Neurology, Little Rock, United States of America
Background and Aims: Stroke is a rare but major risk associated with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). We performed a meta-analysis to estimate the pooled stroke incidence, identify associated risk factors, and clinical outcomes following HSCT.
Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 16 studies comprising 24,871 HSCT patients was performed. Random-effects models were used to calculate pooled incidence rates and 95% confidence intervals for stroke subtypes. Subgroup analyses were conducted for allogeneic HSCT. Risk factors were extracted from multivariable models
Results: Among 24,871 patients, the pooled incidence of stroke post-HSCT was 2.48% (95% CI: 2.28%–2.67%). Ischemic stroke was more prevalent (3.28%, 95% CI: 2.30%–4.25%) than hemorrhagic stroke (1.90%, 95% CI: 1.62%–2.13%) (Fig-1). In allo-HSCT recipients (n = 7,989), the pooled ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke rates were 1.48% and 1.38%, respectively (Fig-2). Most strokes (68.5%) occurred within the first 100 days, with median onset at 137 days for ischemic and 161 days for hemorrhagic events.. Significant risk factors included grade III–IV acute graft-versus-host disease, thrombotic microangiopathy (HR: 10.30), delayed platelet engraftment, hypertension, prior thromboembolism, and exposure to alkylating agents or radiation. Exercise reduced ischemic stroke risk (HR: 0.5) (Fig-3). Stroke was associated with poor survival; affected patients had lower 5-year survival (17.9%–37%) versus those without stroke (up to 55.8%).

Conclusions: Both ischemic and hemorrhagic strokes are uncommon but can be serious complications of HSCT. Hemorrhagic strokes usually occur earlier and are associated with worse prognosis. Significant modifiable and transplant-related risk factors have been identified in high-risk HSCT populations, providing potential targets for risk classification and preventative strategies.

Department of Epidemiology, School of Public Health, Suzhou Medical College of Soochow University, Suzhou, China
Background and Aims: Fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) is a known risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, but its relationship with ischemic stroke outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between serum FABP4 levels and the outcomes of ischemic stroke after 3-month period.
Methods: This prospective study included 3,465 patients with ischemic stroke from the CATIS (China Antihypertensive Trial in Acute Ischemic Stroke) who had their FABP4 levels measured. The primary outcome was a composite of death and major disability (modified Rankin Scale score ⩾ 3) at the 3-month follow-up. Cox proportional hazards and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to evaluate the association between serum FABP4 and adverse outcomes.
Results: At the 3-month follow-up, 853 patients (24.62%) experienced the primary outcomes. CARDIOVASCULAR RISK AMONG STROKE SURVIVORS WITH COMBUSTIBLE TOBACCO AND ELECTRONIC CIGARETTES: NATIONWIDE COHORT STUDY IN KOREAN MEN
EPIDEMIOLOGY.J. Yoo, J. Jeon, M. Baik, J. Kim
Yonsei University College of Medicine, Neurology, Seoul, Korea, Republic of
Background and Aims: Although the use of electronic cigarettes (e-cigarettes) has been increasing, its impact on cardiovascular disease development remains unclear, especially among stroke survivors. We aimed to compare the incidence of major cardiovascular events according to different smoking habits (non-smokers, combustible cigarette smokers, and e-cigarette users) in stroke survivors.
Methods: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted of Korean men diagnosed with acute stroke who underwent national health checkups within 3 years following their stroke between 2018 and 2022. Patients were categorized into three groups based on smoking status: non-smokers, combustible cigarette smokers, and e-cigarette users. The primary outcome was a composite of stroke and myocardial infarction. Slovak Medical University, Bratislava, Slovak Republic
Background and Aims: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability, significantly impacting healthcare systems and economies. Methods: A retrospective, population-based analysis of stroke-related costs was performed from third-party payer and societal perspectives. Data was sourced from oficial sources and Social Insurance Agency. Costs were classified as direct medical and indirect.
Results: Between 2015 and 2019, total stroke prevalence increased by 21%, reaching 199,508 cases in 2019. The total direct costs of stroke rose from €57.4 million in 2015 to €85.8 million in 2019. Hospitalization remained the primary cost driver, growing from 47.2% (€27.1 million) in 2015 to 54.3% (€46.6 million) in 2019. Diagnostic costs represented 37% of the direct costs in 2019, with treatment costs decreasing from 13.8% in 2015 to 8.7% in 2019. Total indirect costs amounted to €12.2 million over five years, with absenteeism peaking at €568,574 in 2018. Cerebral infarction accounted for approximately 53.3% of absenteeism-related costs and 43.1% of disability-related costs.
Conclusions: Stroke imposes a significant and growing economic burden in Slovakia, with hospitalization identified as the primary cost driver. The observed rise in stroke prevalence and associated economic costs underscores the urgent need for enhanced stroke prevention, early detection, and effective treatment strategies. Optimizing management and preventive measures may offer substantial economic savings and improved patient outcomes.
