A COMPUTATIONAL MATERIAL MODEL FOR THE TENSILE AND COMPRESSIVE BEHAVIOUR OF FIBRIN NETWORKS APPLIED TO THE SIMULATION OF ASPIRATION THROMBECTOMY
THROMBECTOMY.K. Bein Snee1, R. Mccarthy2, P. Mcgarry1
1Biomedical Engineering, University of Galway, Galway, Ireland, 2Johnson & Johnson MedTech Neurovascular, Galway, Ireland
Background and Aims: Traditional computational models for fibre-reinforced soft tissues assume that wavy fibres buckle when shortened and therefore cannot support compressive stress. However, compression-tension experiments of pure fibrin clots suggest that fibrin can support both tensile and compressive stress. We develop a model where fibre shortening results in the development of compressive axial fibre stress (compression-tension fibre (CTF) model). This model is validated by replicating aspiration thrombectomy experiments.
Methods: Firstly, we demonstrate that the simple extension of existing fibre formulations to the compressive regime results in unphysical softening and we propose a novel fibre constitutive law (CTF model) which prevents such softening (Figure 1). This allows us to model fibrin networks without adding an artificial isotropic matrix component. To model a blood clot, we construct a network of discrete fibres in which the mechanical behaviour of each fibre is described by our novel constitutive law. The model is calibrated using experimental data for 0%, 5%, 20% and 40% hematocrit platelet-contracted clots (Figure 2).

Results: Simulations correctly predict the experimental lodgement position of clots in a vessel mimic (Figure 3A). Furthermore, simulations match experimentally observed ingestion lengths of tough clots into the aspiration catheter (Figure 3B) and predict the fracture of friable clots due to fibre extension beyond the fracture strain seen in tensile experiments (Figure 3C).

Conclusions: This novel physically-based clot material model provides new insights into blood clot biomechanical behaviour that can be incorporated into the design of thrombectomy devices. Joint funding by Research Ireland (EPSPG/2022/379) and Johnson & Johnson MedTech Neurovascular (Neurvai Ltd.).

EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF ENDOVASCULAR THROMBECTOMY IN PREGNANT WOMEN WITH LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION STROKE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
THROMBECTOMY.N. Aderinto1, I. Abraham2, E. Egbunu3, A. Gaur4, E. Ibitunde5, P. Kingdom6, B. Joshi7, A. Hasan8, E. Kokori9, G. Olatunji9, A. Ogwuche2, P. Bolaji10
1LADOKE AKINTOLA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY, Ogbomoso, Nigeria, 2Department of Medicine and Surgery, University of Ilorin, Ilorin, Nigeria, 3Federal Medical Centre, Internal Medicine, Bida, Nigeria, 4Yeovil District Hospital, Somerset NHS Foundation Trust, Yeovil, United Kingdom, 5University of Ibadan, Ibadan, Nigeria, 6Babcock University, Ilishan-Remo, Nigeria, 7Dorset County Hospital, Internal Medicine, Dorchester, Dorset, United Kingdom, 8University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, Nigeria, 9³Department of Medicine and Surgery, University of Ilorin, Ilorin, Nigeria, 10Dorset County Hospital NHS Foundation Trust UK, Dorchester, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Endovascular thrombectomy (ET) is a standard treatment for LVO stroke in the general population. Still, its efficacy and safety in pregnant women remain uncertain due to limited evidence and concerns about radiation exposure and maternal-fetal outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of ET in pregnant women with LVO stroke, focusing on functional outcomes, maternal complications, and fetal outcomes.
Methods: We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to February 2025 identified studies on ET in pregnant or postpartum women with LVO stroke. Eligible studies included clinical studies, case reports, and case series. Data on functional independence, maternal complications, and fetal outcomes were extracted. A proportional meta-analysis assessed efficacy, with narrative synthesis for safety and fetal outcomes. Quality was evaluated using ROBINS-I and JBI tools. Publication bias was assessed via funnel plot and Egger’s test.
Results: Eight studies were included. A pooled estimate showed 89% functional independence post-ET. Maternal complications included ICH (11%), VTE (17%), and pregnancy-related issues (44%) in the largest study (n=180); smaller studies reported minimal complications. Fetal outcomes were inconsistently reported, with term/preterm deliveries and one miscarriage noted. Radiation mitigation strategies were used in some cases. Publication bias was evident, with smaller studies likely overestimating efficacy.
Conclusions: ET appears effective for LVO stroke in pregnancy, with high rates of functional independence. However, maternal and fetal safety data are limited, and publication bias may inflate efficacy estimates. Standardized reporting and larger studies are needed to guide clinical decision-making in this population.

CEREBROPROTECTION IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE: PERSPECTIVES ON COMBINING CEREBROLYSIN WITH RECANALIZATION THERAPY
THROMBECTOMY.N. Bornstein1, J. Staszewski2, Z. Poljakovic3, M. Kalinin4, D. Khasanova5, A. Elbassiouny6
1Tel-Aviv University, Sackler Faculty Of Medicine, Tel-Aviv, Israel, 2Military Institute of Medicine - National Research Institute, Clinic Of Neurology, Warsaw, Poland, 3Medical School, Zagreb University, Departement Of Neurology, Zagreb, Croatia, 4Interregional Clinical Diagnostic Center, Neurology, Kazan, Russian Federation, 5Kazan State Medical University, Neurology, Kazan, Russian Federation, 6Ain Shams University, Departmetn Of Neurology, Cairo, Egypt
Background and Aims: Current reperfusion therapies for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) are limited in efficacy, with recanalization achieved in only 50% of patients. Safe adjunctive therapy strategies are therefore needed to improve AIS outcomes.
Methods: The CERECAP (Cerebrolysin Recanalization and Reperfusion) initiative investigates the potential of Cerebrolysin, a multimodal neuropeptide preparation, as an adjunctive therapy to standard AIS reperfusion treatments in more than 15 investigator-initiated studies. Across multiple CERECAP studies, patients receive 30 ml/day of Cerebrolysin for 10 to 21 days, initiated immediately after administration of rtPA or performance of mechanical thrombectomy. Secondary endpoints include the incidence of hemorrhagic transformation, early neurological improvement (Day 7), and all-cause mortality.

All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Neurology, New Delhi, India
Background and Aims: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) due to large vessel occlusion (LVO), but its role in distal medium vessel occlusions (DMVOs) remains unclear. The proportion of ischemic stroke patients that receive this treatment in Canada is less than optimal. As well there is disparity between rural/remote communities and large urban centres. The aim of this study is to develop key change strategies to lower Door-In-Door-Out (DIDO) times for patients transferred for EVT.
Methods: As part of the national OPTIMISING ACCESS initiative, a subgroup of the National Roundtable was created with the aim of developing a list of key strategies to lower DIDO times using both evidence and experience. The sub-group includes emergency physicians, transport physicians, stroke administrators, and stroke neurologists.
Results: The current list of strategies to reduce DIDO times include: 1) pre-notification to EVT Centre and transport service of suspected large vessel occlusion (LVO) prior to arriving at Primary Stroke Centre; 2) fast or pre-registration; 3) keeping patient on EMS stretcher to CT; 4) rapid access to CT images; 5) using same ambulance for transfer when LVO screen is positive; 6) initiating thrombolysis in imaging area; and 7) use of Tenecteplase rather than tPA.
Conclusions: A list of evidence-based strategies to lower DIDO times can then be used to initiate a national quality improvement initiative.
EV658 / #2401
EFFICACY OF MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY AFTER SYSTEMIC THROMBOLYSIS IN THE TREATMENT OF ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE: RETROSPECTIVE ANALYSIS OF SUCCES RATE AND PROGNOSTIC FACTORS
THROMBECTOMY.T. Stupac, I. Preguza, V. Spinei, A. Levca, O. Grosu
Institute of Neurology and Neurosurgery, Chisinau, Moldova, Chișinău, Moldova
Background and Aims: Ischemic stroke is a major global neurological emergency, where rapid therapeutic interventions such as systemic thrombolysis (rtPA) and mechanical thrombectomy (MT) are essential to reduce disability and mortality. This study evaluates the efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy after systemic thrombolysis versus monotherapy in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and identifies prognostic factors for favorable outcomes.
Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 259 patients with AIS treated at the Institute of Neurology and Neurosurgery (2019-2023), divided into three groups: thrombolysis (n=126), thrombectomy (n=86), and combined therapy (n=47). We assessed recanalization rate (TICI 2b-3), NIHSS score improvement at 24 hours, and functional status at 90 days (mRS ⩽2).
Results: Complete recanalization rate was superior in the combined therapy group (76.6%) compared to thrombolysis (51.6%) or thrombectomy (65.1%), p<0.001. Mean NIHSS score improvement at 24 hours was 8.1 points for combined therapy versus 5.4 (thrombolysis) and 6.7 (thrombectomy), p=0.003. Favorable outcome at 90 days was present in 68.1% of patients with combined therapy, 47.6% with thrombolysis, and 55.8% with thrombectomy (p<0.001). Optimal prognostic factors included: age <70 years, ASPECTS >7, time to recanalization <240 min. Hemorrhagic complications were similar across groups. Others prognostic factors like NIHSS at stroke onset and comorbidities were not controlled and would be considered in future studies.
Conclusions: Combined treatment offers superior results in AIS with large vessel occlusions compared to monotherapy. Favorable prognosis is associated with younger age, higher ASPECTS score, and faster achievement of recanalization for a positive outcome. Early identification of eligible patients and rapid intervention are essential for therapeutic success.

PRIMARY RESULTS OF THE GRASSROOT INDIA TRIAL (GRAVITY STENT-RETRIEVER SYSTEM FOR REPERFUSION OF LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION STROKE)
THROMBECTOMY.D. Yavagal1, D. Vibha2, S. Giragani3, S. Narayan4, M. Sharma5, S. Vankayalapati6, A. Mehta7, S. Desai8, A. Jadhav9, K. Atchaneeyasakul10, S.B. Gaikwad11
1University of Miami/Jackson Health System, Miami, FL, USA, Neurology, Miami, United States of America, 2All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Neurology, New Delhi, India, 3Apollo Hospital, Interventional Neuroradiology, Hyderabad, India, 4Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research, Dhanvanthri Nagar, Pondicherry-6, Neurology, Pondicherry, India, 5Marengo CIMS Hospital, Neurology, Ahmedabad, India, 6Yashoda Hospitals, Somajiguda, India, 7Mount Sinai School of Medicine, Interventional Neuroradiology, New York City, United States of America, 8HonorHealth, Neurology, Scottsdale, United States of America, 9Barrow Neurological Institute, Neurosurgery, Scottsdale, United States of America, 10Mission Thrombectomy, Seattle, United States of America, 11All India Institute of Medical Sciences, Department Of Neuroimaging & Interventional Neuroradiology, NEW DELHI, India
Background and Aims: Access to mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) secondary to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is severely restricted in resource-constrained environments, primarily due to the prohibitive cost of existing approved devices. The GRASSROOT trial is the first study in a low-and-middle-income country (LMIC) setting, assessing the safety and efficacy of the novel Supernova stent-retriever—engineered with a value-based approach for improved performance across diverse patient populations.
Methods: A prospective, single-arm, multicenter trial in India enrolled patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) due to internal carotid artery terminus, M1/M2 middle cerebral artery, or vertebrobasilar artery occlusions presenting within 24-hours of symptom onset. Primary safety endpoints were symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) within 24-hours and all-cause mortality at 90-days. Primary efficacy endpoint was successful reperfusion (mTICI⩾2b), with a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0–2 serving as the secondary efficacy endpoint.
Results: Thirty-two consecutive eligible patients (mean age 58±16 years; 31% female; median NIHSS 14, ASPECTS 8) were enrolled. Successful reperfusion (mTICI⩾2b) after 1-3 passes of the Supernova stentriever [median=1(1-3)] was achieved in 93.8% of patients without need for adjunctive rescue therapy. First pass recanalization was observed in 68.8% of patients. 90-day mortality was 9.4%, and sICH rate was 3.1%. Rate of 90-day mRS 0-2 was 46.4% (13/28)(complete results at presentation). No device-related deficiencies or complications were observed.
Conclusions: The GRASSROOT trial demonstrates the safety and efficacy of the Supernova stent-retriever. High rate of recanalization along with value-based pricing represent a significant advancement in stroke care in India and other LMICs.
EV660 / #2334
INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS IN WAKE-UP AND UNKNOWN-ONSET ISCHEMIC STROKE SELECTED BY CT-BASED IMAGING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
THROMBOLYSIS.H. Atwan, M. Gamal
Faculty of Medicine, Assiut university, Assiut, Egypt
Background and Aims: Wake-up stroke (WUS) and stroke of unknown onset (SUO) are often excluded from intravenous thrombolysis (IV tPA) due to unclear onset times. CT-based imaging, however, allows patient selection based on tissue viability rather than time. This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of IV tPA in WUS and SUO patients selected by CT-based imaging.
Methods: We conducted a systematic review of randomized and nonrandomized studies assessing IV tPA in adults with WUS or SUO, using CT-based imaging (noncontrast CT, CT angiography, or CT perfusion). The primary outcome was a favorable functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale 0–2). Secondary outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) and mortality.

Results: Fourteen studies with 3,666 patients were included. All studies used CT-based imaging, with three utilizing CT perfusion. Among patients receiving IV tPA, 53% achieved favorable outcomes at 90 days (95% CI: 46%–60%). The relative risk (RR) of a good outcome compared to controls was 1.04 (95% CI: 0.95–1.15). sICH occurred in 3% of patients (95% CI: 2%–4%), with an RR of 1.29 (95% CI: 0.58–2.87). The 90-day mortality rate was 11% (95% CI: 9%–13%), with an RR of 0.98 (95% CI: 0.71–1.36) compared to controls.

Conclusions: IV thrombolysis in WUS and SUO selected by CT-based imaging is associated with modest improvements in functional outcomes, a low rate of sICH, and comparable mortality to controls. These findings support expanding the use of IV tPA based on imaging-guided selection, potentially benefiting more patients with uncertain stroke onset timing.
EV661 / #2476
INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS IN WAKE-UP AND UNKNOWN-ONSET ISCHEMIC STROKE SELECTED BY MRI-BASED IMAGING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
THROMBOLYSIS.H. Atwan, M. Gamal
Faculty of Medicine, Assiut university, Assiut, Egypt
Background and Aims: WUS and SUO are excluded from IV tPA due to uncertain timing. MRI-based imaging, particularly DWI and FLAIR mismatch, allows selection based on tissue viability rather than time. This study evaluates the safety and efficacy of IV tPA in MRI-selected WUS and SUO patients, focusing on functional outcomes, sICH, and mortality rates.
Methods: We conducted a systematic review of randomized and nonrandomized studies assessing IV tPA in adults with WUS or SUO, using MRI-based selection (e.g., DWI/FLAIR mismatch or perfusion-weighted imaging). The primary outcome was a favorable functional outcome at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0–2. Secondary outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality.
Results: Eleven studies comprising 1,831 patients were included. All studies employed MRI-based selection criteria, with several incorporating advanced perfusion imaging. Among patients receiving IV tPA, 54% achieved favorable functional outcomes at 90 days (95% CI: 44%–62%). The relative risk (RR) of a good outcome compared to controls was 1.13 (95% CI: 1.04–1.24). The incidence of sICH was 1% (95% CI: 1%–2%), with an RR of 2.66 (95% CI: 1.00–7.11). The 90-day mortality rate was 3% (95% CI: %–4%), with an RR of 1.97 (95% CI: 1.05–3.70) compared to controls.

Conclusions: Intravenous thrombolysis in WUS and SUO patients selected using MRI-based imaging is associated with modest improvements in functional outcomes, a low incidence of sICH, and mortality rates comparable to controls. These findings support the use of MRI-guided selection for IV tPA in patients with unknown stroke onset.

IMPACT OF ATHEROSCLEROSIS SEVERITY ON CLINICAL RESPONSE TO INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS IN ISCHEMIC STROKE
THROMBOLYSIS.I. Ben Kraiem1, N. Bouattour2, N. Charfi3, K. Moalla2, S. Daoud3, S. Sakka2, H. Hadjkacem3, M. Damak2

Background and Aims: Atherosclerosis is a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, affecting both extracranial carotid and intracranial arteries. Early reperfusion through intravenous thrombolysis improves functional outcomes, although its efficacy may vary depending on the location and severity of vascular lesions. This study aimed to compare the clinical response to thrombolysis between patients with significant versus non-significant atherosclerotic involvement.
Methods: It was a descriptive and analytical study including patients admitted for ischemic stroke to the neurology department of CHU Habib Bourguiba Sfax who received intravenous thrombolysis. Patients were divided into two groups: Group 1 (G1) with significant extracranial carotid atherosclerosis (⩾50% stenosis), and Group 2 (G2) with either intracranial atherosclerosis or non-significant extracranial carotid lesions (<50%). Thrombolysis efficacy was assessed based on clinical improvement in the NIHSS score within the first 48h hours following treatment.
Results: The study included 22 patients who received thrombolysis. Male sex was predominant (M/F ratio: 1.75). Etiological work-up classified 8 patients in G1 and 14 in G2. Background and Aims: Treatment of acute stroke has its clear rules and established standards. We present the results of a multicenter retrospective study using prolonged low-dose intravenous thrombolysis.
Methods: The multicenter retrospective study ESR_PROLONG (2020-2024) included consecutive patients who were given intravenous thrombolysis (20 mg alteplase continuously for 10 hours) during an early (within hours after standard recanalization therapy) recurrence of ischemic stroke. Results: NIHSS is the strongest and statistically significant variable predicting the development of HT (OR = 1.23, p = 0.001).The risk of bleeding decreases significantly with every 1 point increase in ASPECT score. (OR = 0.32, p = 0.0008).As the lesion volume increases, the risk of developing HT increases significantly (p = 0.011). Diabetes mellitus (DM) (p = 0.022) and higher age (over 67)(p:0.023) are risk factors.
Conclusions: The significant relationship between HT and low ASPECT, high NIHSS and lesion maximal size indicates that stroke size is important for HT, independent of duration and other factors.

SAFETY AND EFFICACY OF INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYTICS AMONG PATIENTS WITH EMERGENT INTRACRANIAL STENTING: SUBANALYSIS OF THE RESISTANT REGISTRY
THROMBOLYSIS.A. Mujanovic1, M. Olive-Gadea2, F. Diana3, T. Meinel4, T. Dobrocky1, J. Gralla1, U. Fischer4, M. Ribo5, A. Tomasello3, M. Requena3, J. Kaesmacher1
1Rosenbühlgasse 25, Diagnostic And Interventional Neuroradiology, Bern, Switzerland, 2Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron, Neurology Department, Barcelona, Spain, 3Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron, Neuroradiology, Barcelona, Spain, 4Inselspital, University Hospital Bern, Bern, Switzerland, 5Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebrón, Stroke Unit, Department Of Neurology, Barcelona, Spain
Background and Aims: The value of pre-interventional intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke caused by an intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) and receiving endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) plus emergent intracranial stenting is unknown. We aimed to investigate the safety and efficacy of IVT among patients with adjuvant intracranial stenting after EVT.
Methods: RESISTANT is a study of consecutive stroke patients who underwent EVT and intracranial stenting from 36 comprehensive stroke centres in 7 countries. The primary outcome of interest was excellent outcome, measured with the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score 0-1. The secondary outcomes were functional independence (mRS 0-2) at 90-days and mRS shift. Safety outcomes were rates of symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage (sICH) and mortality. Adjusted multivariate ordinal and logistic regressions were used for all outcomes.
Results: Out of 828 patients (median age 67, IQR 59-77; 35% female), 23% (202/875) have received IVT. After adjustment, there was an association between receiving IVT and achieving excellent outcome (aOR 1.6, 95%CI 1.0 – 2.7). However, there was no significant association between IVT, mRS 0-2, nor mRS ordinal shift. There were also no differences in sICH rates at 24h (aOR 1.5, 95%CI 0.8 – 2.9), nor 90-day mortality.
Conclusions: In this multi-center study of patients who underwent EVT with emergent intracranial stenting, IVT was associated with excellent clinical outcome, possibly partially due to indication bias, and there were no safety concerns. Receiving IVT should not be a criterion for deferring acute stenting among patients with ICAD-associated LVO and IVT should not be routinely withheld in suspected ICAD cases.

COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF TENECTEPLASE AND ALTEPLASE FOR INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE MANAGEMENT ACROSS A STROKE NETWORK IN BOGOTÁ, COLOMBIA, FROM 2023 TO 2024
THROMBOLYSIS.J. Oyola1, H. Bayona1, C. Jimenez Monsalve1, J. Rivillas2, J. Perez3, E. Aguilar3, D. Cuestas3
1Subred Integrada de Servicios de Salud Norte, Bogotá, Colombia, 2Fundacion Valle del Lili, Neurology, Cali, Colombia, 3Semillero de Neuroepidemiología, Subred Norte, Bogotá, Colombia
Background and Aims: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is a leading cause of mortality and disability globally (1). Tenecteplase (TNK) offers advantages like single-bolus administration, higher fibrin specificity, and improved recanalization rates (2). In Colombia, off-label use faces barriers, emphasizing the need for local data to guide public health policy. This study compares AIS thrombolysis outcomes between TNK and alteplase.
Methods: Observational, analytic study of AIS patients treated with intravenous thrombolysis in Bogotá (2023–2024). Multivariable logistic regression was applied to compare baseline characteristics and outcomes.
Results: Data was collected from 233 patients, of which 58.1% were female. The mean (SD) age was 68 (15.6) years. The median (IQR) time in minutes from stroke onset to thrombolysis was 192 (130,275). The adjusted analysis of outcomes between TNK and Alteplase groups revealed no statistically significant differences in functional independence (mRS<3) (OR: 1.06, 95% CI: 0.47–2.42, p-value = 0.889) or symptomatic hemorrhage (OR: 1.46, 95% CI: 0.42–5.07, p-value = 0.553). Tenecteplase was associated with significantly higher odds of mortality (OR: 3.31, 95% CI: 1.24–8.81, p-value = 0.017). However, a subanalysis excluding patients thrombolysed beyond 4.5 hours resulted in an increased mortality risk without statistical significance OR: 2.95 (95% CI: 0.68–11.59, p-value = 0.070).
Conclusions: TNK showed no significant differences in functional independence or symptomatic hemorrhage compared to alteplase, but was associated with increased mortality risk. However, the association lost statistical significance when patients treated with thrombolysis after the 4.5-hour window were excluded. Further research is needed to guide clinical and public health strategies.
EV686 / #447
"TELESTROKE-ENABLED THROMBOLYSIS IN COMMUNITY HOSPITALS: IMPROVED FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES COMPARED TO STROKE CENTER-BASED TREATMENT"
THROMBOLYSIS.P. Papitak, K. Tussanabunyong
Kasetsart University, Medicine, Sakon Nakhon, Thailand
Background and Aims: Limited access to specialized stroke care delays rtPA administration. Telestroke enables thrombolysis in community hospitals, improving accessibility. This study compares outcomes between patients treated at a comprehensive stroke center and those treated via telestroke in the Sakon Nakhon stroke network.
Methods: A prospective cohort study (2019–2024) analyzed 457 acute ischemic stroke patients treated with intravenous rtPA: 262 at Sakon Nakhon Hospital and 195 at community hospitals. The primary outcome was favorable functional recovery (mRS 0–1) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included 24-hour improvement, post-thrombolysis intracranial hemorrhage (PT-ICH), treatment times, and length of stay. Generalized linear models identified factors associated with favorable outcomes.
Results: The telestroke group had a higher rate of favorable outcomes (74.36% vs. 57.2%; OR = 0.462, 95% CI: 0.31–0.69, p < 0.001) and greater 24-hour improvement (84.1% vs. 72.14%; OR = 1.50, 95% CI: 1.14–1.99, p = 0.04). No significant differences were found in mortality (3.1% vs. 4.6%; p = 0.41) or symptomatic ICH (4.6% vs. 7.3%; p = 0.152). Telestroke patients had a shorter hospital stay (5.09 ± 3.51 vs. 7.32 ± 6.57 days, p < 0.001). Independent predictors of favorable outcomes included younger age, higher ASPECTS score, shorter onset-to-door time, mechanical thrombectomy, lower initial NIHSS, and shorter hospital stay (p < 0.05 for all).
Conclusions: Telestroke for thrombolysis in community hospitals achieved comparable or superior functional outcomes and similar safety to treatment in a stroke center. It demonstrates efficacy and safety, supporting its role in expanding acute stroke care access, particularly in underserved regions.
EV687 / #1147
THE USE OF INTRA-ARTERIAL THROMBOLYSIS IN PATIENTS AFTER MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY: A REVIEW STUDY
THROMBOLYSIS.S. Gopalkrishnan, H. Danieli, S. Hasan, P. Raichur, N. Fakhri
University of Louisville, Neurology, Louisville, United States of America
Background and Aims: This systematic review examines intra-arterial thrombolysis as an adjunct to mechanical thrombectomy (MT), focusing on its impact on functional outcomes and safety.
Methods: Four studies were included in this review: CHOICE, ANGEL TNK, ALLY PILOT, and POST-TNK. Three published trials (CHOICE, ALLY PILOT and POST-TNK) and one trial presented at ISC 2025 (International Stroke Conference), ANGEL-TNK. A total of 936 patients with similar baseline characteristics were assessed.
Results: The studies collectively demonstrate a positive trend towards functional recovery with intra-arterial thrombolysis after MT. The CHOICE, ANGEL TNK, and ALLY PILOT studies reported good functional outcomes (mrs < or equal to 2) and showed no significant differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), or 90-day mortality. ANGEL TNK, despite a larger cohort, excluded patients with prior thrombolysis, while the smaller CHOICE and ALLY PILOT studies included them, increasing generalizability. The ALLY PILOT trial also demonstrated that adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis up to 4.5 mg was both feasible and safe following incomplete reperfusion for anterior circulation occlusions. However, the POST-TNK trial found no significant difference in functional recovery between groups receiving intra-arterial thrombolysis and controls.Regarding safety profile, it showed no difference in sICH or 90-day mortality which is similar to findings of CHOICE, ANGEL-TNK and ALLY PILOT. All trials excluded patients on anticoagulants or dual antiplatelet therapy.
Conclusions: Intra-arterial Thrombolysis after MT may improve neurological outcomes with a good safety profile. However, larger studies and randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings and identify ideal patient groups.
EV688 / #1159
TENECTEPLASE FOR TREATMENT OF ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE IN THE EXTENDED TIME WINDOW: A REVIEW OF CURRENT DATA
THROMBOLYSIS.S. Gopalkrishnan, H. Danieli, S. Hasan, P. Raichur
University of Louisville, Neurology, Louisville, United States of America
Background and Aims: Use of Tenecteplase (TNK) in the Extended Time Window (ETW) in Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS) remains an ongoing debate.
Methods: Systematic review of 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) — TIMELESS, TRACE 3, CHABLIS-T II — was conducted.
Results: 1,198 patients were enrolled. 603 received TNK, while 595 were controls. All 3 trials included patients with internal carotid and/or proximal middle cerebral artery occlusions; however, in TRACE 3, patients did not have access to endovascular thrombectomy. TIMELESS and CHABLIS-T II showed better recanalization in the TNK group; however, the median Modified Rankin Score was 3 at 90 days in both groups, demonstrating no benefit in clinical outcomes. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) was similar in the two groups. In TRACE 3, there was improvement in functional outcome at 90 days in the TNK group (33.0% vs. 24.2%), but the incidence of sICH was also higher (3.0% and 0.8%, respectively).
Conclusions: Better recanalization rates are seen with TNK in ETW; however, it may not be associated with improved functional outcome at 90 days compared with medical management. Incidence of sICH also remains largely favorable, except in TRACE 3, which showed higher incidence in the TNK group. There remains a need for more RCTs in this population.

FUNCTIONAL AND SAFETY COMPARISON OF TENECTEPLASE VS. ALTEPLASE IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE: REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE FROM A SECONDARY-LEVEL MEXICAN HOSPITAL
THROMBOLYSIS.M. Ramirez Conejo, G. Ramirez Caballero, V. Villarreal Arizpe
Tec Salud, Internal Medicine, Monterrey, Mexico
Background and Aims: Tenecteplase has been proposed as a pharmacologically favorable alternative to alteplase for intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). This study aimed to compare the functional effectiveness and safety of tenecteplase versus alteplase in AIS patients treated within the recommended therapeutic window
Methods: We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 71 patients with AIS who received intravenous thrombolysis at a secondary-level public hospital. The primary outcome was significant neurological improvement, defined as a ⩾4-point NIHSS reduction or NIHSS ⩽1 at discharge. Secondary outcomes included early improvement at 24 hours, functional independence (mRS 0–1), and safety (absence of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and in-hospital mortality). Multivariate logistic regression models were adjusted for age, initial NIHSS, diabetes, and hypertension.
Results: Among 71 patients (50 treated with alteplase, 21 with tenecteplase), there were no statistically significant differences in early improvement (50.0% vs. 38.1%, p=0.51) or overall functional improvement at discharge (64.0% vs. 52.4%, p=0.52).Functional independence (mRS 0–1) was more frequent in the tenecteplase group (38.1% vs. 22.0%), and the safety profile was favorable (100% vs. 86.0%, p=0.096), though neither difference reached statistical significance. Adjusted analyses confirmed the absence of significant associations between thrombolytic agent and outcomes.

Conclusions: Tenecteplase demonstrated similar safety and functional outcomes compared to alteplase in patients with AIS treated within the therapeutic window. These findings support the clinical equivalence of both agents in real-world hospital settings
EV690 / #989
BARRIERS TO THE USE OF INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYTIC FOR ACUTE STROKE IN A TELESTROKE SETTING
THROMBOLYSIS.C.Z. Reyes, S. Mittal
Thomas Jefferson University Hospital, Neurology, Philadelphia, United States of America
Background and Aims: Over the past two decades, telestroke has been shown to enhance access to care, improve quality of care, and lead to better outcomes for patients with acute stroke, particularly in resource-limited settings globally. With evolving telestroke practices, we aim to identify reasons for not administering intravenous thrombolytic to patients presenting with suspected acute ischemic stroke in a telestroke network.
Methods: This is a retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected data of patients who were evaluated from September 2024 to February 2025 within our telestroke network, which covers urban and rural sites across three states in the United States of America.
Results: A total of 2274 patients were seen, 176 (7.74%) of whom received thrombolytic therapy. Among the 2093 (92.04%) patients who did not receive thrombolytic treatment, the five most common reasons are: presenting outside of the 4.5-hour therapy window (46.11%), mild and nondisabling or rapidly improving symptoms regarded as NIHSS <1 (20.88%), direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) use within the past 24 hours or warfarin use with INR>1.7 (8.12%), patient/next of kin refusal (3.54%), and intracerebral hemorrhage (1.58%).
Conclusions: Presenting outside of therapy window and mild nondisabling deficits continue to be the top causes for not receiving thrombolytic therapy, consistent with published literature in telestroke and hospital settings. Unlike prior studies, anticoagulation use and patient/next of kin refusal were prevalent reasons in our network. These findings highlight the need to address these persistent reasons, such as raising stroke awareness in communities and the potential for DOAC reversal agents.
EV691 / #1445
THROMBOLYTIC TREATMENT IN PATIENTS WITH ISOLATED ACUTE ONSET CONTINUES DIZZINESS WITHOUT FOCAL NEUROLOGICAL DEFICITS
THROMBOLYSIS.C. Roelen1, M. Verhagen1, A. Ros1, K. Jellema2
1Haaglanden Medical Centre, Neurology, The Hague, Netherlands, 2Haaglanden Medisch Centrum, Neurology, The Hague, Netherlands
Background and Aims: The detection of ischemic stroke in patients with isolated acute onset continues dizziness (iAOCD) is challenging, making the decision to initiate thrombolytic treatment difficult. At present, there is insufficient data to provide a treatment recommendation. The aim of this study is to explore the rate of thrombolytic and endovascular treatment in iAOCD patients, and to compare outcomes in patients with and without acute treatment.
Methods: 810 patients with iAOCD were prospectively recruited from 11 participating hospitals in the Netherlands. The diagnosis for each patient was determined by an expert panel. The expert panel based its diagnosis on a standardized set of clinical information, diagnostic results, and three-month follow-up data. The prevalence of thrombolytic and endovascular treatment was quantified in this cohort. Outcomes (at three-months follow-up) will be compared using regression analysis.
Results: In total 14.8% of the patients were diagnosed with ischemic stroke by the expert panel*. A total of 45 patients (5.6%) were treated with thrombolytic treatment; none received endovascular treatment. Of these 45 patients, based on preliminary results, 47% was diagnosed with ischemic stroke by the expert panel*. No complications occurred in the thrombolytic treatment group. Following confirmation of the diagnoses by the expert panel, regression analyses will be performed.
Conclusions: Approximately half of the patients who received thrombolytic treatment were found to have had an ischemic stroke. In this cohort, thrombolytic treatment did not result in any complications, supporting its safety as a treatment option, in patients with ischemic stroke as well as patients with a stroke mimic.

ENDOVASCULAR THERAPY IN LARGE CORE STROKES, A REAL WORLD EXPERIENCE
THROMBOLYSIS.J. Rosales, J. Cirio, M. Lopez, D. Freire, M. Chasco, L. Caballero, N. Perez, E. Scrivano, C. Bleise, P. Lylyk, I. Lylyk, P. Lylyk
Clínica Sagrada Familia, Neurología, Buenos Aires, Argentina
Background and Aims: Background: The efficacy and safety of endovascular treatment (EVT) in large core strokes (LCS) have been recently demonstrated by six RCTs. However, data regarding the benefit of EVT in real-world settings is limited. To describe the experience of an Argentinian center in treating LCS outside the setting of clinical trials, focusing on safety and efficacy outcomes.
Methods: Retrospective review of consecutive patients with anterior circulation LCS who received EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset at our center during 2015-2025 with a minimum follow up of 90 days. LCS was defined as stroke with an ASPECTS score of 0–5 or ischemic core volume ⩾50 ml. Primary outcome was defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score ⩽3 and ⩽2 at 90 days. Safety outcomes were 90-day mortality and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) <48 hours.
Results: 150 patients fulfilled inclusion criteria, median age 72 years (IQR 58-80), 82 (55%) men. Median NIHSS at admission was 18 (IQR 14-22). Median time from symptom onset to groin puncture was 8.0 (IQR 4.7-10.4) hours, with 17% of patients within 12–24 hours and 78% achieving TICI 2b-3. Median infarct core volume was 80 (IQR 44-127), and median ASPECTS score 4 (IQR 3-5), with 22% patients scoring 0–2. At 90 days, 31% achieved mRS ⩽3, 21% mRS ⩽2, mortality was 45% and sICH rate was 23%.

Conclusions: This real-world study demonstrates that EVT for LCS within 24 hours of symptom onset are similar from clinical trials.

ASSESS THE NATIONAL STROKE TREATMENT PLAN ON MORTALITY OF PATIENTS WITH ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE; A REGISTER-BASED STUDY IN IRAN
THROMBOLYSIS.E. Sharifipour1, B. Zamani1, M. Farhoudi2, M. Mehrpour1
1Shahid-Beheshti University of Medical sciences, Neurology, Tehran, Iran, 2Tabriz University of Medical sciences, Neurology, Tehran, Iran
Background and Aims: The 724 plan (the first national project for acute stroke) was implemented in 2016 in Iran to better manage patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Herein, we aimed to evaluate the national stroke treatment project’s effectiveness, focusing on door-to-needle time (DNT) for reperfusion therapy.
Methods: This retrospective multi-center cohort study was conducted between January 2016 and January 2021. Participants included patients with AIS admitted to selected hospitals across the country. The following data were collected: baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes among three groups of patients: those with DNT less than 60 minutes, those with DNT greater than or equal to 60 minutes, and those who did not undergo thrombolysis.
Results: Of 26,399 patients with AIS, most were male (54.3%), with a mean age of 68.0 ± 14.7 years. 29.9% of patients received intravenous thrombolytic therapy (IVT), mainly given in the first hour of admission (73.38%). The proportion of patients receiving IVT was significantly higher among those who arrived via emergency medical service (EMS) than those transferred from other hospitals or admitted directly (p < 0.001). In both adjusted and unadjusted models, receiving IVT within the first hour significantly increased the odds of being discharged home (unadjusted OR:1.37, adjusted OR: 1.40).
Conclusions: The initial findings from our national register-based study indicate that holding such a national plan significantly improves the DNT for IVT among patients with AIS. Timely reperfusion therapy is critical and should remain a priority in stroke management strategies.
EV694 / #2272
MICROENVIRONMENTAL OXIDATIVE REDOX SIGNALING CASCADES AS THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR PREVENTING THROMBOLYSIS-MEDIATED HEMORRHAGIC TRANSFORMATION IN ISCHEMIC STROKE
THROMBOLYSIS.J. Shen
University of Hong Kong, School Of Chinese Medicine, State Key Laboratory Of Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, Hong Kong, Hong Kong PRC
Background and Aims: Using tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) for acute ischemic stroke is limited by adminstration within 4.5 hours and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) complication. Oxidative-redox signaling appears to a player in the thrombolysis-mediated ischemic brain injury but its roles and mechanisms remain unclear. Herein,we tested the hypothesis that microenvironmental oxidative-redox signaling plays crucial roles in thrombolysis-mediated HT pathology during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.
Methods: We performed in vivo, in vitro studies and clinical trials for the purposes. For in vivo study, male Sprague-Dawley rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) for 5 hours plus reperfusion using t-PA (10 mg/kg) with or without adjunctive inhibitors including FeTMPyP, taurine, 4-ABAH, etc. For in vitro study, neurons were co-cultured with endothelial cells or microglia that exposed to oxygen–glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). The BBB disruption, HT, brain oedemia, neurological deficit were assessed in vivo. Superoxide, nitric oxide, peroxynitrite, H2O2 and HOCl were examined by using related specific fluorescent probes, and MMP-9/MMP-2, MPO, NADPH oxidases were assessed in vivo and in vitro. Serum oxidative and redox biomarkers, infarct volume, neurological deficit scores were detected in acute ischemic stroke patients with or without t-PA infusion.
Results: (1) Peroxynitrite-mediated caveolin-1//HMGB1/MMPs signaling participates BBB disruption and HT pathology in delayed-thrombolytic brain damages. (2) Plasma 3-nitrotyrosine is an early HT biomarker in ischemic stroke. (2) Microglial MPO/HOCl/HMGB1 signaling amplifies ischemic brain injury. (3) Baicalin, Narigin and Glycyrrhizin could be drug candidates targeting those signaling events and attenuating thrombolytic brain damages.
Conclusions: Microenvironmental oxdiative-redox signaling could be therapeutic targets to reducing BBB damages and hemorrhagic transformation, improving outcome and extending thrombolytic therapeutic window in ischemic stroke treatment.
EV695 / #2445
BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER PERMEABILITY AND HAEMORRHAGIC TRANSFORMATION AFTER INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS: SUBGROUP ANALYSIS OF ATTEST2 TRIAL
THROMBOLYSIS.A. Mahmood1, L. Spencer1, M.J. Macleod2, I. Ford1, G. Ford3, N. Sprigg4, C. Price5, J. Wardlaw6, K. Muir1
1University of Glasgow, Glasgow, United Kingdom, 2The Institute of Medical Sciences, University Of Aberdeen, Aberdeen, United Kingdom, 3University of Oxford, Oxford, United Kingdom, 4University of Nottingham, Nottingham, United Kingdom, 5Newcastle University, Population Health Sciences Institute, Newcastle, United Kingdom, 6University of Edinburgh, Neuroradiology, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Haemorrhagic transformation (HT) after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) can worsen outcome. Blood brain barrier permeability (BBBP) imaging measures such as extraction fraction (E) predict haemorrhagic transformation. We investigated whether E was predictive of HT after IVT and whether this differed between tenecteplase (TNK) and alteplase (tPA) treatment.
Methods: Participants in the ATTEST-2 trial with technically adequate CTP and follow up CT scans were included. HT was determined by review of 22-36h follow up scans. Volumes of ischaemic core (relative cerebral blood flow <30%), ischaemic penumbra (Tmax>6seconds and rCBF>30%), and extraction fraction >30% (E30) were calculated using RAPID and MiStar software. The proportion of E30 within the ischaemic lesion (E30%) was calculated. Logistic regression was used to identify factors predictive of HT.
Results: 251 cases were included, 126 TNK and 125 tPA. 18/124 TNK and 14/125 tPA had HT (p=0.434). In 97 cases (49 TNK, 48 tPA) with a BBBP imaging lesion, median E30 volume was 10ml (4.5-21.5) for TNK and 14ml (5.25-28.5) for tPA (p=0.29); median E30% was 21% (11-37) for TNK and 19% (11-34.5) for tPA (p=0.59). Cases with a BBBP lesion had higher median NIHSS (16 v 6, p=<0.001), larger ischaemic core (13ml v 0ml, p=<0.001) and larger ischaemic penumbra (133ml vs 4ml, p=<0.001). In a logistic regression model including age, baseline systolic BP, baseline NIHSS, E30% and drug allocation; baseline NIHSS was the only factor predictive of HT.
Conclusions: Measures of BBBP such as E30% were not predictive of HT. E30% did not differentiate HT likelihood in TNK and tPA cases.

SHORT-TERM MORTALITY FOLLOWING INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS IN ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE: A RETROSPECTIVE INSTITUTIONAL COHORT STUDY
THROMBOLYSIS.V. Spinei1,2, A. Levca2, S. Băitoi2, T. Stupac2, A. Grumeza2, O. Grosu2
1Nicolae Testemitanu State University of Medicine and Pharmacy, Chișinău, Moldova, 2Diomid Gherman Institute of Neurology and Neurosurgery, Chișinău, Moldova
Background and Aims: Intravenous (IV) thrombolysis represent the therapeutic standard in early revascularization treatment of Acute Ischemic Stroke, significantly improving the outcome. Although its effectiveness is proven, a significant number of patients have some complications, including early death. The aim of study is to analyse the mortality rate during hospitalization in patients with acute stroke who underwent thrombolysis and the predictive factors associated with death.
Methods: This article is a retrospective study, included 126 patients who underwent IV thrombolysis between 2019-2024 in the Diomid Gherman Institute of Neurology and Neurosurgery. Clinical and radiological data were collected from electronic health records. There were analysed the rate of mortality and the predictive factors associated with death after trombolysis (commorbidities, complications and hemorrhagic transformation).
Results: The short-term mortality rate after IV thrombolysis was 23,80%. Predictive factors for an increased mortality rate are: 1) Comorbidities – 63,33% of patients had both hypertension and rhythm disorders (p<0,046). 2) The presence of a massive ischemic area (hemispheric) or hemorrhagic transformation was recorded in 46,66% of patients (p<0,001). 3) The occurrence of early complications, such as pulmonary thromboembolism and acute coronary syndrome, was registered in 36,66% (p <0,0003). This study confirms that associated risk factors, early complications, and hemorrhagic transformation are the strongest independent predictors of short-term mortality.
Conclusions: Short-term mortality after IV thrombolysis remains significant, despite the demonstrated therapeutic benefits. Early identification of risk factors may contribute to better patient selection and implementation of personalized monitoring and treatment strategies to reduce the risk of death.
EV697 / #2308
ARE WBC AND NEUTROPHIL LEVELS PREDICTORS OF FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE TREATED WITH INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS?
THROMBOLYSIS.J. Ivanovic1, S. Vukasovic2, S. Panic2, T. Svabic Medjedovic1,2, M. Kovacevic1,2, N. Kresojevic1,2, V. Padjen1,2, I. Berisavac1,2, M. Ercegovac1,2, D. Jovanovic1,2, P. Stanarčević1,2
1Neurology Clinic, University Clinical Center of Serbia, Belgrade, Serbia, 2Faculty of Medicine, University of Belgrade, Belgrade, Serbia
Background and Aims: White blood cell count (WBC) and neutrophils are inflammatory markers with a possible impact on functional outcome of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Our study aimed to establish their potential influence on the outcome of patients treated with intravenous thrombolysis (IVT).
Methods: We included 217 patients treated with IVT and analysed WBC and neutrophils at baseline and daily during hospitalization. The NIHSS and mRS were used as outcome parameters for efficacy, and frequency of haemorrhagic transformation (HT) and mortality as the safety outcomes. Logistic regression was performed to find potential predictors of outcomes, and ROC analysis for cut-off values. A p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
Results: The mean age at stroke onset was 62 (SD±14.4), with 83.1% of males. The mean door-to-needle time was 113.77 minutes (SD±46.38). Lower WBC 24h after IVT was associated with lower NIHSS at discharge (p=0.005), as well as mRS 0-1 after three months (p=0.001). Higher WBC at baseline was a predictor of sICH occurrence (p=0.039) and higher discharge NIHSS (p=0.005). Higher neutrophil levels at baseline and during hospitalization were associated with need for hemodynamic support (p=0.003, cut-off 13.35), intensive care treatment (p=0.029, cut-off 6.55), any HT (p=0.00, cut-off 6.85), and sICH (p=0.031, cut-off 11.4), without impact on mortality.
Conclusions: Higher neutrophil levels were associated with conventional predictors of worse functional outcomes, without significant impact on mortality and disability, contrary to higher baseline WBC associated with higher NIHSS at discharge.
EV698 / #1265
THROMBOLYSIS WITH TENECTEPLASE DURING THE SECOND TRIMESTER: A CASE REPORT DEMONSTRATING SAFETY AND FAVORABLE OUTCOME
THROMBOLYSIS.S. Helagalli Paramashivaiah, R. Then, M. Diaz Rojas
Jefferson Einstein Philadelphia Hospital, Neurology, Philadelphia, United States of America
Background and Aims: The use of Tenecteplase (TNK) for acute ischemic stroke in pregnancy is of increasing interest, though evidence remains limited. While intravenous thrombolysis with alteplase has been used in pregnancy, reports on TNK use in pregnancy are scarce. We aim to highlight safety of TNK in pregnancy.
Methods: Case report and literature review.
Results: A 32-year-old woman, 24 weeks pregnant, with preeclampsia and recent non-ST elevation myocardial infarction presented with acute left sided facial droop, dysarthria, weakness and numbness with a neurological institute of health stroke assessment (NIHSS) was 9. Initial computer tomography (CT) was unremarkable; CT angiogram showed no large vessel occlusion. She was within the window for thrombolysis administration. She received TNK after careful interdisciplinary discussion with maternal fetal medicine. Brain magnetic resonance showed acute infarction in the right posterior frontal lobe, operculum and insular cortex. Cardiac evaluation excluded obvious cardioembolic sources. Work-up was negative for infectious and autoimmune etiologies. Patient symptoms rapidly improved with a follow up NIHSS of 2, accounting for facial droop and mild dysarthria. No fetal complications were reported.
Conclusions: Stroke in pregnancy could result in devastating outcomes for both the mother and the unborn child. This case highlights safety of TNK use in pregnancy without deleterious maternal fetal consequences and with disability sparing benefits. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first case report of TNK use in the second trimester of pregnancy. Further research with larger patient samples is needed to establish safety and efficacy in pregnancy.

IMPACT OF TELERADIOLOGY ON THE DOOR-TO-NEEDLE THROMBOLYSIS TIMES
THROMBOLYSIS.S. Trinh, A. Sivagnanaratnam
Northwick Park Hospital, London, United Kingdom
Background and Aims: Over the past year, there have been 2 changes at Northwick Park Hospital (NPH) to the way CT scans are arranged and reported with the introduction of protocolised vetting and the use of teleradiology for reporting scans at night. This study aims to see how these changes have impacted the Door-To-Needle (DTN) times at NPH.
Methods: Changes were implemented in August 2024. Data of patients thrombolysed at NPH were selected between November 2024 to January 2025 and compared with the same months of the previous year. Times were grouped into day and night based on time of thrombolysis and further subdivided into Door-to-Scan times and Scan-to-Needle times. The Median times were calculated to find the average for comparison.
Results:

Conclusions: The target DTN time at NPH is 30 minutes and there is an improvement from 30% to 39.3% in achieving this target during the day which can be attributed to protocolised vetting with improved door-to-scan times. These improvements, however, are offset by delays at night where only 11.1% achieved the target (previously 31.3%). On reviewing documentation, reasons for delay involved issues with teleradiology. With a target DTN of 30 minutes, a median time of 31 minutes from scan-to-needle would suggest that using teleradiology to report thrombolysis scans is not suitable in hyper-acute management.

IMPACT OF IMPLEMENTATION OF CT PERFUSION ON FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES IN PATIENTS TREATED WITH INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS. A SINGLE-CENTER EXPERIENCE
THROMBOLYSIS.D. Vázquez Justes, G. Mauri-Capdevila, M. Paul Arias, Y. Gallego, E. Ruiz, E. San Pedro, A. Sancho, M. Vicente Pascual, F. Purroy
Hospital Universitari Arnau Vilanova, Lleida, Spain
Background and Aims: There is little evidence on which is the best imaging modality for the selection of patients eligible for intravenous thrombolysis (IVT). We aimed to analyze if there were differences in outcome in patients treated with IVT after implementation of CT perfusion (CTP) in our center.
Methods: We retrospectively analyzed data from patients admitted to our hospital with ischemic stroke who had been treated with IVT between 2018 and 2024. We compared patients selected for the treatment previously and after the implementation of CTP in our center in 2022. Primary outcome was the 90-day ordinal mRS shift analysis. We performed a logistic regression analysis adjusting for: NIHSS score, ASPECTS score, time to treatment and vessel occlusion (VO).
Results: 297 patients treated with IVT were analyzed. Of them, 215 (72.4%) had CTP and 82 (27.6%) had been treated without CTP. 100% received alteplase. Age, mRS prior to the event, and VO were similar between groups. NIHSS was lower in the group selected with CTP (p<0.001). Time from symptom onset was longer in the patients with CTP (125min [IQR:90-150] vs 160min [IQR:90-270], p=0.037). After adjustment for covariables, 90-day ordinal mRS shift was better in patients selected with CTP vs without [OR: 96.10 95% CI: 1.707-541.15], with lower risk of hemorrhagic transformation (9.7% vs 2.7%, p=0.050).
Conclusions: In our center, the implementation of CTP may have led to better functional outcomes at 3 months for patients treated with IVT, despite longer time to treatment. This may be related to improvements in the selection of patients.
EV701 / #1662
FUTILE REPERFUSION FOLLOWING THROMBOLYSIS FOR ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE AT 4.5 TO 24 HOURS
THROMBOLYSIS.L. Wang1, J. Yin1, Z. Cao1, Y. Zhang2, M. Hao1, N. Wu1, S. Wu1, S. Wu1, Z. Li1, K. Shen1, Y. Xiong3, Y. Wang4
1Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University, Department Of Neurology, Beijing, China, 2Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Beijing, China, 3China National Clinical Research Center for Neurologic Diseases, Beijing, China, 4Beijing Tiantan Hospital, Capital Medical University, Neurology, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: The futile reperfusion (FR) after successful recanalization following thrombolysis is never investigated. We aimed to evaluate the frequency and predictors of FR in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion after tenecteplase thrombolysis beyond 4.5 hours.
Methods: This was a secondary analysis of the Tenecteplase Reperfusion Therapy in Acute Ischemic Cerebrovascular Events–III (TRACE-III) trial. This phase 3, multicenter, prospective, open-label, randomized, blinded-outcome-assessment trial at 58 centers in China enrolled patients with large-vessel occlusion and salvageable brain tissue on perfusion imaging who were unable to access endovascular thrombectomy within 4.5 to 24 hours after they were last known to be well. Of these, patients who received tenecteplase treatment and achieved successful recanalization assessed with a follow-up arterial occlusive lesion (AOL) scale of 2 or 3 were analyzed. FR was defined as modified Rankin Scale score of 4–6 at 90 days despite successful recanalization.
Results: In a total of 103 eligible patients, we observed FR at 90 days in 33 (32%) patients after thrombolysis. Patients with FR were much older, more likely to be female, less likely to be totally independent (baseline mRS score of 0), had higher rates of diabetes mellitus and had a higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score. In multivariable regression model, the stroke severity assessed using the NIHSS score was independently associated with higher odds of FR (adjusted OR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06–1.30; P=0.003).
Conclusions: 32% patients had poor functional outcomes despite successful recanalization following thrombolysis, which was in alignment with the rate in patients receiving thrombectomy. The baseline stroke severity was strongly associated with the FR occurrence.
EV702 / #2442
BRIDGING INTRAVENOUS THROMBOLYSIS WITH TPA YIELDS HIGHER RECANALIZATION RATES THAN TNK IN TRANSFERRED PATIENTS WITH INTRACRANIAL LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSIONS
THROMBOLYSIS.R. Whelan1, S. Wasyliw2, R. Cooley2, U. Ahmed2, L. Peeling2, B. Newton2, N. Sylvain2, A. Gardner1, G. Hunter2, B. Graham2, M. Kelly2
1Saskatchewan Health Authority, Stroke Services, Saskatoon, Canada, 2University of Saskatchewan, Saskatoon, Canada
Background and Aims: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) with alteplase (tPA) or tenecteplase (TNK) is associated with early recanalization (ER) of large vessel occlusions (LVO) when used as a bridging therapy before mechanical thrombectomy (MT). In 2023, Saskatchewan’s stroke network—including nine primary stroke centers (PSCs) and one comprehensive stroke center (CSC)—transitioned to IV TNK.
Methods: This retrospective review assessed ER rates in 101 consecutive LVO patients treated with IVT (tPA or TNK) as a bridging therapy during transfer from PSC to CSC for intended MT. ER was defined by symptom improvement, LVO recanalization on follow-up vascular imaging, or distal migration of the occlusion.
Results: Among 101 patients, 51% received TNK and 49% tPA. The M1 vessel was the most common occlusion site (58.8% TNK vs. 42% tPA), followed by tandem occlusions (extracranial ICA + intracranial LVO) in 19.6% of TNK and 8% of tPA cases. Recanalization rates as a whole were higher in the tPA group (40% vs 37.3% for TNK), driven largely by LVO recanalization rates (26% tPA vs. 21.6% TNK). Symptom improvement occurred in 7.8% of TNK and 4% of tPA cases, while distal migration rates were comparable (7.8% TNK vs. 8% tPA). IVT dwell time was 32 minutes longer in the tPA group.
Conclusions: In patients transferred from PSCs with LVOs, bridging IVT with tPA was associated with a higher ER rate, potentially due to an extended thrombolytic dwell time. Increased incidence of tandem occlusions in the TNK group may have contributed to lower recanalization rates.
EV703 / #1641
CHINESE PATENT MEDICINES IN THE ERA OF REPERFUSION THERAPY FOR ACUTE ISCHEMIC STROKE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND NETWORK META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS
THROMBOLYSIS.X. Xiong1, X. Zheng1, T. Liu2, C. Que1, S. Cheng1, Y. Gao1,3, X. Lai1,3
1Dongzhimen Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, Beijing, China, 2The Affiliated Hospital of Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Jinan, China, 3Institute for Brain Disorders, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, Beijing, China
Background and Aims: Emerging evidence suggests that Chinese patent medicines (CPMs) might be implemented as an adjunct to reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke (AIS), to provide patients with better clinical outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of CPMs combined with reperfusion therapy in patients with AIS.
Methods: We systematically searched randomized controlled trials on CPMs for AIS patients with reperfusion therapy published in seven databases from inception to December 31, 2024. A frequentist framework-based network meta-analysis was performed using Stata 15.0 software. The study was registered with PROSPERO, CRD42022374804.
Results: 113 eligible trials involving 37 CPMs and 11,913 patients were included; all subsequent estimates refer to comparisons with reperfusion therapy alone. In achieving functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] ⩽ 2) at 90 days, CPMs combined with reperfusion therapy were more advantageous (odds ratio [OR] 1.96, 95% CI 1.54 to 2.49), in which Salvianolic Acid Injection combined with reperfusion therapy demonstrated the greatest efficacy (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.35 to 4.50, surface under the cumulative ranking curve [SUCRA] 80.1%). Maixuekang Capsules combined with reperfusion therapy showed the largest improvement in neurological deficits (mean difference [MD] -7.75, -10.66 to -4.84, 97.9%). Safety analysis indicated no statistical differences in intracranial hemorrhage incidence between CPMs combined with reperfusion therapy and reperfusion alone.
Conclusions: As an adjunct to reperfusion therapy, CPMs may improve functional outcomes and ameliorate neurological deficits in patients with AIS without increasing hemorrhagic risk. These findings require further validation through high-quality trials.

SINGLE CENTER REPORT ON 2 CASES OF CERVICAL EPIDURAL HEMATOMA PRESENTED AS STROKE MIMIC TREATED WITH RTPA
THROMBOLYSIS.P. Yee Hau1, Y.H. Koh1, M.J. Mamauag2
1National Neuroscience Institute, Neurology, Singapore, Singapore, 2Changi General Hospital, Neurology, Singapore, Singapore
Background and Aims: Stroke mimic tends to be safe receiving rTPA .Cervical epidural hemotoma is a commonly missed stroke mimic which rtPA may cause harm.
Methods: We report 2 stroke mimic cases who presented within treatment windows and received thrombolylsis in a primary stroke center.
Results: Case 1:A 34 year old man with no past medical history developed acute right hemiparesis while lying at home. It occured while his wife was massaging his neck. There was no reported trauma or neck pain. NIHSS on arrival, 1 hour from onset was 7,with right pure motor deficit. CT brain and CT angio were reported as ASPECTS 10 and no LVO. Patient was treated with rtPA. DTN was 53 minutes. Patient developed neck pain and acute urinary retention after arrival to stroke unit. MRI cervical spine showed extramedullary lesion over right C3-C4 dsiplacing the cord to left.Patien underwent immediate C3-6 Decompression and instrumented fusion. Patient made good recover post op. Case 2 : A 79 year old lady presented with fall with trivial head injury, subsequent developed neck pain, left hemiparesis and hemisensory loss.Cervical spine X ray was reported ostoephyte changes. NIHSS was 8 with left sensory motor deficit. CT brain and CTA reported as ASPECTS 10 and no LVO. Patient was treated with rTPA with DTN 60 minutes. Neck pain worsened and MRI C spine showed C4-5 intramedullary hematoma. Patient received immediate C4-C7 posterior decompression and fusion surgery.
Conclusions: A high vigilance considering cervical epidural hematoma is needed before offering rtPA.

LEUKOCYTES AS PREDICTORS OF HEMORRHAGIC INTRACRANIAL COMPLICATIONS IN PATIENTS TREATED WITH THROMBOLYSIS FOR MODERATE ISCHEMIC STROKE
THROMBOLYSIS.J. Zdravkovic, M. Jacovic, K. Nikolic, M. Milosevic, S. Mihajlovic, J. Stanarcevic
Special Hospital for Cerebrovascular Diseases "Sveti Sava", Neurology, Belgrade, Serbia
Background and Aims: Leukocytes constitute a pivotal element in the regulation of inflammatory mechanisms and the coordination of the immune response. This study aims to demonstrate the value of changes in leukocyte levels 24 hours after intravenous thrombolysis for predicting the prognosis of hemorrhagic cerebral complications.
Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 134 consecutive acute moderate ischemic stroke patients treated with intravenous thrombolysis at the Special Hospital for Cerebrovascular Disease “Sveti Sava” during April-December 2024. year. Blood Leukocytes were analyzed upon admition and at day one. Hemorrhagic complications diagnosed by neuroradiological diagnostics during the first 24 hours after applied thrombolysis were classified according to the Heidelberg bleeding classification.
Results: Out of the total of 134 patients who underwent intravenous thrombolysis, hemorrhagic complications were documented in 26 cases (19.40%). Among those who developed hemorrhagic complications, 15 patients (57.69%) presented with elevated leukocyte counts post-treatment with thrombolysis compared to their admission values. Logistic regression model showed increased odds of haemorrhagic complications in patients with elevated leukocyte counts, without reaching statistical significance level (Chi-square = 3.639, df = 1, p = 0.056, OR 2.318).
Conclusions: Although the result is not statistically significant at the p < 0.05 level, the p-value indicates a potential clinically relevant association that could be confirmed in studies with a larger number of subjects.

CLINICAL AND RADIOLOGICAL OUTCOMES OF THROMBOLYSIS IN THE GOLDEN HOUR
THROMBOLYSIS.E. Smolyansky1, C. Menezes2, A.A. Fouks3, J. Doherty4, J. Barker5, C. Mutimer5, C. Williams6, S. Thomas6, M. Valente5, A. Warwick7, K.S. Ho8, G. Sharma5, P. Guha5, B. Campbell5, G. Donnan5, S. Davis5, H. Zhao5
1Royal Melbourne Hospital, Parkville, Australia, 2University of Melbourne, Department Of Medicine, Royal Melbourne Hospital, Faculty Of Medicine, Dentistry And Health Sciences, Carlton, Australia, 3Austin Hospital, Department Of Neurology, Heidelberg, Australia, 4University of Melbourne, Melbourne Medical School, Faculty Of Medicine, Dentistry And Health Sciences, Carlton, Australia, 5Royal Melbourne Hospital and University of Melbourne, Melbourne Brain Centre, Department Of Neurology, Parkville, Australia, 6Royal Melbourne Hospital and Alfred Hospital, Department Of Neurology, Melbourne, Australia, 7Royal Melbourne Hospital and Austin Hospital, Department Of Neurology, Melbourne, Australia, 8Royal Melbourne Hospital, Emergency Department, Parkville, Australia
Background and Aims: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) is time-dependent, but data are very limited on treatment ⩽60min from onset (“Golden Hour”; GH). We aimed to investigate clinical and radiological outcomes for GH-treated patients, including exploratory analyses for early and later reperfusion, in a Mobile Stroke Unit (MSU) population.
Methods: We included pre-hospital IVT-treated patients with confirmed infarction on the Melbourne MSU between 12/2017-12/2024. GH(⩽60min) and non-GH(>60min) groups were compared for demographics and 90-day outcomes. In the subgroup with hospital-admission CT-perfusion imaging, we investigated: 1) baseline CTP parameters, 2) early reperfusion change on hospital-admission CTP(median 40min post-IVT) defined as ratio of subthreshold to penumbral hypoperfusion[(Tmax>4s-Tmax>6)/Tmax>4s], and 3) later reperfusion change defined as ⩾20% semi-structured visually-assessed change in baseline CTP-ischaemia to infarct-size >24h. Outcomes were analysed as binary logistic regression with adjustment for age, sex and pre-morbid Rankin.
Results: Of 274 MSU-patients included, 47(17%) received GH-treatment. GH and non-GH groups did not differ in age, sex, NIHSS, pre-morbid Rankin or thrombectomy rates but had significantly improved 90-day outcomes (Rankin 0-1/baseline aOR 2.60[95%CI 1.30-5.20]). In 200/274(73.0%) with CTP-imaging, GH-treated patients had numerically greater median penumbral(36.5[IQR0-111.8] vs 17.3[IQR0-72.2]mL) and core volumes (4[0-19.8] vs 0[IQR0-13.8]mL). Whilst there were no differences in substantial early reperfusion (22.6 vs 23.7%,p=0.42), GH-treated patients showed trend towards increased reperfusion at >24h (76.5 vs 59.8%,p=0.06).
Conclusions: GH-treated patients were observed to have larger baseline penumbra and core volumes yet had significantly improved outcomes, comparable to the effect of thrombectomy. Exploratory imaging analyses showed no evidence of improved early reperfusion for GH-treatment but trended towards improved reperfusion at >24h.
EV707 / #196
PER2 IN DEVELOPMENT AND RECOVERY OF INTRACEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE
BASIC SCIENCE.Suliman Khan, Rabeea Siddique, Qian Bai
The Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, Medical Research Center, Zhengzhou, China
Background and Aims: This study investigates PER2 and other clock genes in ICH progression and recovery using Clock-KO and Per2-KO models. Transcriptomic profiling reveals ICH alters circadian genes and inflammatory pathways, worsening outcomes. Additionally, we assess MIP2’s neuroprotective effects, targeting the PER2-TLR4 axis to integrate circadian regulation with immune modulation. Aims: Investigate PER2’s role in ICH pathogenesis and recovery. Evaluate MIP2’s efficacy in reducing neuroinflammation.
Methods: Wild-type and KO mice underwent ICH induction via collagenase VII. Sleep analysis, behavioral tests, MRI, and immunohistochemistry assessed recovery. RNA sequencing and Western blot analyzed circadian and inflammatory markers. MIP2 (10nM/g/day) treatment reduced neuroinflammation and improved recovery. Data were analyzed using ANOVA/t-tests, with p < 0.05 considered significant.
Results: ICH disrupted circadian rhythms, altering Clock, Per1, Per2, and inflammatory pathways, worsening neuroinflammation and functional deficits. Clock-KO and Per2-KO mice exhibited larger hematoma volumes, increased neuronal apoptosis, and delayed recovery compared to WT mice. MIP2 treatment significantly reduced microglial activation, neutrophil infiltration, and BBB disruption, improving neurological outcomes. Sleep analysis showed ICH decreased daytime sleep bouts and prolonged nighttime sleep duration, while wheel-running tests revealed circadian rhythm elongation (~27.5h in ICH mice). MRI and histological assessments confirmed MIP2’s neuroprotective effects, supporting the PER2-TLR4 axis as a novel target for circadian-based ICH therapy.
Conclusions: ER2 played a crucial role in regulating ICH progression and recovery by modulating neuroinflammatory responses and circadian rhythms, while MIP2 demonstrated a significant therapeutic effect by reducing microglial activation, neutrophil infiltration, and BBB disruption.
EV708 / #1503
EFFICACY OF MECHANICAL THROMBECTOMY IN MINOR STROKE: A META-ANALYSIS AND RESULTS FROM OUR OWN STUDY ON FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES, MORTALITY, AND INTRACRANIAL HEMORRHAGE
THROMBECTOMY.Jose M Ramírez-Moreno1, Pilar Blanco Ramirez1, Nuria García Guillén2, Maria Soledad Jimenez Arenas1, Andrea Parejo Olivera1, Marina Mesa Hernández1, Inmaculada Cordoba Bueno1, María Garcías Falcón1, Noelia Valverde Mata1, Pablo Macias Sedas1, David Ceberino1
1University Hospital of Badajoz, Stroke Center. Neurology Service, Badajoz, Spain, 2Extremadura University, Biomedical Sciences, Badajoz, Spain
Background and Aims: Mechanical thrombectomy has shown efficacy in moderate and severe strokes, but its effectiveness in minor stroke (NIHSS <5) remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of mechanical thrombectomy in minor stroke patients, integrating the results of a meta-analysis that includes our own study and other relevant studies.
Methods: A meta-analysis of observational studies on mechanical thrombectomy in minor stroke was conducted using a random effects model adjusted by the Hartung-Knapp method. Three main variables were assessed: functionality (Rankin at 90 days), 90-day mortality, and intracranial hemorrhage (ICH during admission). Heterogeneity was quantified using I2 and tau2.
Results: The meta-analysis included 9 studies on functionality (Rankin), 8 on mortality, and 8 on ICH. For the Rankin variable at 90 days, the overall OR was 0.9134 (95% CI: 0.6610–1.2622; p = 0.5365), with no significant differences. For mortality at 90 days, the OR was 1.8097 (95% CI: 0.7975–4.1063; p = 0.1307), suggesting a higher mortality risk in the treated group. Regarding ICH during admission, the overall OR was 2.8236 (95% CI: 1.5370–5.1873; p = 0.0050), indicating a significantly higher risk of intracranial hemorrhages. Heterogeneity was quantified with I2 of 29.3% (Rankin), 50.6% (mortality), and 0.0% (ICH), suggesting moderate heterogeneity in the mortality and functionality results, but low heterogeneity in ICH.
Conclusions: The results of the meta-analysis suggest that mechanical thrombectomy does not improve functional outcomes in minor stroke patients and is associated with an increased risk of mortality and intracranial hemorrhage, highlighting the need for future research to better define its risk-benefit profile.

EV709 / #1049
IMPACT OF A PROTOCOLIZED PATHWAY FOR POST-STROKE CARDIAC MONITORING: DIVERT PHASE II
IMPLEMENTATION & KNOWLEDGE TRANSLATION.David Rose1, Jana Braklow2, Krishna Pothineni2, Andrea Natale3, Frank Cuoco4, Darren Sidney4, Rawan Albadareen5, Bibhu Mohanty1, Marla Hairston1, Jessica Mikacevich6, Roberto Carta6, Noreli Franco6, Karah Neisen6, Dhanunjaya Lakireddy7
1University of South Florida College of Morsani Medicine, Tampa, United States of America, 2Research Medical Center, Kansas City, United States of America, 3St David’s Medical Center, Austin, United States of America, 4Trident Medical Center, Charleston, United States of America, 5Overland Park Regional Medical Center, Overland Park, United States of America, 6Medtronic, Minneapolis, United States of America, 7Kansas City Heart Rhythm Institute, Overland Park, United States of America
Background and Aims: Phase I of the DiVERT Stroke (SeconDary Stroke PreVEntion ThRough Pathway ManagemenT) study showed heterogeneity in cardiac monitoring strategies to detect occult atrial fibrillation (AF) in patients with small-vessel disease (SVD), large-vessel disease (LVD), and cryptogenic stroke across participating hospitals. This exposed the unmet need for a standardized, Guideline-Oriented Neuro-Cardio Pathway (GO-NCP). Therefore, DiVERT Stroke phase II implemented GO-NCP and collected clinical data to compare to phase I (pre-pathway).
Methods: DiVERT phase II implemented a prospective 3-step protocol (Figure) during in-patient hospitalization for SVD, LVD, and cryptogenic stroke (index event). Data was collected retrospectively and patients were followed for up to 180 days post-stroke. Consecutive patients receiving usual care (UC) (phase I) (2017-2019) were compared to patients following the GO-NCP in phase II (2023-2024).
Results: Patients participating in the two study phases were similar in age and sex (Table). The rate of cryptogenic stroke dropped from phase I to phase II (67.6% vs. 39.3%, p<0.001). Cardiology was consulted significantly more frequently (54.4% vs. 14.9%, p<0.001) and this resulted in significantly more cardiac monitoring (32.8% vs. 24.9%, p=0.002). Furthermore, GO-NCP resulted in significantly more oral anticoagulation prescribing (21.6% vs. 13.9%, p<0.001), and significantly less lost-to-follow-up (3% vs. 48.2%, p<0.001).
Conclusions: Implementation of a protocolized stroke care pathway significantly increased cardiology consultations during index hospitalization, the use of cardiac monitoring, and anticoagulation prescriptions. This underscores the value and utility of Neuro-Cardio collaboration for patients with SVD, LVD, and cryptogenic stroke.
